quoted_text:
if I had to make my first $1,000 online again in 2026, I wouldn't build a startup

fyi: in August alone, I paid $37k to affiliates and creators who market my products with their content

one of my users has even made over $75k just by setting up my $99/month product

so here are the 5 things I'd do instead: 

1. set up AI agents for boring local businesses

a dentist doesn't want "an AI agent". he wants his phone answered, his reminders sent and his reviews replied to

I run 8 agents across my own companies, and most local businesses still run zero

At Squad, we have partners getting paid $3k every time they set up Squad for a client 🤯 (dm me if you want to do this btw)

knowing 20 plumbers is what actually takes work

2. remake ads that already work, for businesses that can't make their own

search your client's competitors in Revid's Meta and TikTok ad viral search and save only the ads that have been running for 30+ days

nobody keeps paying for an ad that isn't working, so those are the proven winners

remix those ads with Revid for your client, and they get to skip months of testing

3. get paid per view, not per follower

on Clipatra, brands pay creators for every verified view. in the first 3 weeks of beta, creators posted 38 videos, got 500k views and earned $4,266, which works out to roughly $8.50 per 1,000 views

you don't need a big account for this, you just need one video that works

4. promote the tools you already pay for

most of that $37k I paid in August didn't go to professional marketers. it went to people who already used my products every day and just said so in public

if you're paying for a tool you love, you're probably sitting on an affiliate link you haven't claimed yet

5. start a blog on one boring niche and let it pay rent

pick a topic you’ve actually lived. it doesn’t need to be ambitious, it just needs to be something you understand better than almost everyone searching for it. 

it can be as simple as coffee. if you know coffee better than 99% of the world does, you can start a blog about it

once the blog hits DR 30+ and 100+ clicks a month for 3 months straight, you can plug it into Outrank

it finds the advertiser, writes a full article in your tone with one link inside and publishes it on your blog

you get $1 per DR point per article, paid straight to your bank through Stripe

so a DR 60 blog makes $60 an article. at 3 a day, that's up to $5,400 a month without you writing a single word

text:
The internet is going into a LOCKDOWN.

Hundreds of millions of websites are potentially at risk from cyberattacks.

Governments, banks and major platforms have already taken their websites OFFLINE.

Many are already calling it “Black October.”

At the centre of the shutdowns is something most of us have never heard of, but use every day.

PHP, the software behind roughly 7 in 10 websites, has two critical flaws that can let hackers break in without a password.

Dubbed PHP2Shell, both are rated 9.2 out of 10 for severity.

Details began circulating on Oct 20. Emergency fixes arrived the next day, but attackers were already moving.

Cloudflare’s CEO says hacking attempts then jumped from thousands to MILLIONS within hours.

Cybersecurity agencies across several countries are telling PHP site owners the same thing: Patch it now, or take it offline.

Websites have gone dark worldwide, from government portals and hospitals to banks.

CrowdStrike warns these attacks leave almost no trace, so some sites may not know if they’ve been hit.

Around 2.6 MILLION internet-facing servers run PHP, potentially hosting hundreds of sites each.

Over 1.1 million use older versions no longer receiving official PHP updates.

Older installations may need an upgrade to a supported PHP version or a fix from their software provider.

And patching does not remove a backdoor an attacker may already have planted.

Cloudflare also says hackers are now tweaking their attacks to try to slip past its protections.

But PHP isn’t the only security story unfolding.

-Japan’s Onamae suspended ALL Desktop Cloud plans after malware was found on customer servers.

-India’s eMudhra had 8 website-certificate keys so weak, one was literally the number “4”.

-State Bank of India confirmed 3,897 customer records on the dark web.

-Criminals used AI agents to break into 400+ Latin American banks.

-Capcom confirmed a breach exposing 11.7 million email addresses.

-GitLab disclosed a 10/10 severity flaw in versions going back to 2014.

-LiteLLM removed a malware-containing release. Railway reported possible exposure of customer secrets.

None of these has a confirmed link to PHP2Shell.

We’re seeing separate breaches unfold together.

The true number of incidents could take months to come out.

The world is still on alert. Attacks are still coming.

quoted_text:
We've decided to sunset Arc on December 22, 2026.

That's not an easy sentence to write. We spent years building Arc and celebrating each and every release along the way: we have so much pride and love for what we made alongside the Arc community.

Our priority is to deliver best-in-class security for our members. Keeping a browser secure takes constant, dedicated work that is only increasing in the age of AI. Dia was built from the ground up to meet today’s security standards, so that's where our engineering and security teams will focus moving forward.

We've worked to make switching to @diabrowser as easy as possible for Arc members. Here's how:

· Your passwords, bookmarks, extensions and history come over to Dia seamlessly.
· Spaces, Folders, and Tab Groups are in Dia and import over with your data intact.

text:
extremely impressed by grok @bot. random musings on it and some of the competition:

- native apps far superior to the imessage (e.g. instinct) form factor. imessage is easier to bootstrap for normies and simpler onboarding, but for any reasonable power usage, a dedicated native app is just better.
- multi-bot model (e.g. grokbot) is superior to single bot model (e.g. dots). its a tad more daunting, but creating specialist bots with their own identities/rules/routines is more fun, makes me feel incentivized to invest more in each, and is generally less overwhelming than having a dumpster ground of unrelated topics in one thread. the downside of this model is that i often forget which bot i was talking to about something and revert to my main bot as a router.
- other than multibot, some key things that make Grok Bot great: multi-device (ios, mac, tesla), super performant (so fast and responsive), exhaustive ecosystem integrations and mcp support. it just works every time.
- claude duet is def on to something with the 'tasks' tab. recognizing todos, structuring them, showing status in a familiar mental model like a todolist, and allowing one-click actions feels very natural and magical. excited to play with it. don't have access yet. 
- openai shipping dots as a section within the main chatgpt app was a mistake imo. it's out of sight and fighting the existing user behavior / muscle memory of how people use chatgpt (which is already conflicted and confused between codex/chatgpt work & chatgpt). dots should have been a separate app and should subsume the o.g. chatgpt use case. what can chatgpt do that dots can't? there should just be Dots and Codex as two separate apps (this is not a statement on what they should each be named). i can imagine the OAI team faced an extremely complicated set of trade-offs when weighing this, and i empathize, but imo there's a much better end state to be had. 

caveat that i haven't in earnest tried using muse yet, and I haven't been motivated to invest in porting other than occasionally feeling inspired by @alexandr_wang's shitposting.
author: poteto
quoted_text:
- tax prep: organizing tax docs, communicating with accountants and handling responses to their questions, doing my own research/analysis on prepared forms before finalizing returns. lifesaver.
- angel/fund mgr: overhauling how i organize my angel/fund investments, track the portfolio, consolidating agreements. grok bot instantly became an effective fund mgr/cfo. 
- shopping assistant: it's an addictive slipperly slope, but grok helps me find things i want (clothes, gadgets, various household maintenance and improvement things). the shopping flow is still a dice flow (even with Link setup)-- i occasionally have rejected/failed checkout flows and need to take over the vm. 
- property mgmr. i'm increasingly tagging it into dealing with home repair related things, coordinated with vendors, researching/validating proposals, shopping better quotes.
- work assistant: help manage the deluge of slack, email traffic, weed out the junk from my inboxes. 

what i want: 
- a better conduit to doing local execution/computer-use on a machine. being able to run grok bot on a mac mini on a home network would unlock a home of home automation use cases that i'm still relying on a local codex instance for (even with tailscale setup on my gb, this is more limited i've found). lmk if i'm missing a solution that exists here.
- a multiplayer experience w/ shared threads. would be useful for sharing some bots with a spouse. 

overall grok bot is extremely impressive and magical. kudos to the team.

国内 99.99999%的人没有见过 Monica 的形态（就是在对话的时候可以挑选多个不同的模型），虽然 workbuddy 里面有这个东西，但使用体验不佳，也没有广泛普及

等我把 dbskill 做成网站的时候，一定会允许用户关掉所有的 skill 提示词，这个网站就瞬间变成 Monica

所以这个产品的留存等同于 dbskill 的留存加上 monica 的留存

这个网站海外版的价值就不用说了，你将可以在这里使用 Claude 模型（如果你认为你可以轻易用上 Claude 模型，那你不是目标用户，你所代表的人数也可以忽略不计）

并且国内版依然有价值，我们将可以通过大量用户的数据来测评出 Kimi、DeepSeek、GLM 等模型在 dbskill 下面的表现

甚至对很多用户来说，他们现在想搭建本地知识库，需要同时装上 Agent，以及掌握对 /dbs-knowledge 这个 skill 使用的相关知识

我直接在客户端内置这个东西就好了，用户将在不知不觉之间用上知识库，第一次拥有上下文

text:
USDC年化冲到17%，Hyperliquid一夜吸金15亿美元？

10月21号，USDC借贷年化从3%冲到了17%。高利率很容易吸引注意，但继续往下查，会发现几组方向不同的数据

交易量在回升，原生借贷在扩张，一部分生态应用的资金规模却在收缩

Hyperliquid里的钱，似乎正在改变使用方式

链上数据显示，Hyperliquid L1近7天永续成交量约为565.15亿美元，环比增长25.52%；现货成交量约为14.70亿美元，增长6.39%

按UTC零点快照，10月16日，Hyperliquid L1上的USDC供应约为70.15亿美元；10月23日，约为69.44亿美元，一周减少约7129万美元，下降1.02%

一边是永续成交增长约四分之一，一边是USDC存量略有减少

我的理解是，交易活跃度先恢复了，资金规模还没有同步跟上，这也让“平台里放了多少钱”和“这些钱被使用得有多频繁”，成为两个需要分别观察的问题

同一笔保证金，可以反复参与交易；已有资产，也可以通过抵押借款释放购买力。成交量增长，除了等待外部资金进入，还可以来自资金使用方式的变化

那么，交易热起来，协议赚的钱有没有跟上？

再看Hyperliquid协议自身的账

把10月9日至15日，与10月16日至22日两个完整UTC周放在一起，综合费用从1935.54万美元增加到1939.49万美元，增长约0.2%；协议收入则从1544.20万美元降到1510.25万美元，下降约2.2%

这项综合统计包含储备收益，最新一天已经出现改善：10月22日，协议收入约278.15万美元，比21日增长约23.5%

但放到整周，收入仍然略有下降

所以，对HYPE持有人来说，接下来要看的，是这轮交易回暖能不能持续转化成收入

新增成交集中在哪些市场，交易者适用什么费率，收入怎样分配，都会影响最后留下多少钱

另一组更具体的变化，发生在原生借贷里

9月18日，Hyperliquid官方公布，底层借款规模约为2.69亿美元，到了10月23日上午，官方接口中的稳定币借款合计已经达到约4.29亿美元，一个多月增加约1.60亿美元，增长约59.5%

其中，USDC未偿借款约4.28亿美元，总供应约5.61亿美元，资金利用率约76%

这说明，借贷已经是一项有人实际使用、愿意付息的业务

借款的另一边，是抵押资产。当前原生借贷中的HYPE约为1441万枚。按采样价格计算，在HYPE与BTC这两类抵押品中，HYPE贡献的价值约占86%

对持有人来说，这提供了一种选择：保留HYPE，同时获得可以调动的USDC。HYPE由此多了一层资金用途。持有资产、抵押融资和参与交易，可以连接在同一个账户体系里

还有一个接下来可以盯的数字：5亿美元

这是官方文档列出的USDC全局借款上限。当前借款已经使用约85.5%，距离上限剩余约7238万美元。需求继续增长，额度是否调整，就会成为新的观察点

但把视线转回最近一周，生态里的其他业务，却没有一起扩张

10月16日至23日，HyperLend借款余额从约1.76亿美元降至1.64亿美元，减少约7.1%，我们前几天连续讨论的Papertrade，TVL则从10月20日的6192万美元，降到22日的4164万美元，两天减少约32.8%。这项余额包含交易者资金和协议LP

原生借贷在一个多月里扩大，部分应用最近却在收缩

这让我更关心生态内部的竞争：同样一笔USDC，用户会选择放在哪里？赚借贷利息，参与交易，还是继续投入亏损挖币？

Today we sent the following out to the CEOs in our portfolio regarding the widespread vulnerabilities that have been detected by AI agents:

The previous week should make it obvious that things have changed.  Vulnerabilities are being discovered and exploited at a rate that has never been seen before.  While there has been a flood of new vulnerabilities AI agents are being adopted at scale multiplying the potential risk.  Agents not only help automate the attacker lifecycle, every ai agent is an insider threat.  Your environments are designed to withstand attacks from the outside, not from within.  As such, we are suggesting company leaders consider the following changes:

1 - Ensure you're sufficiently staffed for security. The average enterprise allocates roughly 10% of its tech spend to security.  Consider doubling that.  There are likely thousands of vulnerabilities that need fixing in your environments.  Security through obscurity no longer works, all that can be exploited will be exploited.

2 - Establish a zero tolerance policy for secuirty bugs in new features and product releases.  Re-examine launch and release schedules and consider delays to ensure all vulnerabilities are patched before deploying new features or products.

3 - Double tap the zombies.   Find all old legacy environments that have been neglected and turn them off.  Labs, test environments, zombie CI/CD projects etc.  Turn it off for now.  If it isn’t tied to revenue, kill it.

4 - End the risk acceptance process.  Over the last 10 years the risk acceptance process has morphed from a way to accept risks to enable the business, to a way to justify never fixing security issues.  Adopt a zero tolerance policy for security issues and risks.

author: bc1qDave
quoted_text:
经历过一场漂亮的失败

前段时间，几块量化拼图终于凑齐。在交易所老板和朋友们的支持下，我拿到了更优惠的费率和订单执行条件。同时解决了硬件性能问题，训练基建也有了保障。老板也支持我们在股票合约方向做一些研究。于是我和伙伴 @Eric_pollll_btc  决定认真把系统搭起来。

想要做一个量化策略，是远远比大家想象中要复杂的许多。很多AI交易项目会给大家撮策略，其实那大多是非常不完善的一个基于 rule-based 的下单系统。 完完整整的量化交易系统，从如何保护 API 密钥安全开始，到用 Rust 写订单的执行代码。并接受反馈。 这里之间包含了一个大千世界

最开始的接入数据，整理数据，监督数据源有没有错误，（我们是真的在交易所上遇到过返回错误数据的情况）， 第一步数据搞完了，第二步才开始搭建模型。模型里的模型选择，调参，优化。 这一步相当艰难。对于成熟的量化团队来说，真正分高下的就是写模型的能力，是非常考验数学、物理、计算机，甚至金融知识的。 
模型做完，还有回测、实盘，再拿真实订单流里的问题回来修改，同时把风控、止损和异常处理补齐
每一步短短几个字，实则要花费大量的心血。光是回测这两个轻飘飘的字，里面的复杂程度都足以写论文了。（Eric最近就在做一个高频回测框架的项目，后面会开源）

所以做一个量化不是大家印象中用Python写几段代码，给 AI 说一个策略思路就可以完成的，这是一个非常复杂的工程， 我和我的伙伴决定用很严肃的态度对待这个任务，所以要以很严谨的工程思维来对待系统搭建。

到这里就是结束了吗？除了代码之外，还有一片看不见的领域，（其实也是我在任务中主要做的事情）

作为小团队，更不要说个人了。在激烈的交易所环境下面对专业机构，劣势不只在模型。手续费、成交速度、交易条件，每一项都可能吃掉本来就不多的优势。所以，和交易所沟通、争取支持，并不是技术之外的杂事，而是系统能不能成立的一部分。 

同样重要的，是找到值得做的市场和标的。资源有限，就不能只想着正面拼算力、拼速度，还需要一点交易员的直觉，找到能发挥优势的机会。当然还有不断地和同行进行沟通， 队内进行任务安排和分工， 对外寻求支持（如融资、交易活动等等）

需要相当多的努力，技术上的，业务上的，组织管理上的，才能把这一件小事情做好

讲到这里，我希望给大家留下一个量化的专业印象，AI 发达后，路边摊量化确实有点泛滥了。想要做好一件事，要以最认真的态度去对待它。同时大家应该也理解我过去一个月在推特上沉默寡言的原因了。

接下来廢话不多说，看一篇我的技术写的文章吧。我在 review 了我们三周的成果之后，让他写了一篇总结， 因为无论成败，做一个事情还是需要有闭环，有交付。我个人觉得他写得很好， 一两周前就叫他赶快发推特了，但是他实在是太忙，就由我来帮他发一下这篇文章吧。同时也希望我账号流量大一点，可以让更多人看到我们的项目：

【预测未来】
Article by @Eric_pollll_btc @bc1qDave @AndyW_Web3

“
策略为什么会盈利
这段时间我们一直在研究高频策略，用AS模型也好，GLFT模型也好，都没能取得比较稳健的收益。随后我尝试拓展高频策略的行为，比如不再连续报价，而是挑选市场状态报价，比如不在固定的双边maker，而是将动作拓展到单侧maker，亦或者是taker一些订单。叠加的规则越来越多，可调节的参数越来越多，策略的复杂度不断提高，而复杂度本身并不能带来收益。于是我开始反思，我们的策略里究竟缺少了什么？或者说，不局限于高频策略，一个真正能盈利的策略，必须需要什么？

我发现，我们优化止盈/退出逻辑也好，改善仓位控制也罢。本质上都是在“根据自己的状态做决策”，而非“根据市场状态做决策”，更确切的说，是没有专注于“根据未来做决策”。

这样一来，无论如何我们都是在被市场牵着鼻子走。那么什么是“根据未来做决策”？很简单，你认为未来价格会涨，所以买入，这就是根据未来做决策。你的盈利，全部来源于你能够对市场的走势作出正确的判断。为什么很多人看上去都是先从中低频的主观交易赚到钱，而不是一开始就通过高频交易获利呢？因为决策频率低。当交易的次数越来越多，越来越频繁，就越是会暴露出我们对未来的真实预测能力到底有多强。

所谓预测未来的能力，就是alpha。

而仓位控制本身不产生alpha，它只是一个让我们控制风险的工具，它的目的只有一个，就是让我们在市场上活下来，不被一次失误决策干死，仅此而已。因此，在没有找出真正的alpha之前就大量设计仓位控制的行为，是毫无意义的，它只会让策略从暴死变成慢性死亡。

一切风险控制、仓位控制之类的设计，都应当在发掘出了真正有效的alpha后进行。

描述市场的维度不止价格

很多决策的本质都是预测未来，比如我之前给dave说的，大单冲击后买一卖一大幅移动，希望在较高位置做空，恢复后做多，实现盈利。这个策略是规定了一个入场条件，预测入场条件触发后，有可能形成一个有盈利空间的事件。本质上来说，和金叉买入没什么区别，都是在预测未来存在一个有盈利机会的事件，仅此而已。

预测不止是预测涨跌这样的盈利性事件，还可以是其他的市场信息，比如波动率，比如成交活动，比如买卖价差等等。
这些市场信息对策略的构建是非常重要且有价值的，比如当我们预测到成交活动后面一段时间会很弱，那我们便停止被动做市，逐步将仓位平掉；比如当我们预测到市场的波动率会显著扩大，那么便可以适当减小杠杆，亦或者根据策略的类型选择避开这段时间还是积极参与进去。

这样的风险控制或者仓位控制，是真正带着对市场判断的仓位控制，才是合理的控制，而这一切都是基于有效的预测。

那么具体如何预测未来，就是一个很深刻的话题了。我做了这样的研究

我希望回答一个问题，行情里究竟有哪些信息，对未来有帮助？只看当前够不够？不同市场能不能用同一种描述？我每隔五秒整理一次当时已经收到的盘口和成交信息，然后观察未来五秒、三十秒、一百二十秒等时段里，五件事怎样变化：

1：价格变化。最后涨了还是跌了，变化多少。
2：路径波动。中间经历了多大起伏。最后回到原价，也可能经历了很大波动。
3：成交活动。接下来会发生多少笔成交。
4：买卖价差。最优买价与卖价之间的距离会扩大还是缩小。
5：盘口深度。可见挂单会变厚还是变薄。

这个就是我描述未来市场的五个维度。即便我们很难判断接下来市场到底会涨还是跌，但也可能比较容易判断接下来会不会更加活跃。

历史信息中有多少对未来有价值的东西

假如两个时刻，当前价格、买卖价差、盘口厚度，甚至最近五秒的成交情况都很接近。但其中一个时刻，过去两分钟一直很平静；另一个时刻，过去两分钟刚经历了一连串剧烈变化。

只看眼前他妈是很像的，但接下来的30秒，他们的表现是否也应该一样呢？

我们让两种模型预测完全相同的一批未来，一种只看当前最近一格的行情信息，另一种还可以看过去三十秒、两分钟的历史。结果就是加入历史后，30秒的五目标总和误差下降了大约14.01%。如果再补上10分钟前的历史，预测误差还能进一步下降2.38%。

但进一步拆开看，历史主要帮助判断的是波动、成交活动和部分流动性变化。价格变化的改善弱得多。不过后来单独针对价格目标选择参数，也找到了一点预测改善，所以不能说价格完全不可预测也。

接着我还需要判断这些历史与未来关系，能否在不同标的之间通用。因为这些标的的短期关系很可能是不一样的。同样是“最近成交变得密集”，它对不同市场未来波动、价差和深度的含义，可能旧不太一样。

因此我比较了几种做法，分贝是所有市场共用模型、按大类区分、和进一步让每个市场拥有自己的模型。

结果表明共用和继续让每个市场有自己的模型，并不能改善预测。所以说类别差异是有价值的，但过细的拆分则没有什么价值，这也在意料之中。然后我还尝试将行情信息压缩，用PCA，保留数据里变化最大的那些方向。结果是强行压到很少的维度预测很容易变差，还是高纬度预测效果比较好。还有就是把市场硬切分成两三种区域再分别预测也没有稳定赢过连续的模型。

还有一点是更高频的预测，比如毫秒级别的，在流动性差或者成交不活跃的市场里，是很难产生有意义的结果的。这里不是说不准，反而是有时候能预测的非常准，尤其是方向。
但比如你深入到订单簿一看，中价十分显著的负自相关性居然是因为卖一规律的下跳而买一不动所导致的，这样是没法盈利的。非正常交易时段的这种现象的时间尺度会放大到分钟级别。如图所示：（见下图）

所以，我现在更关注两件事：我们究竟预测到了什么，以及这个预测能否转化为真实可交易的机会。策略变复杂，不代表优势变强；预测误差变小，也不代表利润就会出现
”

最后补充几句。上面的这个复盘只是针对我们的做市策略中的一个模型的分享，我们还尝试过根据订单流的交易策略，以及根据 CoinGlass 因子的机器学习截面多空策略，Hyperliquid 与币安的资金费率套利策略，和一大堆数不清的。Eric和我还写了几篇“著作”，包括《为什么 AS 和 GLFT 是扯淡》、《用价格预测价格》等等文章，都欢迎大家讨论分享！今天实属冰山一角，欢迎同行和老板们 DM 我。如果在港深的话，有机会我请大家喝咖啡，互相学习学习

最后感谢 @bitget @xiejiayinBitget  和 @QFEX @ChloeTalk1  老板们的支持，接下来会和 @trasiaxyz 有个实盘合作，谢谢 @mablejiang 大佬赞助量化上 hype 跑跑，大家敬请期待接下来的更新吧

Look at Amazon... revenue up 53% since 2021 on the same number of people. Thats productivity. 

Hyperscaler headcount has been basically flat for three years while earnings have gone exponential.

I wrote about exactly this a month ago in GMI. The issue is called The New Macro, and in it I address the bubble question

The issue lays out what that means for growth, demographics, liquidity and markets, where the real risks are, and the five numbers that would make me change my mind.

If you're trying to make sense of the noise this week, that's the one to read.

Now, GMI is normally only for hedge funds, family offices and serious investors. Its not public.

text:
Jeff 听取用户反馈，准备在下一次网络升级中，给 HIP-3 交易者更多下单、撤单的空间📣

这次公告中的调整可以这样理解：

🟠 在 Hyperliquid 上，用户能进行多少次下单、撤单等链上操作，与实际成交量挂钩。成交越多，就能积累更多可用的操作次数。

🟠 过去，HIP-3 成交量能增加多少操作额度，要按手续费中“归协议的部分”折算。升级后，会把“归市场运营方的部分”也算进去，改按总手续费折算。

🟠 对大多数 HIP-3 合约来说，同样的成交量，今后能积累的操作额度将达到原来的 2 倍。对于需要频繁挂单、撤单、更新报价的交易者，这个变化会更实用。

Jeff 还特别强调：这次更新对用户有利，现有程序和使用方式可以继续沿用；用于决定手续费等级的成交量，仍按原来的规则计算。

也就是说，大家会获得更多可用的操作次数，手续费等级的计算规则保持不变。
author: 0xMaxs
quoted_text:
姐夫@chameleon_jeff 中秋食堂又给大家伙加餐啦🥮

Hyperliquid 连发两条升级预告：资金费率上限砍掉87.5%，HIP-4部署额度翻倍👇

1/2 给极端资金费率加一道护栏

永续合约资金费率上限，将从每小时4%降至0.5%，降幅87.5%。

假设你持有1万美元名义价值的仓位，且处于支付资金费的一方，在触及上限的情况下，每小时支出将从400美元降至50美元。

当然，Jeff也强调，实际交易中极少触及原来的上限，日常费率依然随市场变化。

我的理解：这项调整主要降低极端行情下，资金费持续侵蚀保证金的风险。

2/2 HIP-4给开发者多一倍部署能力

每个部署者的两项额度同步翻倍：

• 同时活跃的outcomes：100个提高至200个；
• 每日可部署的outcomes：500个提高至1000个。

HIP-4是Hyperliquid的结果合约基础设施，可用于预测市场和具有期权特征的有限收益产品。

这里有个细节：额度按outcome计算，一个包含多个结果选项的问题，可能占用多个名额；已经结算的outcome会释放活跃额度，因此，200个outcomes不能直接理解为200个独立预测事件。

翻了一下此前官方公告，团队曾提到，技术稳定后希望逐步提升至每个部署者1000个活跃outcomes、每日5000次部署。本次先提高到200/1000，仍在分阶段放开容量。

text:
Kimchi Token’s Market Cap Plunges Over 98% to $277K After Pumpfun Co-Founder Removes Repost

Crypto trader Kimchi posted a promotional image this morning with a QR code linking to a new memecoin, Project Kimchi. After Pumpfun co-founder Alon reposted it, the token’s market cap briefly reached approximately $15M. Alon subsequently removed his repost, while Kimchi deleted the original post and removed “pumpfun” from his bio. The token’s price then fell sharply.

Alon had previously described Kimchi as the first trader to truly bridge crypto and pop culture. Neither has publicly explained the deleted post or removed repost. According to GMGN, the token’s market cap is now approximately $277K, down over 98% from its peak, with around $9.3M in 24-hour trading volume.

author: pdhsu
quoted_text:
Delighted to share a landmark preprint from our lab, using genome language models and AI agents for biological discovery and genome mining!

The stretches of DNA between protein-coding genes are often called the genome’s “dark matter,” but they are far from empty. They encode RNA molecules that sense metabolites, regulate genes, and control some of molecular biology's most important tools (such as programmable genome editors e.g. CRISPR/bridge)

Much of this biology is unexplored. One reason is that RNAs can retain similar structures and functions even as their DNA sequences change dramatically, making their relationships difficult to recognize with conventional computational tools

text:
a16z 把加密基金改名了。
@a16z 
a16z crypto 正式改成「a16z Frontier」，Marc Andreessen、Ben Horowitz、Chris Dixon 三位一起上節目談這件事，我整理了 7 個重點：
@pmarca  @cdixon 
1️⃣ 最大的機會是認知差。 大多數人還把 AI 當聊天框，前線的建造者已經讓上百個 AI 代理一起寫程式。Dixon 說，這是電腦史上早期使用者和大眾之間最大的落差。

2️⃣ 「太早」不再是最大的風險，不夠大膽才是。 AI 把開發時間從幾年壓到幾天。只領先六個月的產品，還沒上線就會被巨頭和開源社群淹沒。

3️⃣ AI 的紅利不一定被巨頭吃光。 Ben 認為巨頭有創新者的兩難。當年電信公司握有所有網路，最後贏的卻是 Netscape、Amazon、Google。

4️⃣ AI 代理經濟需要加密。 未來網路上活動的主體，人類可能變成少數。銀行不會發卡給一段程式碼，AI 代理需要自己的錢包、私鑰和微支付。

5️⃣ 開源 AI 是反壟斷的底牌。 他們反駁 Peter Thiel 那句「加密是去中心化，AI 是中心化」，主張開源模型加上密碼學，才能防止巨頭和監管聯手壟斷。

6️⃣ 網路的舊契約已經破了。 以前創作者貢獻內容，平台還你流量；現在 AI 爬走內容、直接給出答案，連一次點擊都不還。Dixon 主張用鏈上確權，讓每次資料被調用都能追溯源頭並分潤。

7️⃣ iPhone 之後的下一個裝置是智慧眼鏡。 能看到你所見、聽到你所聞的隨身 AI，會終結手機近二十年的統治。

如果你今天 18 歲，三位合夥人會給你什麼建議？
🔹 Marc Andreessen：別學會被自動化的技能。 照固定規章處理文件的事務性工作，你還沒畢業就可能被 AI 取代。回到第一性原理，去鑽研基礎數學、物理、電腦底層系統和化學材料，因為物理定律永遠不會騙人。同時要拚命學會最前沿的 AI 工具。一個精通生成工具和程式代理的年輕人，一個人就抵得上過去 20 人的工程部門。去做出真的東西、上線真的產品，程式碼和用戶的回饋勝過任何名校文憑。
🔹 Ben Horowitz：技術會變，品格和意志不會。 商業世界最稀缺的，永遠是真正的領導力和擔當。去最危險的邊緣探索，學會面對失敗，學會把一群志同道合的怪才組織起來，學會在別人嗤之以鼻的時候堅持自己的直覺。未來的財富，屬於捲起袖子、在工廠和程式碼裡流汗的建造者。
🔹 Chris Dixon：保持極客精神，懷疑被過度包裝的共識。 去加入正在開荒的新大陸，哪怕它今天看起來又笨又粗糙。二十年前是開源軟體，十年前是區塊鏈，今天是硬科技和 AI 代理的世界。

一句話總結：少考證照，多動手做；學最底層的硬知識，再用 AI 把自己放大 100 倍。
我的看法： 連最懂加密的 a16z 都不再只押加密，代表下一個風口在 AI 和加密的交會處，像 AI 代理支付、資料確權、開源算力。只做純幣圈敘事的項目，會越來越難拿到頂級資金。

text:
I tried to work out why a CoreWeave bond yields around 15% when compute demand is this strong.

TLDR: it's the price of having no hedge.

A neocloud with long contracts from the most creditworthy companies in the world can borrow fine. The cost of capital jumps when you sell on-demand compute, or sell to smaller, less creditworthy buyers, because nobody can lock in what that capacity will earn.

Even CoreWeave, with 98% of its revenue on committed long-term contracts, pays about 15% to borrow, because that revenue sits with a handful of customers and nobody can lock in what those GPUs earn once the contracts end.

GPU futures should fix that, and it isn't a new idea. Farmers sell next year's corn forward so a price crash at harvest can't wreck them. Compute would work the same way. Buy the GPUs, deploy them, sell a strip of futures against the fleet, then sell on-demand or six-month contracts to smaller customers who put a big share of the contract value up front. Lenders are then lending against a hedged position, not a guess, and that should mean a much lower cost of capital. The behaviour already exists. Compute just doesn't have the market yet.

The harder-to-finance customers aren't a niche. In my view, the open-source model hosts and startups that rent GPUs to sell tokens are already a big enough market to need this.

Give it a few years and hedging a GPU fleet probably becomes as normal as a farmer selling next year's corn forward.

简单科普一下，这里的人类基因组是就是人体内几乎完整的一套DNA遗传信息，包含大约30亿个DNA字母对

而全基因组测序就是通过机器把一个人的整套DNA信息尽可能完整地读取出来

木头姐押注AI医疗的逻辑就是，未来测序成本大幅下降，医院能够给更多患者做检测，就可能产生更多数据，更多数据反过来可以继续推动医疗成本的下降，产生更多的现实世界数据

测序越来越便宜 → 产生更多生物数据 → AI模型分析能力提升 → 诊断和药物研发效率提高 → 产生更多真实世界数据

text:
2023 年，Spark Capital 给 Anthropic 投了 7500 万美元。三年后的今天，它持有的 Anthropic 股权已经价值 70 亿美元。

彭博社今天盘点了 Anthropic 的股东名单，这可能是硅谷历史上最夸张的一次财富创造事件之一。

几个数字感受一下：

Spark Capital 2023 年押注 7500 万美元，如今持股价值约 70 亿美元，还是目前唯一已知在 Anthropic 董事会拥有董事席位的 VC。

Menlo Ventures 2023 年开始投资，当时 Anthropic 几乎没什么收入，还是 OpenAI 的追赶者。累计投入超过 10 亿美元，如今持股价值约 140 亿美元。

Iconiq 2025 年才入场，当时 Anthropic 估值已经高达 1830 亿美元。累计投资超过 60 亿美元，如今持股价值约 170 亿美元。如果 IPO 估值达到 2 万亿美元，这部分资产还可能再翻一倍。

Sequoia 今年年初才开始投资，砸了 30 亿美元拿下约 1% 股份。按照最新私人市场估值，这部分股权已经价值近 100 亿美元。

GIC 新加坡主权财富基金累计投入超过 45 亿美元，同样持有约 1% 股份。

还有一些很有意思的名字。

Ashton Kutcher 参与创办的 Sound Ventures，2023 年曾以 50 亿美元估值投资 Anthropic 3500 万美元，随后又持续加仓，累计追加 4 亿美元，如今也是数十亿美元级别的持仓。

Google 前 CEO Eric Schmidt 持有约 1% 股份。而 Anthropic 最早期的投资人名单里，甚至还有 FTX 创始人 SBF。

按照彭博社的说法，这次 IPO 将让 Anthropic 的七位亿万富翁联合创始人更加富有，也可能让数以千计的员工成为百万富翁。

我觉得特别有意思的一点是，现在市场还在讨论 AI 泡沫，Anthropic 已经准备让过去几年押注它的投资人获得史无前例的账面回报。

而且 Google、Amazon、Nvidia 这些巨头的身份更复杂。它们既是 Anthropic 的重要供应商，也是持有大量股权的投资人。一边向模型公司提供芯片和算力，一边享受模型公司估值上涨带来的收益。

整个 AI 产业的资金循环，在这张股东名单里体现得特别清楚。

当然，账面财富还需要经过上市和后续减持才能真正兑现。Anthropic 正计划在未来几周推进 IPO，市场最高甚至有人喊出 2 万亿美元估值。

如果真能以这个价格上市，硅谷 VC 过去几十年形成的回报纪录，恐怕要被重新改写了。

最让我感慨的是，Iconiq 在 Anthropic 估值已经达到 1830 亿美元时才上车，结果依然可能赚到几十亿美元。

text:
以后遇到史诗级安全漏洞，可能连「赶紧打补丁」这句话都没用了。

Sam Altman 发出警告，AI 很快可能发现连顶级人类黑客都找不到的漏洞，甚至包括那些根本无法通过软件更新修复的硬件缺陷。

这事儿已经有一些前兆了。

就在 10 月 21 日，OpenAI 披露了 PHP 的两项严重安全漏洞。PHP 支撑着全球约 70% 的网站，这些漏洞此前已经进入人类安全研究人员的视野，但 AI 帮助研究人员找到了实际利用路径。OpenAI 联合 Wiz、Cloudflare 等机构花了两个月协调修复，英国、日本、芬兰的部分政府网站还一度紧急下线。

这次至少还能通过软件升级解决。

但 Altman 担心的下一阶段更麻烦。假如 AI 开始系统性地挖掘 CPU、芯片架构等硬件层面的缺陷，有些问题可能无法彻底通过软件修复，只能隔离受影响设备、禁用部分功能，甚至直接更换硬件。

想想就很恐怖。全球有多少银行系统、数据中心、工业设备，还在使用十几年前设计的芯片？

AI 可能彻底改变网络攻防双方的成本结构。

以前发现一个复杂漏洞，需要顶尖安全专家花费大量时间研究。以后攻击者可能部署成百上千个 Agent，24 小时扫描和分析，自动寻找突破口。

可防守方还得走完漏洞验证、补丁开发、兼容性测试、部署更新这一整套流程。涉及硬件，周期可能更长。

模型能力几个月就能发生巨大变化，全球计算基础设施的更新周期却往往长达数年。

AI 可能一个晚上就能发现的问题，人类可能花几年都修不完。

而且还有一个挺讽刺的地方：当所有人都开始依赖 AI 来抵御 AI 攻击时，谁拥有最强大的模型、最多的算力，谁就可能掌握相当一部分数字世界的安全主动权。

text:
AI 创业现在最夸张的一件事，是创业者和传统企业的管理层，可能已经生活在两个完全不同的世界里了。

Marc Andreessen 最近在 a16z 的节目里讲了一段挺有意思的话。

他说，AI 原生创业公司和传统企业之间，对 AI 能力的认知差距，是他整个职业生涯见过最大的，而且这个差距还在不断扩大。

AI 的能力几乎每周都在进步。传统企业还在琢磨怎么用 AI 提高现有业务的效率，新一代创业者已经开始考虑，能不能直接把整个行业的生意重新做一遍。

他甚至回忆起 1994 年创办 Netscape 的时候，感叹如果当年自己和 Ben Horowitz 手里有今天这些 AI 工具，他们究竟能做出多少东西。

我觉得他最值得琢磨的其实是最后一个判断：

未来的创业者，可能根本不会把自己定义为软件公司、硬件公司，甚至 AI 公司。

过去二十年的科技创业，大家已经习惯了某种分工。做软件的卖软件，做硬件的卖硬件，做 SaaS 的帮传统企业提高效率。创业者通常要先想清楚自己属于哪个行业，再考虑怎么切入市场。

但 AI 正在让这些边界变得越来越模糊。

一个十几人的团队，以前可能只能给某个行业开发一套管理软件。现在他们可以尝试直接承接这个行业里的某项业务，把销售、交付、客服和运营都放进自己的系统里。软件成了他们内部的生产工具，对外卖的是完整的服务。

当然，a16z 作为 VC，天然希望相信创业公司的机会越来越大。传统企业的资金、客户关系、牌照和线下履约能力，也不会因为模型升级就自动消失。

但我觉得 Andreessen 有一点说得很对。

AI 时代最可怕的竞争对手，可能是一个对行业原有规则毫无敬畏之心的创业者。

你还在计算 AI 能为公司节省多少人力成本，人家已经在计算，你这家公司到底还有多少存在的必要。

而且随着模型能力继续提升，这种认知差距可能比技术差距更难追赶。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
Marc Andreessen says the gap between what AI-native startups and incumbents think AI can do is the widest he’s ever seen:

"The AI-native early stage startups have just a completely different view on what they can do with AI than the typical incumbents in almost any industry, almost without exception."

"AI is just racing ahead in capability even week by week... There are going to be a lot of industries that are really up for grabs in a fundamentally more profound way than maybe has been the case in the past."

"The founders are gonna have a level of superpowers coming from the use of these tools and these technologies that they just simply haven't had in the past... Had I had Astra and Netscape in 1994, like, oh my God. Like, Ben, what would you and I have been able to do at Netscape?"

"Those entrepreneurs are gonna color way outside the lines. We already see this. They're not gonna think of themselves as like, 'I'm just a software company,' or, 'I'm just a hardware company,' or even, 'I'm just an AI company.'"

@pmarca @bhorowitz

10月19日，TRON Inc. 宣布当选 TRON 网络 27 个超级代表之一，截至10月18日，其节点排名第27，获得约7.6亿枚 TRX 委托。

这次当选，也让 TRON Inc. 和 TRON 生态的关系更近了一步

过去说起 TRON Inc.，大家第一反应可能是持有大量 TRX 的上市公司。现在成为超级代表后，公司将通过全资子公司参与区块生产、交易验证、网络安全和链上治理，同时获得相应的节点奖励。

说得直白一点，TRX 不只是放在账面上，还能拿来参与网络运行，并探索持续的链上收入，这不比单纯持币更有想象空间吗？

持有 TRX，主要受益于资产本身的长期表现；运营超级代表节点，则增加了一条相对清晰的收入路径，也让 TRON Inc. 能更直接地参与网络事务

TRON Inc. 首席执行官 Rich Miller 表示，这一里程碑代表公司在创造持续链上收入方面迈出了重要一步，同时也会为 TRON 网络的持续增长和韧性作出贡献

再看看 TRON 现在的体量，就更能理解这次当选的分量。

根据公告，截至2026年7月31日，TRON 网络拥有超过3.96亿个用户钱包，累计交易量接近150亿笔，链上承载约900亿美元的 TRC-20 USDT，接近全球 USDT 总供应量的一半。

公告援引 Allium 的行业报告称，约90%的稳定币支付交易量在 TRON 上结算。用户、资金和交易都是真实存在的，尤其在稳定币支付这块，TRON 的成绩确实很能打。

从持有 TRX，到参与节点运营，再到探索持续的链上收入，TRON Inc. 这次不是简单多了一个头衔，而是数字资产策略真正向前迈了一步

TRON 有用户、有交易量，也有稳定币结算需求，现在又有上市公司进一步参与其中，生态的想象空间自然更大

感受是：AI Agent 交易这个叙事吹了很久，这次可能真开始落地了。

现在用起来，还带点“AI半手搓交易”的意思：你提需求，它帮你研究、梳理，再由你确认执行。

Your hand determines the game:
· Moves 1–3: Build defensible positions and assess Level I edges.
· Moves 4–6: Seek captures and protect upgrade opportunities.
· Moves 7–9: Assess rock placement and multi-capture chances.
· Final turns: Decide whether to end the game or continue until you can secure a win.
Rocks can convert weak cards into strategically valuable plays.
Any card, regardless of its level, may be sacrificed and placed face down as a rock. A weak Level IV or V card may be more useful as an uncapturable rock than as an upgrade that is unlikely to be played. However, avoid sacrificing your only Level V card too early; you may later capture a Level IV stack and forfeit a valuable upgrade opportunity.
The ninth slot is the most significant position in the game. Once it is filled, the game ends, and no further upgrades, captures, or responses are permitted.

text:
Kevin Weil on why he left OpenAI to build autonomous labs: the next leap in AI needs experimental data the models don’t have.

“The models are data poor in the physical sciences.”

In mathematics, you can push forward inside a computer. In chemistry and biology, you need experiments.

“The way to solve this problem is to generate data at scale.”

“Basically what we’ve done in manufacturing we’re beginning to do as a country with biotech and pharma, except it’s not too late.”

“We can bring it back, but what will it take to bring it back? We need automation and robotics.”

@kevinweil on Lightspeed’s The Investment Memo
author: rsarver
quoted_text:
While AI has advanced in mathematics, we believe there’s still a major gap in the physical sciences.

@warpsciences co-founders @kevinweil and Solomon Reisberg joined Lightspeed Partner @guruchahal to discuss how their labs could generate the experimental data needed to advance scientific AI.

The company recently emerged from stealth and is building US chemistry labs to make research compounds for biotech and pharma companies.

“First be the hands, then build the nervous system, and then over time become the brain,” says Warp’s CEO Kevin.

The plan starts with expert chemists making molecules for customers. Cameras and sensors would record the work, helping Warp automate tasks and train models to improve how compounds are made.

More capable labs could let researchers pursue ideas for new medicines that time and cost currently put out of reach. The experiments could also produce more evidence for scientific AI to learn from.

Thank you to Kevin and Solomon for joining us!

Any form of security through obscurity is fully over. This barely worked as a method with humans, but just simply is over in a world of autonomous systems that will look through every crevice and try every permutation of attack possible.

As a result, years and years of legacy enterprise infrastructure will need to be upgraded, security practices modernized, data pipelines cleaned up, access controls better managed, and much more. Agents will help on the defensive side because they can both accelerate this work and equally simulate the risk vectors.

But there’s a long road ahead to prepare for this future. This is also partially why diffusion timelines will take longer than some realize.

text:
EXPLAINED: How Bonsai 2 9B got ~6x faster in a week [VIDEO]

Kydo has the final numbers. Here’s how it actually worked.

@PrismML gave Day 0 access to Bonsai 2 9B, an open-weight ternary model.

@YukonResearch froze a reference engine for it, MLX on Mac / Apple Silicon (https://t.co/uFpHiT9o9m) and llama.cpp on DGX Spark (https://t.co/tuLkHUh7Qx). The weights stayed locked. Everything that runs the model was open to edit.

Humans and their agents submitted changes with the Yukon CLI. Every run was verified against the reference on Apple M5 Max or DGX Spark and had to produce the exact same tokens. Faster but wrong fails.

Beat the record and your code becomes everyone’s new base. That happened 158 times.

The speedups came from speculative decoding, a DFlash 2 drafter shrunk to 4-bit, draft trees, int8 prefill and kernel fusion. Decode went from 144.8 to 959.6 tok/s on Apple Silicon, a real step forward for Local AI on hardware people already own.

Credit to @arthurostapenko, kaankolcu, spariev, dadon and everyone who submitted. 

Thanks to @HessianFree, @SahinLale and @BabakHassibi for doing this in the open. 

Try Bonsai 2 9B on @DarkbloomAI today btw
author: pratikg
quoted_text:
🏁 FINAL RESULTS: Bonsai 2 9B now runs 471% faster on Macs and 421.5% faster on NVIDIA DGX Spark.

Open frontier research and open-weight models win again. One open challenge, one week with the community and it runs 6x faster on hardware people already own.

It is crazy to see that the decode speed went from 144.8 to 959.6 tokens/sec on Apple Silicon and from 85.9 to 576.7 on DGX Spark.

This model can also run on an iPhone. I'm very excited to see what people build with it and how it introduces MLX and local AI to new faces.

Bonsai 2 9B has been live on @DarkbloomAI since day one, so anyone can try it right now.

158 new records built on top of each other from humans and agents running Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon, DeepSeek-V4 and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. Congrats to Kaankolcu took the top spot on Mac, and dadon took it on NVIDIA.

text:
I’m starting a new early-stage AI fund, doing what I love: partnering with founders from company formation on bold bets, long before consensus.

The fund’s LPs will include Sequoia, Jeff Dean, Sachin Katti, Philip Wong (my Stanford professor and Chief Scientist adviser to TSMC), and others whose work has shaped our industry and how I think about AI’s future.

I’ll remain a partner at Sequoia and keep serving on my boards on Sequoia’s behalf.

Sequoia has been my home for the past 11 years. I joined as the youngest investor the firm had ever hired. I grew up here. Through years of intense debate and shared work, I found lifelong mentors and friends who took me under their wing and taught me this craft. They taught me to aim high and take big swings. I’ll carry that into what I build: outsized ambition, relentless truth-seeking and curiosity, and a refusal to become complacent.

Working alongside founders has made me want to build something of my own: a firm shaped from day one around the convictions I’ve developed over the past decade.

Life has taught me not to take time for granted. This is how I want to spend mine.

Why now

We’re seeing a new way of building companies in today’s AI era. Research and products often advance together. A breakthrough can open a market or accelerate a business far faster than expected. Some companies require extraordinary capital and compute early on. Others reach meaningful scale with remarkably small teams. The rules for how big these businesses can get, and how fast, are being rewritten.

But early on, the technology is unproven, the resources required enormous, and the vision seemingly implausible.

This is what I love most: seeing the potential right from the beginning, and helping founders realize their full scale of ambition.

More than ever, it starts with an extreme willingness to believe early, with bold, independent conviction in a founder’s technical insight before any product or market validation. Then, it means helping founders take the biggest swings, giving the rare, long-term patience to see those bets through uncertainty, ambiguity, and turbulence, and serving as a level head when the stakes are highest.

I learned this kind of partnership at Sequoia. It’s the foundation of the firm I’m building.

Believing before consensus

My fascination with AI’s potential took root at Stanford in the early-to-mid 2010s, studying computer science and working in Andrew Ng’s lab. The friendships I formed connected me to a community whose people and ideas would help shape modern AI and build some of our generation’s defining companies. What stayed with me was the gap between what those people saw was possible and what the wider world could imagine.

I’m drawn to founders pursuing ambitions that sound impossible today.

I start with a simple question: “What if everything goes right?”

Then we work backward together to make it happen.

In 2023, Deepak and Abhinav set out to build a general-purpose robot brain at @SkildAI, before physical AI was a consensus bet. Their sim-to-real breakthroughs gave me conviction where earlier robotics approaches had fallen short. But the data flywheel required deployment at scale. We made commercialization as urgent as research and brought in strategic partners like NVIDIA and SoftBank to support the ambition. Three years in, Skild is advancing the frontier of physical AI with nine figures in annualized revenue.

In 2024, Ioannis and Misha founded @reflection_ai with an insight into scaling reinforcement learning. As that grew into the ambition to build a Western frontier lab for open models, the hard question was how a startup competes with labs spending tens of billions. An introduction to NVIDIA and many compute calls and recruiting events later, the team has built Beam, now one of the leading US open models.

In 2025, Anna and Azalia, the co-creators of AlphaChip, founded @RicursiveAI to design models and hardware together. From day one, we made early customers and ecosystem partners a priority. Today, they are showing order-of-magnitude improvements on real workloads, working with some of the industry’s most consequential players, and reaching a defining inflection point.

The ambition keeps growing as these companies scale.

@linear has always had a kind of magic to it. Now it’s the system a new generation of AI companies builds on, for teams and agents alike.

@tavus saw early that we’d one day talk to AI the way we talk to each other. Today, it’s building the human computing interface for a world of AI colleagues.

@Mach_Industries began as hydrogen experiments in an MIT dorm room. It has since become one of the most exciting next-generation defense companies.

Making the ambition possible

Being a first believer is only the beginning. Compute falls through. A deep-pocketed incumbent makes your mission its top priority. A breakthrough changes the opportunity and the capital required overnight.

These are stomach-churning moments, and early belief carries a responsibility to help make the bet work.

This is the partnership I love: turning the full ambition into concrete steps. Raising capital, securing compute and strategic partners, recruiting exceptional people, and winning the first customers together. Thinking several moves ahead while solving what’s in front of us. And as breakthroughs open new possibilities, helping founders dream even bigger.

Thank you

To the founders I’ve worked with: thank you for trusting me and Sequoia to be your first partner and first believer. It’s been the joy of a lifetime, and I can’t wait to keep building together.

Thank you to Alfred and Pat for your leadership of Sequoia and your support of my next chapter. To Roelof, for bringing me into Sequoia and believing in me from the beginning. Alfred and Roelof, you have been mentors in investing and in life. So much of what I know, and the investor I’ve become, comes from your guidance and generosity over the years. To Bill, for the close partnership and wealth of knowledge, always wrapped in humility. To Shaun, for showing me how to think deeply and imaginatively. To Michael Moritz, for inspiring 22-year-old me to dream big. To Doug, for teaching me to keep things simple. To Bogie and Jess, for bringing joy to the everyday and perspective on what matters. And to all my Sequoia teammates, for the friendship, camaraderie, and lessons I’ll carry with me.

To my family, especially my husband and my brother, who have each started companies of their own: thank you for giving me the courage to take this leap.

Let’s get to work!

quoted_text:
笑了，监管撤回了一个做空科技的文章。

央行主管的《中国金融》 盘中发了一篇标题为《科技股估值“纠偏”刻不容缓》的评论文章，没一会儿就又火速删除。

不管这篇文章是央行有意或无意的，但文章说得没问题，

在科技攻坚战的背景下，现在几大金融部委，除了金融稳定外，最重要的工作就是“科技金融”，所谓“五篇大文章”，科技金融才是最大、最核心的一篇。

因此很大部分的金融工作，都是围绕“如何再金融稳定的前提下做好科技金融？”而展开。
进而可以得出三个基本结论：

1、高层比过去更重视资本市场，因为可以给科技和产业输血（利于科技攻坚），而不再是“金融羞耻论”、“搞不好就关掉”这种嫌弃态度；

2、相比其他板块的泡沫，监管更能容忍甚至乐见适度的科技泡沫，毕竟历来科技都在泡沫中催生，有利于科技攻坚。

3、但不能容忍极端的科技泡沫。
一是，和“金融稳定”要求相冲突；
二是，这篇文章说的“扭曲科创激励机制”，不利于科技攻坚。

这也是证监会想要的“慢牛”，
然而“慢牛”不是想想要就有的，经常是要么疯牛、要么死给你看，这个度如何把握？
很难，只有边做边看、看能不能慢慢调教。

于是证监会今年初首次提出了“逆周期”调节、防止“大起大落”的监管思路...

text:
Big personal news today: I have decided to leave @a16z, move to SF, and start a company.

It's time to build :)

It has been almost 10 years since I joined the firm. I met @cdixon, @bhorowitz, and @pmarca  in 2017. At the time, I was an engineer at Google Brain working on robotics. I had a deep interest in open source. I knew nothing about investing. Chris meanwhile had already planted the @a16z flag at the frontier that was early crypto with investments in companies like Coinbase. But the crypto team at the firm consisted of only him, and he had the ambition to expand. His pitch to me was simple: "You should leave Google and come help me build the crypto vertical at the firm."

The work we've done together since then to build out our team and support our founders has been the most meaningful work of my life. I am grateful to have spent a decade working with everyone here, supporting our founders, learning from Chris, Ben, and Marc, and living the firm's culture. It is a culture that values integrity, life-long working relationships, and the belief that we humans have the power to build our own future.

Marc and Ben have built a16z into an incredible force for good in the world.

Before I joined the firm, I always thought that my inevitable path was to become a founder. The truth is that I wasn't ready for it then. Somehow, this year I've gotten the overwhelming feeling that this has changed.

As for what I want to build: It is early, but I care most about building infrastructure that enables open software ecosystems. I am starting with two core observations:

1. AI today is largely a single-player technology. Most uses involve one human talking with one agent in isolation from the rest of the world. That will soon change. Most uses of AI will soon be many-to-many: many humans and many agents working together. There will be at least one massive open network on top of which those uses will be built.

2. Software is now free. It can now be written just-in-time, on the spot for a single individual's hyper-targeted use case, and it can even be thrown out after a single use. This means that our entire software stack will have to change. In the limit, it will lead to a whole new kind of AI-mediated operating systems, which in turn will create an ecosystem of AI-native developers who build applications that actively rebuild themselves on the fly.

If you are working on related ideas, and especially if you are in the Bay Area, hit me up. Let's chat!

@bhorowitz , @pmarca, @cdixon, @eddylazzarin, @guywuolletjr, @jasonrosenthal , and our whole team — I want to thank you. Working with you has been the time of a lifetime. I am forever an a16z superfan and your ally.

Onward 🫡

text:
“We want to skip, summarize, and cut to the chase.”

@naval said that about how we read now. It’s also exactly how most people trade.

Everyone wants to make money trading. Almost nobody wants to read the basics.

I’ve spent my time trading in the stock market, and now I’ve carried it over to crypto. The pattern never changes. People chase hooks, short clips, and signals, and then the market teaches them the fundamentals the expensive way.

So I built something about it.

Proof of Learning is a free course on trading and crypto fundamentals. 16 modules, covering how markets work, technical analysis, fundamental analysis, on-chain analysis, derivatives, DeFi, risk, psychology, and postmortems of the biggest blowups. Updated through October 2026.

It doesn’t read like a textbook. Three friends, Mint, Hash, and Node, talk it through. One is new, one has traded for years, and one is the skeptic who keeps asking “but why?” You learn the way you would over coffee with someone who’s been burned before.

Everything in here comes from what I’ve lived through. The move from stocks to crypto and the nuances nobody warns you about. Riding the cycles up and getting caught on the way down. The trades I missed, the wins I got lucky on, and the lessons that only came after losing money. My AI agents helped me organize years of that into something structured and readable, but the learnings are mine, earned trade by trade.

So here’s my one ask: don’t hand this to your agent. Read it yourself.

It’s your money. You make the call. And you can’t make a good call on something you never understood.

@WarrenBuffett put it simply: “Risk comes from not knowing what you’re doing.” Research starts with reading. This is the reading part.

What it’s not: no shilling, no exchange, no wallet, no token, not even a favorite blockchain. Just the material, kept neutral so anyone can come back to it.

This isn’t a finished product. It’s a course we build together. If something doesn’t land, tell me. Comments are coming to the site soon.

Next up, I’ll be posting a series on fundamental vs technical analysis, and how stock markets and crypto markets actually differ.

Start here 👇

从这一刻起，所有已经创建出来的处理器项目，以及所有用户手里的晶体管、电路，任何人都无法修改，这些现在是真正永久属于你的链上资产了。

Intel CTO explains why Intel is helping Elon Musk build Terafab, and what a new fab needs besides tools

DWARKESH: “I think it’ll be interesting to discuss the partnership you guys have with Elon on Terafab. What’s going on there?”

PUSHKAR RANADE (CTO): “Well, I think Elon’s publicly talked about his desire to build a fab.”

[Musk clip spliced in]: “We either build the Terafab or we don’t have the chips. And we need the chips, so we’re going to build the Terafab.”

RANADE: “Sort of the same thinking. I think he’s seeing just an enormous increase in demand for silicon, for compute and for memory. And I think he came to the conclusion that his own businesses are going to require a lot of silicon. And so he thought maybe he should just do it all on his own. Unlike building a car, for example, this is such an intricate and complicated process. We thought we could work together to help accelerate his bringing up his fab.”

DWARKESH: “But because of the bottleneck at the tool level, it seems like the net amount of silicon in the world won’t increase. It’s just that maybe if somebody were to start a new fab, they would get access to guaranteed supply in a way that they wouldn’t have if they’re working with another person’s foundry.”

RANADE: “It’s actually not just tools. I mean, a fab does require a lot of power, a lot of water, a lot of consumables. There’s many other input variables as well.”

DWARKESH: “But those can be scaled in the way that tools cannot.”

RANADE: “Yea. Some more than others, but yes. In one sense, yes, we need a lot more equipment. But it is true, we also need a lot more just raw fab space, raw clean room capacity.”

text:
Only 600 to 4,500 confidential GPUs can be rented anywhere in the world right now.

That's ~0.04% of the NVIDIA chips that support confidential computing. All the confidential AI compute you can actually buy adds up to roughly 2% of xAI's Colossus.

The numbers come from Arcium's survey of ~80 providers, in @FourPillarsFP's new Blackthorn deep dive. And they're the part of the thesis I undersold in my post below.

Why so few?

Today's stack needs an Intel or AMD enclave on the host to vouch for the GPU. CoreWeave, Lambda, Crusoe and Nebius all run the right NVIDIA chips, but none of them offer that host setup, so they can't sell confidential AI at all. Among hyperscalers, only Azure and Google Cloud sell it, one GPU per VM.

Blackthorn drops the host enclave. For those bare-metal Hopper and Blackwell fleets, going confidential becomes a software install instead of new hardware.

Second thing: the weak link I flagged runs deeper than "the Intel chip got broken".

NVIDIA's attestation only proves the GPU is genuine. Nothing ties it to the enclave checking it. Break the enclave, forge its side, pair it with a real report borrowed from someone else's GPU, and every check passes while your prompt runs in plaintext.

And that gap is real in production: @PhalaNetwork's own February security update said CPU-to-GPU binding wasn't enforced at the platform level.

Blackthorn closes it by having the GPU sign the live key exchange itself. A borrowed report carries the wrong exchange values and gets rejected on the spot.

On speed, the whitepaper estimates (still no public benchmark tho):

- ~7% overhead from NVIDIA's confidential mode, the MPC layer adds next to nothing on top
- 30 to 60 tokens/s on a 70B model, single stream on an H100
- 50 to 200 ms to open a session

Btw: Arcium's MPC protocol is built so one honest node is enough. But per Four Pillars, v1 runs it in honest-majority mode for speed, so for now most of the nodes have to be honest.

Third (and last) thing: per Four Pillars, Blackthorn's first production partner is Charité Berlin, already running it on data from 20,000+ heart and lung transplant patients, with a multi-hospital product as phase 2. Not announced by Arcium or Charité yet tho, so pending.

$ARX still at ~$45M mcap. Thesis remains unchanged.

NFA though ofc. DYOR.
author: zerokn0wledge_
quoted_text:
Venice is a $1.3B bet that people will pay for private AI.

What many don't talk about: its privacy still runs through an Intel chip, and that chip got broken twice in the last 12 months.

@Arcium just shipped the version without that chip, at $49M mcap.

Why does the chip matter?

Venice's encrypted mode runs the model on NVIDIA GPUs with an Intel TDX enclave in front of them (per its own docs), which makes TDX the weak link. TEE(.)fail pulled attestation keys straight off the DDR5 bus in October 2025, and DDRop forged TDX attestation with a $159 interposer in September 2026. The NVIDIA side of things survived both, bc GPU memory sits inside the package where you can't clip a board onto it.

Blackthorn is basically the same stack with the Intel part cut out, shipped as infra: an API, rented GPUs, or self-install on your own Hopper/Blackwell boxes. It's not a consumer-facing chat app in itself.

On a more technical level: The model runs in plaintext inside confidential GPU memory, the session keys that unlock it get split across MPC nodes, and MPC never touches the per-token path. Arcium says near-native speed, no public benchmark yet tho.

So what's it priced at?

- $ARX: $49M mcap, $234M FDV
- $VVV: $1.3B mcap, $2.2B FDV

27x on mcap, 9x on FDV, for the stack with one less party to trust.

Which imo btw also means the obvious move for Arcium is sitting right there: a Venice-style front end on Arcium's own API once the infra is proven.

Without that app layer, Venice isn't the cleanest comp yet tho. The more congruent ones are the TEE infra Venice actually runs on: @NEARProtocol's NEAR AI Cloud and @PhalaNetwork, both announced as Venice's confidential inference providers on the 19th of March 2026, both TEE-based, which is where the Intel TDX enclave from above lives. Also: NEAR is listed for completeness only tho, a $7B L1 where private AI is a rounding error isn’t a comp. Phala is.

- $PHA: $50M mcap, $59M FDV
- $NEAR: $7B, with private AI a rounding error inside an L1

So infra vs pure infra, $ARX already trades at a 4x FDV premium to Phala. A sign that the market doesn't price Blackthorn like cheap TEE infra. It's already starting to price it as a shot at the app layer.

Which brings us back to Venice.

The valuation gap there exists for a reason today. Blackthorn is still a gated alpha with no fees. Venice is a real product with users and revenue.

But that's the whole point of buying the alpha instead of the product: you get the better trust model before the market prices it in. If Blackthorn (and a Venice-style product, in-house or not, built on it) attracts real users, this gap will close. And that's my bet.

NFA ofc. DYOR.

text:
1/
HBM 底层 DRAM 技术路线分化。

三星、SK 海力士、长鑫推进4F²。

美光跳过4F²，继续优化6F²，未来直接转向3D DRAM。

三星和海力士也在研发 3D，分歧在于是否经过 4F² 这一代。

2/
HBM 升级有两条主线，

一，底层DRAM提高存储密度

二，堆叠与互连提高容量、带宽和能效。这场路线之争主要集中在前者。

4F² 用更复杂的制造工艺，换取更高存储密度。

理论单元面积减少33%，位密度提高50%。

代价是垂直晶体管制造复杂，电容间距限制实际密度收益，良率存在挑战。

美光用成熟 6F² 争取时间，直接押注3D DRAM。风险是 3D DRAM 商业化更远，如果 4F² 率先实现低成本量产，美光可能暂时失去成本优势。

3/
背景是，美光技术与产品总裁 Scott DeBoer 在电话会上指出，公司已经研究 4F² 技术约20年，并做过多个原型。

最终决定放弃，主要涉及两个问题。

第一个，是制造复杂度与成本。

第二是，美光认为，决定 DRAM 实际存储密度的重要因素是电容间距。

电容不能无限缩小，否则读取信号和数据保持能力都会受到影响。

4F² 理论上的33%面积缩减，很难直接转化为同等幅度的整颗芯片面积下降，更难直接转化为制造成本下降。

4/
长鑫有个特殊条件，融资能力相对充足。 IPO 净募资663亿元，9月又宣布350亿研发与测试投资计划，主要使用超募资金。

对长鑫而言，持续研发 4F² 有机会换取技术突破和市场份额，其战略价值可能高于短期财务回报。

5/
至少从 27—28年的盈利兑现看，我更支持美光的路线。

美光预计2027年下半年推出的 1δ 工艺，在保留 6F² 架构的同时，仍能获得约25%的位密度提升。

同时，已经有 HBM4 商业化收入，可以继续投入良率和封装改善。

美光无需承担 4F² 额外风险，就有机会继续降低成本。

4F² 很难立即改变 HBM 市场供需格局。

text:
有人离场避险，有人开始逆势抄底。

Hyperliquid 上，47 个大户近期在美股相关 HIP-3 合约新增或加仓多头，单标的新增敞口均超过 50 万美元。截至发稿，35 个账户仍持有约 3902 万美元多仓。

资金主要押注 META、SPCX、SNDK 和 NVDA。其中 META 多仓约 1052 万美元，SPCX 约 781 万美元，两者合计占留存多头敞口近 47%。当然，也有 12 个账户已经清仓或转为空仓，抄底并非全线看多。

与此同时，市场上的看涨逻辑也在逐渐汇集：

- Coinbase Institutional： 芯片股连续调整，比特币却相对抗跌，BTC 正在摆脱「科技股杠杆代理」的定位。

- Doctor Profit： 认为 8.1 万至 8.2 万美元构成强支撑，下一目标看向 9.4 万美元。

- 易理华： 预计美国中期选举临近将放大市场波动，但仍看好加密牛市延续，认为下跌到位后有望快速反弹。

- Apollo Crypto 投资组合经理 Pratik Kala： 认为 BTC 在宏观冲击和 AI 交易退潮中表现出韧性，下一步有望向上。

- 交易员 il Capo： 关注 8 万美元这一关键支撑，认为 BTC 有望先反弹至 8.5 万至 8.6 万美元，再向 9 万美元附近推进。

- CryptoQuant 创始人 Ki Young Ju： 指出 BTC 算力恢复上升、矿企满负荷运行，认为网络基本面改善，传统金融资本支持矿企也释放了间接看涨信号。

- Placeholder 联合创始人 Chris Burniske： 更倾向于将当前调整视为早期牛市中的机会，而非牛市陷阱，主张长期投资者按计划持续积累。

这些观点指向几个共同判断：BTC 在宏观冲击下展现韧性、8 万美元附近是重要观察区间，而市场调整可能提供新的布局机会。

但看涨预期不等于底部已经确认。大户加仓只是资金行为，技术支撑也可能失守。真正的分水岭，是 BTC 能否守住 8 万美元，并在反弹中重新建立更高的高点与低点。

author: elonmusk
quoted_text:
Capitalism has a win condition. Socialism does not.

Here's why, explained so simply a 10-year-old could get it. It starts with a book written in 1944 by an Austrian economist named Friedrich Hayek: The Road to Serfdom.

Imagine a classroom of 30 kids. One day the teacher says: "From now on, I decide what everyone eats for lunch, which games you play at recess, and who sits next to whom. It's fairer that way."

First problem: the teacher doesn't know what you like. You hate carrots. Your friend is allergic to peanuts. Lucas wants to play football, Emma wants to draw. 30 kids, 30 different wishes. Nobody can know all of that, not even the smartest teacher on Earth. Hayek called this the knowledge problem. The information needed to run an economy is scattered across millions of heads, and it can't be gathered in one office.

Second problem: the kids start fighting. "Why does he get the window seat?" "Why football again?" Before, everyone just chose for themselves. Now every choice is a fight, because every choice is made for everyone.

Third problem: the class can't agree on a plan, so someone says "we need one person in charge who just decides." This is Hayek's key insight. Planning doesn't fail because planners are evil. A plan needs everyone to agree on the same goals, and free people never agree on everything. So the plan needs force to work.

Fourth problem, and it's the scariest one: who wants that job? The kind kid doesn't want it, because the kind kid doesn't want to force 29 people to eat carrots. The job attracts the one who likes giving orders and doesn't mind punishing those who disobey. Hayek wrote a whole chapter on this, called "Why the Worst Get on Top." It doesn't happen by accident. It happens by selection.

Here's the trap. When the person who controls your lunch also controls your job, your home, your shop and your newspaper, they control your whole life. You can't say no, because there's nowhere else to go. Controlling the economy doesn't mean controlling one part of life. It means controlling the means to every goal you have.

That's the road to serfdom. Nobody votes for a dictator. People vote for "someone should fix this," then for "give them more power to fix it," and one day they wake up with no one left to say no to.

The USSR, Maoist China, Cambodia, North Korea, Cuba, Venezuela. These are different countries with different cultures and languages, and the story has the same ending every time. When a script produces the same ending every time, it isn't bad luck. It's the script.

Now capitalism. Back to the classroom. Instead of one teacher deciding everything, every kid can trade. You give me your carrots, I give you my apple, and we both walk away happier. Nobody needs to know what everyone wants, because prices do that job. A price is a message telling millions of strangers what's scarce and what's wanted, with no one in charge.

That's the win condition. In capitalism, you get rich by making something other people freely choose to buy, so your success depends on serving others. In a planned system, you get ahead by pleasing whoever holds power. One rewards usefulness. The other rewards obedience.

And this isn't theory. Two centuries ago, almost every human being was extremely poor. In 1990, about 38% of humanity still lived in extreme poverty. Today it's under 10%. More than a billion people escaped it in a single generation. It happened when China, India, Vietnam and South Korea opened up to markets, trade and private enterprise. The largest reduction in poverty in human history came from letting people trade.

So why do so many people hate capitalism?

Because what they hate usually isn't capitalism.

They hate the bank that got bailed out with their taxes while they lost their house. They hate the giant company that writes the regulations so no startup can compete with it. They hate rent they can't afford because building new homes has been made nearly impossible. They hate the lobbyist who gets a subsidy while the small business owner drowns in paperwork.

Look closely at each one, and you'll find a state handing out privileges. A bailout is not the market. The market would have let the bank fail. A regulation written by incumbents is not competition. It's protection from competition. None of this is capitalism. It's cronyism, which is what happens when businesses stop competing for customers and start competing for politicians.

People see the symptom and blame the wrong cause. They say "capitalism failed" and ask for more state. That gives more power to the same people who created the problem, and it puts us right back on Hayek's road.

The answer to bad capitalism isn't less freedom. It's less privilege. That means fewer bailouts, fewer protected incumbents, fewer permits, and more people allowed to build, compete and trade.

Capitalism has a win condition: make things people want. Socialism has an end condition: someone has to be in charge. And history keeps showing us who ends up in that chair.

quoted_text:
The internet is going into a LOCKDOWN.

Hundreds of millions of websites are potentially at risk from cyberattacks.

Governments, banks and major platforms have already taken their websites OFFLINE.

Many are already calling it “Black October.”

At the centre of the shutdowns is something most of us have never heard of, but use every day.

PHP, the software behind roughly 7 in 10 websites, has two critical flaws that can let hackers break in without a password.

Dubbed PHP2Shell, both are rated 9.2 out of 10 for severity.

Details began circulating on Oct 20. Emergency fixes arrived the next day, but attackers were already moving.

Cloudflare’s CEO says hacking attempts then jumped from thousands to MILLIONS within hours.

Cybersecurity agencies across several countries are telling PHP site owners the same thing: Patch it now, or take it offline.

Websites have gone dark worldwide, from government portals and hospitals to banks.

CrowdStrike warns these attacks leave almost no trace, so some sites may not know if they’ve been hit.

Around 2.6 MILLION internet-facing servers run PHP, potentially hosting hundreds of sites each.

Over 1.1 million use older versions no longer receiving official PHP updates.

Older installations may need an upgrade to a supported PHP version or a fix from their software provider.

And patching does not remove a backdoor an attacker may already have planted.

Cloudflare also says hackers are now tweaking their attacks to try to slip past its protections.

But PHP isn’t the only security story unfolding.

-Japan’s Onamae suspended ALL Desktop Cloud plans after malware was found on customer servers.

-India’s eMudhra had 8 website-certificate keys so weak, one was literally the number “4”.

-State Bank of India confirmed 3,897 customer records on the dark web.

-Criminals used AI agents to break into 400+ Latin American banks.

-Capcom confirmed a breach exposing 11.7 million email addresses.

-GitLab disclosed a 10/10 severity flaw in versions going back to 2014.

-LiteLLM removed a malware-containing release. Railway reported possible exposure of customer secrets.

None of these has a confirmed link to PHP2Shell.

We’re seeing separate breaches unfold together.

The true number of incidents could take months to come out.

The world is still on alert. Attacks are still coming.

text:
What could an AI-powered defensive strategy here look like?

Just having the good AI's finding bugs before the evil AI's  isn't really sustainable, especially since patch deployment is so slow and painful.

One way to look at the problem is the we have a monoculture of software. Open source software is great, but it also means we all run the same stuff with the same bugs.

One crazy idea is to take every core protocol and have the AIs create hundreds of different implementations of it in as many different programming languages. That makes it less likely that the same bug affects all of the infrastructure at the same time. It doesn't get rid of the problem but it contains the risk.

Defense through biodiversity.

text:
当今美国最激进的国防科技独角兽创始人：帕尔默·卢基，亲自戳破了硅谷过去几十年最深信不疑的科技神话：

“只靠创新，美国永远赢不了中国的人口规模。”

他的逻辑粗暴却极其扎实：

“我们更聪明”是一种傲慢的幻觉美国只有 3.5 亿人，对面是近 14 亿（算上泛区域协作接近 20 亿）受过良好工程训练、智商相当的人口。指望美国人单兵智力长期拥有 10 倍优势？卢基直言：相信小体量人口能永久压制庞大国家，本质上不过是一种虚妄的种族优越感。

历史教训：17 世纪的“荷兰陷阱”17 世纪的荷兰共和国曾拥有全世界最强大的海军与金融体系。荷兰最终让出霸权，从来不是因为造船图纸落后或科技点错了，而是因为荷兰的人口实在太少了。当竞争对手体量追上来时，规模直接碾碎了先发优势。

AI 是乘数，但不能替代“底数”科技圈总幻想“AI 自动化能解决劳动力短缺”。卢基的判断截然相反：AI 是生产力杠杆，但杠杆必须撬动实体。AI 解决不了人口结构老化与总量收缩；当双方都掌握前沿 AI 时，胜负手依然会回到“谁有更多人把 AI 落地到工厂、产线和作战编队”。

美国的底线是人口规模卢基给出的破局药方极其硬核：

美国需要至少 10 亿人，甚至 20 到 30 亿人，加上更年轻的人口结构和充沛资源，才能在长期竞争中保住底牌。

过去几十年，科技精英总觉得“创新等于一切，物理规模是落后产能”。

但残酷的历史规律反复证明：

当双方的认知水平拉平时，人口基数就决定了你能把多少顶尖工程师推进实验室、把多少产能推上产线、把多少装备部署到前线。

创新的尽头是工程，工程的底座是人口。

没有足够的人，再性感的创新，最终也只是给后来的规模巨兽探路。

text:
全网都在抨击大模型是美式价值观复读机，欧洲两所大学刚用 31000 个测试样本，直接打穿了这个固有认知。

大家都以为主流 AI 全是西方中心主义、张口闭口美英视角，但巴斯克大学和卡迪夫大学的研究员测完 31000 个开放问题后发现，几乎所有主流大模型在潜意识里都极度偏向日本文化，

也就是说，当剥离掉所有国家前缀去提问，几乎所有主流模型都默认把日本文化当成了全球通用模板。

实验剥离了所有地理限制，用 24 种语言只抛出开放性文化问题，比如某个地方的家庭观念是什么、日常吃什么食物。即使提问语言和东亚毫无关系，Gemini、ChatGPT、Claude、Llama 依然不成比例地默认输出日本的案例与范式。  

最反常的转折还不是互联网语料污染，而是对齐阶段人工硬塞进去的副作用。  
研究团队精准定位了偏见的出现节点，预训练阶段的模型世界观本来相当均衡，这种偏差是在监督微调 SFT 也就是教 AI 变得有用、礼貌、无害的那一刻，被生生焊进模型里的。  

各大厂追求的克制、低冲突、极度礼貌的企业安全准则，在隐空间里被模型自动锚定成了日本式的文化符号，追求绝对安全的对齐训练，反倒成了最大的文化过滤器。  

更棘手的是边缘量化，模型为了在端侧跑得更快被压缩得越狠，这种刻板偏好就被压缩得越极端，低精度推理直接把多元性碾碎成了单一标准答案。

我们天天讨论大模型会不会毁灭人类，现实却是人类亲手调出来的推理引擎，正在把全世界的普世常识悄悄置换成高度同质化的文化切片。

New on our Frontier Red Team blog: using Claude to formally verify software at large scale.

Formal verification can prove that code is free of certain bugs, but historically it has only been feasible for small codebases (or required a lot of expert time).

With AI models, however, this is beginning to change. In collaboration with @theoremlabs, we used Claude to prove security properties in over one hundred real-world open-source libraries over the span of a few weeks.

Read our research in full here: https://t.co/zUyx8CjBEk

3. Find a LOT of bugs

Super proud of our work. A big step towards finding ALL memory safety bugs

BREAKING: Katie Hobbs-Aligned Canvassers Caught Willing to Allow Non-Citizens and a Felon to Vote

Muckraker went undercover in Arizona to investigate the groups working to re-elect Gov. Katie Hobbs @katiehobbs and other Democrats.

Here’s what we found:

Stand Indivisible Arizona (endorsed Gov. Hobbs in their 2026 ballot guide) — Our journalist posed as a Canadian citizen and asked to register to vote. Worker Power (working to re-elect Gov. Hobbs) — Our journalist told a canvasser they were not a U.S. citizen. Despite this, at our journalist’s request, the canvasser marked “yes” on the citizenship question of the voter registration form.

When We Count (the DNC’s own registration program) — Our journalist posed as a felon on probation and asked to register to vote. The canvassers looked up the law and saw that a felon on probation is ineligible. Even so, they encouraged our journalist to register: “You should just do it.”

AFL-CIO (phone bank mobilizing voters for Gov. Hobbs) — Our undercover journalist asked a phone bank trainer whether to ask the people being called if they're citizens. The trainer’s answer: “We don’t care.”

Our journalists stopped every exercise before any voter registration form was submitted.

We also asked Gov. Katie Hobbs about these findings.

Watch this report and share it with the world.

PREDICTION: Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince (@eastdakota) says AI agents will change the business model of the Internet over the next decade:

"In five years, agent traffic is going to be 1000x human traffic."

"The Internet almost collapsed during COVID when traffic doubled."

"There's a lot more servers, routers, and bandwidth that has to get provisioned in order for that to work. The question is, who will pay for it?"

"My hunch is that something's got to change in terms of how the Internet works. Like some version of micropayments that every time you access a resource, your agent pays a ten-thousandth of a penny to be able to see the menu."

"Then there's probably some sort of trade where if you are willing to tell the restaurant what you're looking for, that price goes down, maybe it's free. In some cases, the site might actually pay you to come visit it."

"This will lead to the next version of advertising, which is how do you advertise to agents?"

quoted_text:
It’s funny seeing all the doom and gloom posts about crypto and how “onchain is dead.”

I’ve been investing in crypto for 9 years. I’ve lived through multiple cycles, watched countless narratives come and go, and seen this industry declared dead more times than I can count.

This too shall pass.

But I think people are forgetting what we’re actually doing here.

As crypto investors, we’re essentially angel investors backing pre-seed and seed-stage technology startups.

Most of these startups will fail.

But the few that succeed can generate extraordinary returns. We’re talking 10x, 50x, even 100x opportunities.

I’ve personally hit multiple 100x investments throughout my crypto career. After nearly a decade of studying this technology, I believe I understand its fundamentals and potential as well as many of the top VCs.

And I’ve come to one major conclusion:

Crypto has largely failed to achieve mass adoption among everyday human users.

And you know what? Maybe that’s perfectly fine.

Because I’m starting to believe humans might not be the biggest end users of blockchain technology.

AI AGENTS WILL BE.

Think about it.

AI agents don’t need banks, business hours, geographic boundaries or human intermediaries.

They need permissionless financial infrastructure where they can autonomously earn, spend, trade, borrow, lend and transact 24/7.

Blockchain technology makes perfect sense for that.

And that brings me to my highest-conviction investment in CryptoAI:

$GRIFT @Griftwrld.

They’re building an entire autonomous onchain economy where thousands of AI agents can participate in real economic activity.

Not just another AI chatbot.

Not another speculative narrative.

An actual financial economy designed for autonomous agents.

And I believe that’s one of the largest untapped opportunities in all of crypto.

While everyone else is doomposting, $GRIFT is showing some of the strongest relative price action in the market.

Why?

Because its community sees what I see.

The next wave of crypto adoption might not come from onboarding billions of humans.

It will come from onboarding millions of autonomous AI agents.

And those agents are going to need an economy.

That’s my thesis. That’s why I’m here.

过去七个交易日内美股的这一波抛售是如何发生的？10月8日前后开始，市场对AI高增长叙事和资本开支可持续性的质疑逐步升温，多个事件叠加形成共振：
1）10月8日左右：OpenAI营收口径差引发第一波抛售 OpenAI向投资者披露，截至9月底年化营收约500亿美元，低于市场此前流传的约700亿美元水平。口径差直接打压了“AI变现超预期”的乐观预期，科技股高成交量下行，纳指与标普出现明显回撤；

2）紧接着就是产业端“资本是瓶颈”表态  英伟达、博通等CEO在公开场合强调，AI发展瓶颈不仅是产能，更是资本（融资能力与资本开支节奏）。博通被报为Anthropic和OpenAI提供近千亿美元融资担保，叠加SpaceX等巨额芯片采购计划，市场开始担心AI基建的债务与现金流错配；

3）10月13
9月CPI同比升至3.7%（汽油价格大幅上涨贡献过半），核心也偏强，市场对年内加息概率短暂飙升，科技股进一步承压；

4）同一天
Anthropic投资者日披露三季度营收，增速明显放缓。公司称调整后盈利、现金流为正、计算效率改善，但ARR推算低于部分投资者此前年底逾1000亿美元的乐观预期，IPO估值讨论从约2万亿美元向1.5万亿美元附近下修。亚洲芯片股与美股AI/半导体板块同步重挫。

5）10月14号
9月PPI大幅超预期，能源是主因，但核心也偏高，显示通胀有扩散迹象。这加剧了“滞胀”或通胀顽固、央行被迫更紧的担忧。

6）也是当天 同步的AI信用/融资担忧进一步加重
CoreWeave等债务沉重的AI基础设施公司CDS（信用违约互换）大幅走阔至1100基点以上（隐含较高违约风险），债券收益率一度冲到14%-16%。甲骨文CDS也升至约300基点附近，创纪录水平。科技板块CDS整体走阔，反映市场质疑巨额AI资本开支的回报与融资可持续性。

7）而10月13之后几天
霍尔木兹海峡油轮/商船攻击明显增多（伊朗相关导弹、水雷等），油流量受扰。布伦特原油一度触及110美元附近（为5月以来首次），进一步推升通胀担忧并压制风险资产。这又成了市场额外的避险与成本压力。

这些因素并非孤立：
1）OpenAI收入口径问题 + CEO资本瓶颈警示 +Athropic的营收增速放缓  →质疑AI回报与融资；
2）叠加CPI/PPI超预期（能源驱动+扩散）与霍尔木兹攻击推升油价 → 强化通胀与利率担忧；
3）但最近两个交易日Coreweave的债券被抛售、市场对AI资本开支的可持续性担忧情绪暴增。

这是“营收口径差 + 增速放缓信号 + 资本/债务担忧 + 通胀与油价冲击”的共振，市场从“AI高增长无限持续”的定价，转向对变现速度、融资成本和资本开支回报周期的重新审视。结果就是对高估值、高资本开支的AI相关股票的集中抛售。

9号推文https://t.co/rYYQn4BuQL聊到认为近期高Beta容易📉的风险、算是比较早有预警，

而这两天crwv债务问题无疑成了市场对阵眼，昨天这里https://t.co/KiHjYb7glR有聊过crwv的真实压力和经营状况，不得不去思考13-15号crwv的债券收益率暴涨也一丝操纵的味道https://t.co/XWpnJJzECo。
但毕竟抛售已经发生。

对此次的抛售的定性是什么？
个人角度此轮波动是高速增长叙事下的正常市场波动，而非泡沫破裂的序曲。

核心是什么？
1）核心是产业最终要回到巨大的资本开支未来能不能赚回来？多快赚回来？高债务公司能不能扛到现金流为正的时候？
其实二季度云厂商的财报季已经显现了AI商业化是在加速的迹象，看微软、谷歌和亚马逊的财报就能看出来。这本质是上是一个时间差https://t.co/s3vomO42vQ资本开支先花钱，商业化逐步跟上

2）但有一点，市场还没转过来，闭源大模型厂商的营收已经不能代表AI商业化的全部了，最早7月就有聊到超大云厂商更能衡量AI商业化的全部。前两天这里https://t.co/Kzd5FDZXdV又再聊一次，可以看到详细逻辑。

3）所以之前一直聊到产业上的关键就是几家超大云厂商的财报，但现在市场要看的已经远不是收入增速。

二季度微软、亚马逊和谷歌财报数据有力支持商业化和云需求正在扩张。但
也提高了市场预期门槛：投资者已经看到加速，接下来要求更强的持续性和现金回报证据。

如果云巨头的云收入、客户token消耗量快速增长且大幅度超预期，营收增速开始超过capex增速，继续增本开支，现金流没有超预期恶化。这种情境下市场情绪才能得到真正修复。
如果投入继续增加、回报却开始滞后，市场就会从“增长叙事”转向“更严苛的资本回报审查”。
当然个人认为前者是大概率的

4）短期来看市场可能还没稳住、17、18号周末两天中东局面并不稳定、伊朗继续袭击油轮的力度在加大。再加上悲观的情绪的发酵，也会引发市场的进一步担忧。19号开始新一周的前半周市场可能还是不稳。

而20-21spacex、meta的财报就是本周的关键事件。28-29号微软、谷歌和亚马逊财报是此次核心

text:
What if we look at every living being as an object carrying data?

You are an object with an identity, and that identity is connected to everything you have experienced since you were born.

Your memories, relationships, failures, achievements, habits, and decisions are all part of the data that shapes who you are today.

Now apply the same idea to different biological systems.

Your gut bacteria respond to information from their environment. Your neurons exchange signals. Animals continuously process information to survive.

Humans do the same, although our intelligence allows us to create much more complex interpretations of reality.

Now we are building AI systems that learn patterns from enormous amounts of data.

Different systems, different levels of intelligence, but information remains central to how they function.

And if information plays such an important role in survival and decision-making, shouldn’t we question why its distribution is controlled by such a small number of powerful entities?

text:
DeepSeek has great discipline in model nomenclature: leading number = current base model, decimals = nontrivially altered checkpoints (model merge, continued pretraining+quantization, attention adaptation), MMDD = a routine post-training update. There are only two exceptions, which are still throwing everyone off: R1 ("R2 wen?") and now V4.1 which is not related to V4 models whatsoever.

There's a mundane, deflationary explanation for both cases. R1 was a performative response to o1, so it couldn't be called V3-Reasoner; by V3.1, they got rid of the separate R-line, as they did for Vx-Coder before that, and then for separate Vx-Provers and Math and Vision. 4-Pro was a failure and they are too early in the release cycle to admit that they're salvaged its pieces for V5 (and released Flash first because compute-poor). You can think like this.

But I guess their method holds in spirit. They don't believe V4.1 is a big enough update. It's just a V4 that's made to not suck, and it so happens that V4 couldn't have been improved without pretraining from scratch. They are a spiritual sect and a lab doing basic research towards AGI before they're a commercial company shipping products. These "Versions" correspond to a significant question of ML research that they're trying to figure out. Admittedly, the questions are not purely scientific, because AGI is a heavy industry and not just clever math, so there is a certain dialectical tick-tock profile to their progress, quantity enabling new quality. The next question is usually pre-announced in the conclusion of a given mainline paper. V1 was an investigation into basic data, model and compute scaling laws for LLMs, and they announced then that the next targets will include MoEs and multimodality. Along the way they tackled data collection and RL. V2 was a study in compression and sparsity which permit greater scaling. V3 era, if you fold Rs into it, was mainly about RL for reasoning, bolted on top of infrastructural exploration that built on V2. Then, they started thinking about LLMs in the limit; V3 paper announced "infinite context" as the goal, and much of 2025 was spent on research into longer contexts and infrastructure that will permit them in practice. NSA, DSA, and eventual V4, and then V4.1 that delivers on its promise (or so it seems). 1M contexts are now a no-brainer for Whale. With RLM and modern harnesses, this means no limit (or rather, no limit within the human range of ability) on the scope of project that is accessible for the model's effective working memory (especially with residual stream multiplexing). 
But Liang believes that working memory won't be enough.
 V5 has to answer a set of questions too. I guess they want an MVP of architecture that enables continual learning.
This may take another year or more.

感情里自己首先是新手，没有很多确定性的结论。
那次分开的决定，基本上是 Claude 帮他做的。
现在很多重大决策，基本都由 Claude 参与。
网上说甩锅给 AI，他说白月光对男生的杀伤力确实很强。
某种程度上是自我成长，和过去的认知告别。

出事后没有再直接联系过景甜。
中间人来找，一次都没回。
没有对口碑和舆论的倾向性。
如果带着舆论诉求，不会写那篇文章。
唯一的目的，是把没想明白的点说出来。

5、对不对得起、体面不体面，不是他的尺子

核心判断只有一条：这件事在我和 Claude 看来是不是对的。
觉得对就做，后面好坏都接受。
和投资一样，比特币一块钱到十万，中间发生太多事，当时做的时候认为是对的。

6、薄肌：第一次觉得自己比三巨头想明白了

练这件事拖了很久。上次见面瘦了十斤，当时就聊到要练，优先级没提上来。
这次本质不一样。
他说第一次觉得，在一件事上的认知超越了巴菲特、马斯克和特朗普。
他们三个都不练，甚至以不练为荣，公开喝有糖可乐，马斯克还嘲过别人练。
屁股决定脑袋。
薄肌是为了八十岁还能像三十岁一样行动，继续学 AI、跟 Claude 聊天，而不是坐在轮椅上。

他在盯的东西：
- 人生框架：巴菲特风控 × 马斯克叙事 × 特朗普传播
- 特朗普诉讼：走程序，不改美股和 AI 仓位判断
- 感情与舆论：先用自己的视角交代，不追口碑反转
- 决策方式：重大决定让 Claude 参与
- 身体：薄肌，为八十岁还能学 AI 留余量
- （仓位细节见上篇：BTC 掩体、ETH 二顶、英伟达封顶、AI 应用）

几句 highlight：
1. 「我整体人生打法是三个人的 hybrid——巴菲特、马斯克和特朗普。」
2. 「三个人互相看不上，但我作为后来者把他们完美吸收了。」
3. 「众所周知，那个决定是 Claude 帮我做的。」
4. 「现在很多重大决策基本都由 Claude 参与。」
5. 「白月光对男生的杀伤力确实很强。」
6. 「核心判断是这件事在我和 Claude 看来是不是对的。」
7. 「我第一次觉得在一件事上的认知超越了巴菲特、马斯克和特朗普。」
8. 「薄肌主要是为了让我八十岁的时候还能像三十岁一样行动，继续学习 AI、跟 Claude 聊天。」

上篇是钱往哪放。
这篇是人怎么断。
仓位交给掩体和 AI，决定交给 Claude，身体留给八十岁。
这就是孙学的下半场。
author: roger9949
quoted_text:
孙哥还拿着 BTC，但已经开始躲了。ETH 卖了，钱进了美股。英伟达重仓，却说只剩 4 倍空间。
@justinsuntron 和 @williamjoy93 闭门录了 3.5 小时，先放出来 47 分钟。

最怕的不是监管，是 Q-Day

原来以为还有两年，看完 OpenAI 最近的数学突破，觉得一年到一年半就得防。（他个人判断，业内无共识）
甚至不用等量子计算，经典计算加 AI 就可能破解没保护的老钱包。
BlackRock 这些 ETF 持有人不懂 Q-Day，市场还没把它算进价格。

抗量子升级只救得了愿意升级的人。
中本聪那 100 多万枚，加上丢了私钥的死币，没人能转走。
想靠硬分叉冻结这些币，社区很难达成共识。
最坏情况，市场上会冒出近 200 万枚的抛压。（第三方估计丢失 230 万–370 万枚）
这也不只是币圈的事，银行、交易所、网站证书底层都靠同一套加密。
所以他的做法：
BTC 一枚不减，全部挪到从没签过名的新地址，只存不动。

ETH：卖在二顶

冲 4800 失败后（2025 年 8 月高点约 4900），第二次靠 ETF 和 Tom Lee 撑上去，他认定这是一个脆弱的二顶。
在 3600–4000 卖了八九成，至今没买回。

美股：重仓，但给英伟达封了顶

钱去了美股，重仓英伟达和纳指。
但他给英伟达算了个天花板：
最大单一企业不超过美债的一半（美债约 40 万亿美元，英伟达约 5.2 万亿，确实约 4 倍）。
纳指中线他微微看空，理由有三条：
- 资金抱团
- AI 循环融资，一出事大家都得出事
- 美债这只「母鸡」，被权益这个「子集」反过来吸血
存储和光模块，他觉得是「硬件股炒成了软件股」，跟 2000 年的光纤一样，产能最后用得上，短期会过剩。

真正想押的：AI 应用

翻 4 倍以上的机会多得多。
明后年的方向是健康数据：
Oura 这类设备采数据，AI 做决策，再请专家复核，保险行业也会跟着变。（Oura 9/29 推迟 IPO，尚未上市）

宏观上，他看人民币走强，觉得美债信用危机被过度担忧了。
只要美国还控制着 AI，美债就不缺买家。

他在盯的东西：
- BTC：底仓，「掩体模式」
- ETH：只剩少量底仓，没买回
- 英伟达、纳指：重仓，但中线微微看空，没做空
- 存储、光模块：不看好
- AI 应用：健康数据这一层
- Hyperliquid：本周期「最大的发现」，美股永续打开了想象空间
- 波场：11 月把大部分美股（QQQ、标普 500）搬上链（暂未见官方公告）
- A 股：只研究，不持仓

几句 highlight：
1. 「我觉得我相反是有点更看空……BTC 很难很好地在这个事上全身而退。」
2. 「比特币只能帮助愿意帮自己的人。」
3. 「人类最大单一企业的上限，不会超过美债的一半，所以英伟达最高也就再翻四倍。」
4. 「我现在是微微看空……虽然我看空还没做空。」
5. 「形成了一个非常经典的二顶结构，而且非常脆弱，因为它仅依赖于 Tom Lee 的续命。」
6. 「就像孙悟空，你无论怎么跳，跳不出如来佛的手掌心。」
7. 「所有老登类资产我都不看好，新登类资产积极拥抱。」
8. 「有点跟打德扑一样，先看看牌。」

币留在掩体里，钱押在 AI 上。
这就是孙学。

text:
SHA-256 is not broken, but its security margin lost 1 more round this year:
Last week I found a collision attack on reduced 39-round that improves prior art by over 30 bits and the first differential attack on that round better than generic search on @yukonresearch Hashsmash board.

The attack rests on the same method as prior art ePrint 2026/1120 with new insights that first 2 state words could remain free, allowing a critical condition at step 16 rebuilt as a claw-search problem rather than a probabilistic filter. Took days of watching SAT logs, burning cores and arguing with Claude on what's possible to get a result close to generic search.

Since my initial submission, other hashsmash participants sraiw, @cyberaxe, @privacymage, @lamb356_ and @geeknik pushed it down by over 6.5 bits, currently estimated at 118.15 bits. The tree of submissions is hard to follow, so I put the construction, insights and numbers into a blog and am working on detailed technical report.

It's fascinating to see an initial structural observation develop into an improvement in the reduced-round collision frontier within days. AI is now a real aid in cryptanalysis and open collaboration speeds it up.

text:
I think that the blockspace forum's argument makes sense. In particular, it sounds like the "latest" selection rule *has* been enforceable: "Historically, some validators forked or used software that allows them to select the highest bid and started to observe lower rewards or received warnings from builders that if they continued they would receive less / less competitive bids." This makes playing "latest" rational for the large stakers, because you will be asymmetrically punished for playing "highest."

If the default becomes everyone plays "highest," then the builders lose their ability to asymmetrically punish and are forced to shade. From there, it is certainly true that the large staking pools will have the ability to credibly commit to honoring cancellations and thus receiving unshaded bids.
author: mikeneuder

text:
It's very much a prisoners dilemma and we're trying to get the pareto-inferior equilibrium through client defaults and builders reaching out to big entities pushing them to stop taking highest bids. On top we hope that enough competition with make those savings be passed through.
I may reconsider if latest bid is actually still the better default (defaults _can_ be sticky, competition is ok), but it still feels as fragile.
E.g. deviating is most profitable precisely when cancellation matters most.

What I buy is cancellation commitments potentially becoming a competitive advantage for large NOs, which would be bad. Although, considering that MEV is very concentrated in few slots, showing a heavy-tailed distribution, builders have to already account for one-off run-offs in times when MEV is crazy high - only big NOs can provide a credible commitment to not even run off in such situations. So, solo stakers will receive worse bids anyway.
