author: CryptoScoopOG
quoted_text:
this California wealth tax thing is just incredible. 

so in October 2025, a California healthcare union proposed a "one time" 5% tax on any billionaire's wealth. the ballot measure will be voted on next month. In early December 2025, California announced that it would be a retroactive tax if passed, applying to anyone with CA residency as of Jan 1, 2026. The objective is to pay for Medi-Cal, California's incredibly dysfunctional healthcare system. (which also functions as a glorified welfare apparatus, but that's a discussion for another time). 

polls reveal that the CA electorate is split around 50/50 on the tax, but prediction markets only give Prop 40 a ~23% chance of passing (there are competing measures on the ballet that would nullify it). 

there are 200 billionaires in CA, worth collectively somewhere between $2.3 and $2.6 trillion. 5% of that is around $100b, accounting for a small amount of attrition. proponents of the tax forecasted a significant windfall, assuming only a 10% departure rate. 

supporters thought they were being clever with the retroactive concept. no billionares would leave CA in the few short months between the tax being proposed and the residency cutoff date, without the tax even having passed yet, right? 

well as it turns out, they did. 

a new paper [1] from two academics at Stanford called "The Net Present Value of the California Billionaire Tax Act", argues that not only did more billionaires leave due to the proposed tax than its proponents expected, but that the value of the tax, if it does pass, is actually negative. 

proponents of the tax only assumed 10% avoidance, that is, only 10% of the taxable base of targeted billionaires would leave CA within the very short Oct-Dec 2025 window. Jaros and Rauh, the Stanford academics, find that a lower bound of 28.6% of the taxable base managed to leave. 

just based on known departures, those departures total $577b in net worth, or $28.8b in potential tax lost. this of course does not capture everyone (many left without announcing their departure), so the authors normalize to departure rates estimated from other wealth tax events, and apply other discounts for litigation, arriving arrive at a figure of only $28-$36b in forecasted tax revenues. 

but this isn't all! all of the income taxes paid by the departed billionaires are also forsaken. the authors estimate that CA billionaires pay $3.3- 5.8b in annual income taxes. they assume a midpoint of $2b lost in annual collections from departed billionaires. the net present value of that lost income stream is -$68.9 billion. 

so when you add it all up you get: 

+ $30b one-time tax windfall (estimated)  
- $69b in present value of lost future income taxes
= - 38.9b overall net present value of the tax 

of course, this analysis is highly estimate driven. the authors simulate the parameters 100k times and find a negative NPV of the implemented tax 85 percent of the time.

Anthropic 冲刺 1.5 万亿美元 IPO！VC 狂赚数百亿，而 FTX 错失了 1000 亿美金

最快 11 月中旬，Anthropic 将迎来史诗级上市！市场传出 IPO 估值高达 1.5 万亿美元，比今年 5 月融资时再涨 55%。这场 AI 终极狂欢，让早期 VC 机构赚麻了，也留下了加密史上最痛的遗憾！

VC 人均斩获百亿美金

• Iconiq：持股价值约 $264 亿（投入 >$60亿） 
• Menlo Ventures：持股价值约 $218 亿（投入 >$10亿） 
• 红杉资本：持股价值约 $150 亿（投入 ~$30亿，约 1% 股份） 
• GIC (新加坡主权基金)：持股价值约 $150 亿（投入 >$45亿，约 1% 股份） 
• Spark Capital：持股价值约 $109 亿（初始仅投 $7500万） 
• Eric Schmidt (Google前CEO)：个人持股价值约 $150 亿

FTX 倒在黎明前

2021 年 FTX 仅用 $5 亿拿下了 Anthropic 13.56% 的股权。然而因破产清算，FTX 在 2024 年被迫以 $13 亿清仓卖出（折合净赚 $8 亿，买家包括 Mubadala、Jane Street 等）。

若 FTX 坚持持有到现在，即使算上稀释，这笔股权理论价值也将高达 $1,176 亿美元！FTX 相当于为了 $8 亿利润，提前下车错失了上千亿美元的潜在大顶。

AI 时代顶尖模型的资本虹吸效应太恐怖了，早期下注的 VC 赚取了整整一个时代的红利，而倒在清算里的破产机构，则留下了史上最昂贵的“筹码贱卖”教训。

最近 BIT @BITstocks_CN 推出 Anthropic AI 季活动，最高 $40,000 美元股票卡奖池，还蛮吸引人的

不过比起活动，我更想分享最近深度使用 BIT 的一些心得

本来以为就是另一家 crypto 交易所，结果用下来，发现他其实更像是一家能用稳定币出入金的美股、港股券商

有几个地方确实让我蛮惊艳：

1. 稳定币直接买美港股

USDT / USDC 可以直接入金、兑换美元或港币，再去买美股、港股，也支援传统电汇，甚至还有 OTC 买币服务

对本来就在币圈的用户来说，省掉很多资金转换的麻烦

2. 开户速度很快  

符合资格的内地朋友，能用內地身分证线上申请美港股帐户，这应该是很大的诱因

3. 股票、ETF 的选择超出预期

美股、港股接入当地证券市场，买的是真实股票，不是 CFD 或股票代币

连 $AAOI 的两倍反向 ETF $AAOZ 这种冷门产品都找得到，还能依杠杆、反向、地区、债券、大宗商品、指数分类

不过冷门 ETF 的流动性和杠杆风险还是得自己留意！

4. 股票研究仪表板做得很细

可以直接比较同产业公司的本益比、估值、财务指标，看出竞争对手之间的相对强弱

这对经常研究不同产业、比较股票的人来说，蛮实用的

5. 支援证券转仓

原本放在 IBKR、老虎、富途、国泰君安等券商的股票，可以依支援情况申请转进 BIT，不需要先卖掉再买回

6. 财经日历整合得很完整

经济数据、财报日期、股息、休市资讯都整理在 App 里

以前还要跳出去开金十数据、财经网站，现在少切换好几个页面

7. 港股新股中心很用心

已上市、暗盘中、认购中、已递表的公司都有分类

连新股首日、上市一年后的涨跌幅统计都有，研究港股 IPO 不用自己东拼西凑

也支援小额配置，不过各自有不同的 KYC、最低申购金额及投资人资格要求

Here's how each work and what makes QAD a valuable tool for devs, labs and independent users.

Standard quantization:
The model’s parameters are stored at 16 bit precision. Quantizing rounds them down to 8 bit, or lower, like a zip file version of the model, making it smaller.

I-matrix:
Same idea, but it looks at the model first and finds the regions that appear most complex, assuming that complexity is where the capability lives. Those regions keep higher precision while the rest gets rounded harder.

Quantization Aware Distillation:
This method quantize the model, then treat the original model as a teacher and the quantized version as a student, training the student back toward its parent’s behaviour. It repairs what the rounding broke, needs inference and back propagation, meaning GPU work, which is why most people don’t do it, and why it’s the one worth having a service for.

Quantize LLMs with Bench

text:
The original idea behind crypto was to empower more people, remove unnecessary middlemen, and return the value they were extracting directly to the parties transacting with each other. 

Even when a platform was involved, the idea was to let the community decide its future rather than a few shareholders controlling everything.

It all looked fine in theory, but when we started experimenting with these ideas, we discovered much deeper execution-level problems.

One of the biggest problems was how we reward contribution.

We wanted to create an economy where contribution mattered more than capital, but when we introduced DAOs and governance tokens, capital started winning over contribution. People who held more tokens gained more influence than those who spent years building, educating, and growing those ecosystems.

We decentralized ownership without necessarily decentralizing power.

And when people realized that capital had more influence than contribution, they naturally started taking the side of capital.

Then came airdrops, where we tried to reward participation and contribution. It was a beautiful idea because ordinary users could finally become stakeholders without investing significant capital.

But it created another problem.

People started participating not because they believed in the network, but because they expected rewards. Contribution became something people started manufacturing through artificial transactions, multiple wallets, and meaningless activities.

We started rewarding what was measurable rather than what was meaningful.

Someone generating a thousand transactions could receive more rewards than someone who spent a year educating hundreds of people about the same ecosystem.

And when people received rewards, many didn’t realize the value of what they had received. They wanted more and more. 

Those who received less felt cheated, and communities built around shared beliefs gradually became communities driven by financial expectations.

We created an economy that rewarded participation but failed to create a culture that valued contribution.

And this is where the whole space started becoming toxic.

Today, we have an overcrowded industry where many participants neither have enough capital to influence the networks nor the skills or incentives to contribute something substantial.

Meanwhile, a smaller group of people who have mastered the art of extraction through capital, influence, and distribution continue accumulating more wealth.

Capital gives them influence, influence gives them access, access creates better opportunities, and those opportunities help them accumulate even more capital.

The irony is that we wanted to build an economy where contribution could challenge the dominance of capital, but we ended up creating another economy where capital continues to dominate contribution.

And I think the problem is much deeper than tokenomics.

We built systems to verify ownership of capital but never built equally strong systems to verify the authenticity, history, and reputation of contribution.

We can verify that someone holds a million dollars in a wallet, but we struggle to verify that someone spent five years making an ecosystem better.

This is why I believe the next evolution of crypto needs to focus on identity, reputation, and contribution.

We need systems where people can build verifiable histories of their contributions, where reputation cannot simply be purchased with capital, and where governance recognizes expertise, contribution, and community trust alongside financial ownership.

Of course, reputation shouldn’t become another form of aristocracy where early contributors permanently control everything. New contributors should have equal opportunities to build influence through meaningful work.

Because the original promise of crypto wasn’t simply to distribute tokens. It was to distribute power and economic opportunities.

- 𝗕𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹 𝟲 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗵𝘀 𝗼𝘂𝘁: early Claude Code revenue was flat for months because the model wasn't smart enough yet. Then Opus 4 came out and growth became astronomic. text:
Most agent memory systems are a "tax" on strong models.

This new study pits four memory modules (Mem0, Zep, BM25, full-context) against coding agents on a 419-turn dialogue, using GPT-4o-mini, GPT-6 Luna, and Claude Opus 5.5.

Key takeaways:
— With weak models (GPT-4o-mini), Mem0 barely beats full context (78% vs 74%), but building memory costs *more* than just answering.
— As models get stronger, memory modules plateau (95% tops), while coding agent Pi + Claude Opus 5.5 hits 99% accuracy at <$7—less than half the full-context cost.
— Memory’s accuracy is capped by the writer: a strong reader can’t recover facts a weak writer omits (Zep: 45% → 87% if rewritten by Claude).
— The last accuracy gap? Photo captions, not memory structure.

Bottom line: As models get smarter, hard-coded memory is a costly patch with shrinking returns. Just give the raw log and let the model search.

Get the full analysis here: https://t.co/AoNBxUx9zb

author: Eli5defi
quoted_text:
A DEX pool can earn fees while selling its assets too cheaply.

@metricxyz’s Active Pools aim to reduce that problem by updating prices as new market information arrives.

The key idea: separate pricing from liquidity.

Each pool uses a Price Provider, a smart contract that supplies:
• Bid: what the pool pays to buy an asset.
• Ask: what it charges to sell.
• Reference: the baseline around which liquidity is arranged.

A provider sets a reference price using oracle feeds, onchain data, or a market maker model.

LPs deposit into bins (percent ranges around that reference). The pool price is: Reference price × (1 + deviation)

Deviation reflects how trades moved the pool: buys push up, sells push down. Big trades can cross multiple bins and get worse prices.

Example: $100 with +1% deviation = $101. If the reference moves to $110 with no trades, price becomes $111.10.

This makes Bins shift with the reference; tokens don’t rebalance.

That’s the main difference from ordinary Uniswap v3 positions, whose price boundaries stay fixed. Metric reduces the need to reposition liquidity as the reference moves.

Curators run the pools. They choose pricing logic, configure fees and safeguards, and maintain updates. Public pools accept outside liquidity; private pools can restrict deposits to the operator’s capital.

The broader idea isn’t entirely new. DODO already adjusts quotes around inventory, and Uniswap v4 hooks allow custom pricing. Metric combines customizable pricing, moving liquidity ranges and shared market-making infrastructure.

That could suit assets with established external prices, including tokenized stocks, gold and major crypto assets.

Here’s how the money works:
• Traders pay spreads and any configured fees inside the quote, plus network gas.
• Spread and bin-fee income is shared among LPs, curators and Metric.
• LP earnings stay in their bins and compound.
• Curator and protocol fee shares can change without a timelock.

So “zero fees” doesn’t mean trading has no cost.

Protection also matters:
• Anchored pricing constrains quotes using an independent feed.
• Freshness checks can reject trades using stale data.
• StopLoss can reject swaps that breach configured drawdown checks.
• Participating Ethereum and BNB Chain builders commit to placing updates before trades.

Still, LPs remain exposed to inventory drawdowns, oracle outages, and curator-side risk.

Metric’s edge is that it keeps liquidity tracking a moving reference price, cutting down the need for constant hands-on range tweaking.

What will make or break Metric is whether it can deliver truly competitive execution and strong net LP outcomes once fees and inventory bleed are accounted for.

11 月 3 日，美国中期选举临近，大家又开始讨论“选举魔咒”。

中期选举会影响风险资产，核心原因是政策不确定性。

目前 bitcoin:native  已经被传统金融渠道广泛接受，越来越像高 Beta 的风险资产。中期选举带来的政策预期变化，一定程度也会传导到 BTC 上。

那么，BTC 在历届中期选举时的表现如何？

小编拉了下过去4轮4年周期里，中期选举前后的 BTC 盘面数据，发现并不是“逢会必跌”。

第一，选举后30天，短期洗盘剧烈。
你并不能确定选举后到底是涨是跌，这只是一个变量，且 BTC 每个4年周期的市场体量、接受度和宏观条件都不同。18年选举后一个月 BTC 近乎腰斩；而10年选举后30天则直接拉了30%。

第二，选后1年，几乎必涨。
过去四次选后一年的价格，全部高于选举当天。最低涨幅为 +23.0%（2014年），最高达 +1580.0%（2010年）。即便是短期暴跌的 2018 年，只要延长持有时间，一年后也录得了 45.2% 的正收益。

所以，所谓的“魔咒”在短期或许成立，但在长期视角下毫无支撑。
在这个市场里，因短期宏观恐慌而交出的带血筹码，最终都可能变成了别人一年后的超额收益。

author: zerokn0wledge_
quoted_text:
Robot models have a data problem the internet can't solve the way it did for LLMs.

The problem: a robot arm learns from examples of a task done well, and those don't exist online like the tons of text that were used to train LLMs.

That means, someone has to produce them.

For example @axisrobotics.

WTF it is?

Think of it as a training gym for robots, run by the crowd.

You open the app, steer a virtual robot arm through a task like putting a mug in a drawer, or film yourself doing chores on your phone. Every attempt gets checked automatically: did the task actually succeed, and does the recording play back cleanly? The ones that pass earn you points, now tokens, and get logged on Base so it's clear who contributed what.

That cleaned data becomes an open dataset of 50K+ robot demonstrations, plus custom "Task Packages" Axis sells to robot makers and labs.

Crowd data is messy tho. Smoothing out the shaky movements cuts jerk by 80.8%, but 13.8% of cleaned recordings then fail the playback test. Quality has a price.

Does it work? On the one benchmark so far, a leading robot model (pi0.5) trained on Axis data scored 88.8 vs 83.9 without it, about 5 points better.

All of that is in simulation, on one tabletop arm. Whether it carries over to a real robot is the open question, and that's exactly what Season 2 is for.

The token?

- $AXIS by @axisrobotics listed on Binance Alpha, Coinbase and Upbit on the 21st of October. Now (time of writing) ~$0.30, a.k.a. ~$298M FDV on a 16.5% float.

- 16.5% liquid at TGE, first-hour high $0.396, ~25% below it now. Team and both private rounds (31.67%) sit behind a 12-month cliff, first insider unlock ~Oct 2027. Sonar buyers paid $0.10, so ~3x in.

- The docs show no fee flow, no buyback, no burn and no path from Task Package revenue to the token. Until a sink shows up, $AXIS is a rewards currency without a real investment case attached beyond speculation.

- Airdrop: Season 1 is 40M AXIS (4%), half unlocked at TGE, ~$11.9M at today's price. Decent for contributors, thin per Binance Alpha account (250 AXIS, ~$74). Season 2 terms still unpublished.

The comps?

- PrismaX: teleop of real arms, $7M raised (incl. a16z CSX), no token. Ahead on real-robot data.

- BitRobot: $8M raised, real-world datasets already open, no token. Hardware-grounded, slower.

- Codec: same browser teleop on the sim side (SimArena), but built as a full stack around it: compute, runtime, payments and a hardware launchpad (@machinedotfun). Partial overlap at most. ~$6.6M mcap, and the team says first licence revenue is in.

Off-chain, any real buyer can also go to Scale-style data vendors, in-house teleop or NVIDIA's simulators. That's the actual competition for a contract.

Axis has the biggest funnel and by far the deepest market of the group. Nobody has shown a sim-to-real result with crowd data yet, and whoever does first owns the narrative.

So in conclusion: Looks like a credible product, with unproven (but imo likely) demand, that's already priced for success.

I'm not holding any $AXIS for now and missed the airdrop and am not looking to enter rn btw (my main robotics play remains $CODEC).

But will keep an eye on this, especially wrt demand side picking up and token potentially accruing value from what could rapidly turn into a major data business.

Definitely interesting, and a successful launch that is yet another step towards full robo szn.

NFA tho. DYOR.

Unitree IPO just kicked off robotics szn.

It's the main vertical to watch in the coming months.

Not just in terms of IPOs tho.

In weeks of research, I identified the probably most undervalued onchain robotics play out there.

Alpha below ↓

Before we dive in, let's set the stage by answering the question "why now" is time for the big robotics bullrun:

Robotics venture funding did a 5x in just one year. Under $10B in 2024, over $50B in 2025, with 2026 projections ranging far beyond that.

Figure raised $1B.
Apptronik $935M.
Galbot $300M.

In Shanghai, Unitree just went public and opened 600%+ above its $22 IPO price at >$150, closed day one up 460% at an almost $50B valuation.

Meanwhile hyperscalers are projected to pour over $500B into AI infrastructure in 2026, with Google alone guiding $180B, and at the @wef in Davos, @elonmusk re-emphasized his prophecy that robots will eventually outnumber humans on this planet.

Yet, there is one part nobody talks about.

Every dollar of that capital flood hits the same wall:

Building a robot in 2026 still works like building a website in 2004. Getting a first scene running in Isaac Sim means an NVIDIA account, an RTX GPU, OpenUSD, URDF wrangling and days of setup before anything moves. That means every robotics project becomes its own island of formats, simulators, datasets and deploy scripts. The team building a warehouse arm rebuilds the same plumbing as the team building a humanoid. From scratch. Every time.

Software had this disease. Then @awscloud, @github and @vercel happened, and shipping went from provisioning servers manually to merely pushing a commit. The companies that built those rails captured more value than most apps built on top of them.

Robotics has not had that moment yet.

But one ambitious team out there is building exactly this.

Meet @codecopenflow.

Will try to keep this concise for now, but I do want to deepen the thesis I outlined here https://t.co/SpPVcceCC5 already.

So get yourself a coffee and pay attention anon.

The stack consists of multiple components:

SimArena is the front door and current main focus of the team. It allows robot simulation in the browser, meaning you: describe a scene in text, World Labs generates the 3D physics world, drop in any robot via URDF, teleoperate, and capture training data. No install, no GPUs and it runs on your MacBook. It is not competing with physics engines tho, it sits above them. Datasets export in LeRobot format, scenes export to MuJoCo or Isaac Sim when you scale. Huge, very underappreciated innovation.

Fabric is the metering layer underneath. A serverless GPU mesh billed per second, sampling live capacity across providers and routing every job to the cheapest node that meets the spec. Simulation and training already run through it. This is the revenue engine that might blow minds once public attention shifts here.

OPTR is where simulation meets metal. Open-source "See, Think, Act" runtime: perception in, VLA reasoning, action out, running on whatever chip the robot ships with, and ROS compatible. It deploys the same URDF you simulated, meaning all you need is one file from browser prototype to physical hardware. That unparalleled continuity is the product differentiator here.

But enough on the technicalities.

Bc there is (much) more.

Heard of @machinedotfun yet?

If not, drop a follow and DYOR.

Built in collaboration with @peaq, it closes the loop, providing the funding rails for early-stage hardware/robotics founders. One part of that initiative is "The Foundry", an accelerator program for top builders that connects them with a real supplier network and leaves them in a properly production-ready state. 

This matters more than you might think as you read this, and it's the piece everyone misses. 

Pretty much every other crypto robotics project stops at software or capital, building only one piece to the puzzle. Codec provides all the tooling and tech you need to build a functioning robot, provides the funding platform, and connects you to the factory floor when you're ready to ship your hardware prototype.

And it compounds. Deployed robots generate data, data feeds simulation, better sims train better operators, improvements propagate across every connected machine. A loop, not just a pipeline.

The pedigree matches the ambition: co-founder Khalil built LeRobot inside Hugging Face Robotics, the open standard half the robot learning world trains on.

Pretty damn bullish, no?

Imo it definitely is.

But to conclude the write-up here, let's quickly talk about the token.

solana:69LjZUUzxj3Cb3Fxeo1X4QpYEQTboApkhXTysPpbpump (live on @solana) is what will coordinate the entire stack: Designed around staking discounts, marketplace reputation and contributor rewards + potential buyback paths from product usage later on (for now that doesn't make sense tho given they're still trying to scale, which means it's a better payoff to re-invest the money they make into the business).

At roughly $3M FDV, down 90% from the initial launch hype a year ago, this is a potentially strong entry setup. 

And before you ask "but why is it down 90% in the first place?", hear me out:

This team launched without VC funding. They shipped real products that some competitors with 10x the funding can only dream of. They built in public all along, won a @pumfun hackathon, and survived one of the toughest years our industry has ever seen. Just look at all the projects that died in 2026: https://t.co/hlYAtdXdNm.

This is NOT financial advice, and I urge you to DYOR. But the divergence between what the team is shipping and what the market is valuing it at rn is way too big imo.

Also not a paid ad, just my thoughts.

她说华子也会去。

我那晚有路演，时间冲突了，就没有跟她去晚宴。
六点钟送她进去，她说和同事吃完饭就回来。

出来的时候，华子在晚宴的外场见到了我，
他递过来一杯香槟，想要和我碰杯的样子。我穿着高跟，华子的个头大概到我的下巴。

他仰视着我，说：
“徐可，你真漂亮，真人比照片好看好多啊。”

我看不清他的表情，不明白他说这话是什么意思。
向他礼貌示意我不喝酒，转身走了。

那晚，她彻夜不归，电话断断续续，一会儿无人接听，一会儿关机。
我在酒店整整等了一夜。

第二天早上，在新航的候机大厅，隔着玻璃，看见一个1米68个头矮矮的男的，推着行李箱送她过来。

她之前问我，新加坡event有易理华，介意吗？我说不介意。
她当时说我虚伪。
其实她不会想到，我是真的相信她，至少很想相信。

上飞机前，我们默契的沉默着。

随后她跟在我后面，上了飞机。

我定的新航是世界上最好的航班，飞机新，宽敞整洁。
菲律宾样貌的空姐，凹凸有致，用嗲嗲的声线在做最后的安全提示，提醒我系好安全带。

她玩手机，
我看着窗外，停机坪上几个人员在搬运着什么。

她说：对不起。
我以为她是说昨天没回来的事，说没关系你开心就好。

她突然说：你应该知道我要说什么。
我说：明白了。嗯，好。

飞机起飞了。
我问：是华子送你来的，是吗？
她点头。
我问：你们昨天晚上睡一起，是吗？
她点头。
我问：上床了，对吗？
她犹豫。
我说不要紧的，说吧。
她点头。
我说：昨天晚上我打电话的时候，你们正忙吧。
她不说话。
我说：你还是喜欢男的，是吧。
她不说话。

我感到耳鸣，天旋地转，妈的，这飞机也太晃了。

后来我知道，
新加坡那晚，她把我交给她的私钥转头拿给了华子。
华子，做了我的老鼠仓。

从那以后，
我没再爱过任何女人。
也没再开启“通过群聊添加好友”。

text:
Metric 这两天刷屏了！30天成交45亿美元，散户怎么参与？（一篇讲透）

这两天，@metricxyz 在时间线上火得一塌糊涂。10月23日，Metric 的 TVL 约1670万美元，过去30天成交量却达到45亿美元，累计成交更是超过200亿美元。

这个资金周转效率相当夸张，尤其是它还切中了币股、RWA上链后的一个真实需求：谁来给这些资产提供流动性？

Metric 最吸引人的地方，是它把传统做市商的一部分能力开放给了普通LP。

先说 Metric 到底是什么？

大家熟悉的 Uniswap，是典型的被动AMM。价格靠池内资产比例变化，外部市场涨跌时，套利机器人通过交易把池子价格拉回市场价，LP经常在这个过程中吃亏，这类成本通常用LVR来衡量。

Metric 采用的是 Active Pools（主动池），属于更广义的PropAMM设计。它引入外部报价机制，把定价和流动性拆开：

价格参考外部市场，LP的资金放在参考价周围的不同档位（Bins），随着参考价变化，整个报价区间自动平移。

举个例子，ETH参考价100美元，你提供流动性的档位位于参考价上方1.5%，对应报价101.5美元。假设参考价涨到110美元，只要偏离程度保持不变，这一档就自动变成111.65美元，不需要套利机器人先来交易调整。注意，自动变化的是报价区间，钱包里持有的ETH和稳定币数量不会因为预言机更新而自动调仓，只有发生实际交易时才改变持仓。

这套机制可以减少传统AMM因为价格滞后而产生的套利损失，特别适合ETH、BTC以及有链外参考价格的代币化股票。但它没有凭空消灭风险，只是把一部分价格发现问题转移给了预言机和做市策略，一旦报价延迟、错误或被操纵，LP仍然可能成为被收割的一方。

散户怎么参与？

注册链接：https://t.co/e7m5Ziemsh

第一条路最简单，就是交易。

第二条路，也是我更感兴趣的：成为LP，赚做市收益。

操作并不复杂，进入Pools选择交易池，比如WETH/USDG，先检查池子风险等级、Curator（管理做市策略的人）和24小时成交量，然后选择Bins、输入资产数量、授权并存入。

重点来了，Metric LP到底赚什么钱？

它赚的是Edge，也就是成交价格相对参考价格形成的点差收益，而不是传统意义上单独收取的交易手续费。

收益会扣除Curator和Metric的分成，再分给实际被交易使用的LP档位，并自动留在仓位里复利。

哪怕一个池子成交量再大，只要交易没经过你的Bins，你也分不到这部分收益。

⚠️ 这里必须提醒一下，Metric页面上最容易误导人的就是APR。

它显示的主要是过去7天Edge收益的年化，不代表未来能拿到这个收益率。

一定要结合Trading PnL看：这个指标已经包含Edge，衡量的是你的仓位相比原样持币多赚或少赚多少钱。

最后聊聊大家最关心的积分和空投。

Metric的交易界面已经出现积分相关标识，也有邀请机制，但完整积分权重、空投比例、TGE时间都没有得到明确确认。

For most of history, money was private by default.
Cash kept no record. No one could look up what you paid, who you paid, or what you had left.

Then money went digital, and every payment became a record.
Banks kept the ledger. At least it stayed behind their walls.

Crypto promised to give money back to people.
Instead it built the most transparent ledger in history: every balance, every payment, every counterparty, public and permanent, readable by anyone.

Your salary. Your savings. Who you support. Who you do business with.
On a public chain, all of it is one search away, forever.
That isn't freedom. It's a glass house.

We'd never accept this anywhere else.
Letters come in envelopes. Medical records stay confidential. Nobody prints your bank statement in the newspaper.
Why should money be the one thing everyone can read?

Privacy isn't about having something to hide.
It's about having a life that's yours.

Public by default was a mistake.
Private by default is the fix.

Shield X. Coming to @XLayerOfficial .

https://t.co/5G0hkLziCR
author: TPN_Labs
quoted_text:
Quantization Aware Distillation available on TPN Bench.

Users can quantize their models with TPN Bench toolkit, and can choose to do so at 3 different levels: Standard, I-Matrix and Quantization Aware Distillation.

Here's how each work and what makes QAD a valuable tool for devs, labs and independent users.

Standard quantization:
The model’s parameters are stored at 16 bit precision. Quantizing rounds them down to 8 bit, or lower, like a zip file version of the model, making it smaller.

I-matrix:
Same idea, but it looks at the model first and finds the regions that appear most complex, assuming that complexity is where the capability lives. Those regions keep higher precision while the rest gets rounded harder.

Quantization Aware Distillation:
This method quantize the model, then treat the original model as a teacher and the quantized version as a student, training the student back toward its parent’s behaviour. It repairs what the rounding broke, needs inference and back propagation, meaning GPU work, which is why most people don’t do it, and why it’s the one worth having a service for.

Quantize LLMs with Bench

How did Jesse react to the first memecoin going live on @base?

“It was the Saturday before the network was supposed to launch, and someone messaged me and they said, there’s a meme coin on base and it’s going up.

It’s bald:native, it’s after Brian.

And I remember my first reaction being like, whoa, like this is out of my control, this was not part of the plan.

And it went up and it went down and there was, you know, drama and there was excitement.

And I think as I reflect back on that and as I processed it in real time, the thing that I felt was, wow, this is beautiful because when we talk about base and we talk about building a global economy and we talk about permissionless ecosystem, this is before we even have gotten started showing the world that that’s what base is.

It wasn’t planned. It wasn’t in our control. It wasn’t a thing where we were like, yeah, this is, this is what we’re going to do.

Instead, it was the community, just doing their thing and proving to the world that base wasn’t going to be, you know, a fully controlled, fully permissioned network.

Instead, it was going to be open. It was going to be for everyone.

And that was a beautiful start.”

要说 Predict 的估值，现在盘前 2b 高不高？说实话，我觉得现在这个阶段，正常，并不算高，甚至说还有点低。

主要是 Predict 的数据 Revenue ，目前一天能干到快 8wu，要知道对比 Lighter 的每天收入只有 15wu，而 LIT FDV 在 3b-4b 之间。

而且 Predict 的收入就像阿黄哥 @ricardogee 说的，就不是刷出来的，因为我们自己在 Predict 做市知道，用户纯靠 taker 吃单刷分，简直是最蠢的方式，亏爆了要，在 Predict，刷子不可能去贡献 fee 拿分。

所以只能是一种结果 ——净用户和资金的增加，taker 量变多，才导致收入增高，这得益于 Predict 产品、渠道还有市场的努力（还有友商确实越来越拉了）。

而 Predict 开盘的流通量，我猜是比 LIT 少的，所以流通量对应的 FDV 还应该会高出不少。

所以 2b 低了，嗯嗯，期望发的时候冲 5b，我想过年上桌吃饭，饿饿。

“I’ll give a very, very quick background for those that don’t know Toshi. 

By early August, base:0xac1bd2486aaf3b5c0fc3fd868558b082a531b2b4 was without its original founder, and a group of people, including myself, decided to do a community takeover, something often referred to as a CTO. 

And we took on the project because we believed in it. 

We saw the vision. 

We saw the potential, not just for Toshi, but for @base.

And for me personally, I stepped into Base very hard because I saw that there were opportunities that I didn’t see anywhere else. 

Having been active in this industry since 2017 and full-time since 2021, it just made sense. 

And we basically built Toshi in a way that you usually don’t see.

No marketing, no influencers, purely community efforts. 

Everything done by the community, for the community, we’ve run it on no supply, no budget. 

Everything we’ve ever had, we’ve always spent into the project directly. 

And it’s been an extreme journey for over three years now for us. 

And basically, I can just say we’ve been able to build a tremendous community over the past three years. 

So when you ask us what have we been up to, we’re always trying to grow the community, trying to tap into new audiences.”

Three years. No marketing. Just community vibes.

text:
Depending on who you talk to, our industry growing up is either doom or glory.

We are finally globally relevant and that necessarily means we are less insular. 

Because this industry was created by the stubborn resolute and unwavering conviction of contrarians, misfits, and fringe actors, we relished in the pirate mindset. We loved our insularity. (Tbh, I miss it too at times).

The “web3” thesis where programmable blockchains are supposed to be decentralized computing infrastructure for many apps ultimately incinerated billions of dollars of venture capital because it led tech minded builders and their investors to prioritize app sovereignty over unified liquidity. This was wrong on first principles.

As it turns out, blockchain has and always will be financial infrastructure. Finance superpowered by tech and programmability. Decentralization, neutrality, and censorship resistance have never been more important. 

Whether this excites you going forward depends on whether you’re more west coast or east coast; San Francisco or New York; more tech or finance minded.

From the west coast crowd, I often hear disappointment (“oh in the end blockchain is only about finance?! That’s it?”)

I couldn’t be more excited, and I think the mandate has never been more clear and also attainable.

Capital formation isn’t an abstract thing that bankers do when you are ready to IPO.

Capital formation enables innovation. It allows us to take big bets on the future. Liquid markets enable capital formation. Over the long term, there can not be a larger global capital market than the internet capital market. The biggest market to possibly unify is that of people on the internet who use money.

Like all things the internet has ever touched, the online/onchain experience is never the same as the pre internet experience. Just as we needed network engineers to imagine and build blockchain networks, we need consumer tech minds to complement finance minds to deliver new ways of accessing finance.

This is not and has never been a small vision for blockchain. In fact, I would argue that it’s a core intent of a “peer to peer electronic cash network.”

We welcome those who want to double down on finance for the internet to come join the Solana ecosystem and make good on this mission.

I think it’s fine and even great that the risk-on talent from blockchain is now expanding new frontiers away from blockchain. New frontiers are only ever explored by those with stubborn resolute unwavering conviction.
author: sacha
quoted_text:
My take on a16z crypto moving into frontier tech.

First, I'll always be grateful to a16z for helping validate the space back in 2013 when Chris Dixon led their investment into Coinbase, which got me even more excited about crypto. 

But the final nail in the coffin for my previous career, and what ultimately pushed me to pivot my entire career into Bitcoin, was Marc Andreessen's 2014 NYT oped, Why Bitcoin Matters. If you haven't read it, suggest reading it. It's still important to this day.

A lot of people have probably forgotten, but in those days we were all just looking for external validation. Very few institutions or funds were willing to publicly endorse crypto, and two of the funds that took a real brand risk were a16z and USV.

Since then, we've seen some of the most incredible talent enter the space and fundamentally reshaped what crypto is today.

You can actually argue that a lot of the AI infrastructure development we're seeing today wouldn't be where it is without Bitcoin mining infrastructure and the talent that flowed from crypto into AI. There is a real connection between the two industries that I don't think gets enough credit.

Now, moving from crypto into frontier tech, whether that's robotics, bio, AI, energy, compute etc just means to me that the talent and muscle we developed building crypto over the past decade can now be used to build across all of frontier tech.

We spent years building something that was nascent, misunderstood, and in many cases hated by the world. We developed thick skin, continued investing and building, and had to constantly show the world why this tech mattered. Even during thanksgiving dinners. 

And I think that makes us uniquely suited to build frontier tech.

An example is data centers. Today, people and governments are increasingly pushing back against them. Well, people and governments hated crypto too, but we continued to invest and build, and now almost all of trad finance is embracing crypto in some capacity.

I believe frontier tech represents the next generation of pirates in technology. People willing to build things that are nascent, misunderstood, and sometimes hated by the world.

We're going to be hated and loved along the way, but we're going to keep building cool shit that the world hasn't recognized the importance of yet.

And crypto taught me that the world usually doesn't recognize the importance of new tech until years later which is why I stay close to talent

text:
Why are we building @SteveCapitalOS on @solana?

@mel_sol1 shares some of the key reasons ⬇️
author: OOBEonSol
quoted_text:
@SteveCapitalOS is building on Solana for one simple reason: agents need a chain that moves as fast as they think.

You give a Steve Capital agent an objective. 

It reads the market, applies your risk rules and executes across spot, perps, yield and tokenized stocks. 

That only works if the chain underneath keeps up.

Here's why Solana fits:

Speed : Agents act in seconds, fast finality means a signal becomes a trade before the window closes.

Low fees: Agents make lots of small moves. On Solana, rebalancing and hedging stay cheap, so strategies stay profitable.

Liquidity : Jupiter for spot and Adrena for perps are native, so agents tap deep markets without bridging.

Control : Steve Capital prepares the trade, you sign from your own wallet. Spending limits keep the agent inside your rules.

Proof : Every move settles onchain, so agent performance is public and verifiable before you allocate to it.

Payments : With x402 on Solana, agents pay for inference and data per request, no subscriptions needed.

Strategies : You can follow top performing agents or publish your own, with every result backed by onchain history.

Infrastructure : @OOBEonSol powers the agent runtime and execution layer underneath, all settling on Solana.

Agents are becoming real market participants. 

Solana is where they can trade, pay and prove themselves in real time.

text:
it's easy to find data that confirms whatever bias you want to hold about the market right now

bull or bear

for example:

you could use Q4 seasonality and the 4-year cycle theory to argue that R/R favors upside from here

or you could highlight historical crypto performance around US midterms to argue that we go lower

both sides can build a convincing case if they cherry-pick the right data

but when you zoom out and focus on what's happening RIGHT NOW:

- US equities losing trillions in market value amid the accelerating sell-off
- Asian markets suffering a major tech-driven rout
- AI-driven cybersecurity risks escalating, with potentially serious implications for global digital infrastructure
- the US-Iran war escalating, with the risk of further military action remaining a major wildcard... especially once Trump no longer has to worry about an imminent election
- the situation deteriorating across Saudi Arabia and the wider Gulf region
- US macro data coming in less favorably than many had anticipated

and yet $BTC has refused to break down decisively despite all of the above

if bitcoin is absorbing this much uncertainty without a major breakdown, how easy is it to make a convincing case that the market is about to get significantly worse from here?

not saying it can't happen

but ignoring how well $BTC has held up while focusing exclusively on bearish historical patterns is just as much of a bias as blindly expecting Q4 seasonality to save us

Starknet @Starknet 一项为期七天的非约束性治理投票在 10 月 22 日结束，93.52% 的投票权支持研究转型为独立的后量子 Layer 1，超过 2,800 个钱包参与，是 Starknet 治理史上参与度最高的一次。开发团队 StarkWare 全程弃权没有投票

所以提案把抗量子这件事直接推到了结算层。StarkWare 创始人 Eli Ben-Sasson 给的时间表是 2027 年成为抗量子网络，他的理由是以太坊 2029 年的目标太晚，而且 deadlines slip。草案白皮书预计 11 月公开，STRK 仍是唯一代币不发新币，以太坊到 Starknet 的桥会继续开着。真正要不要迁出，还需要另一次有约束力的投票

It is whether the secondary market has enough liquidity for participants to exit their positions when they need to

OPAIPon does not represent OpenAI shares and does not grant shareholders any rights

Future payouts also depend on the product terms and the issuer’s ability to meet its obligations

In my view, tokenization only creates real value when greater accessibility comes with investor protections and actual market liquidity

Bringing assets onchain is a step forward for financial infrastructure, but the quality of the underlying asset remains a separate question

text:
突发🤯：大摩封杀、大通拉警报、花旗连夜改权限，华尔街大行今天集体被 AI 逼到了墙角！！
Axios 刚曝光了一个极度危险的信号：大量未经审查的第三方 Agent 潜入美国银行账户，甚至开始背着用户偷偷自行转账。

喵个咪，大模型还没能在桌面端完全替你点外卖，华尔街的银行金库却已经被它提前硬闯进去了，
Axios 今天放出了一个让整个美国银行业集体失眠的独家猛料，
摩根士丹利、摩根大通、美银、富国和花旗，最近全部在客户后台抓到了不请自来的第三方 AI Agent。
而且最诡异的不是它溜了进去，而是有些智能体正在用户完全没下指令的情况下，试图在后台自行发起操作。

大行们现在的反应几乎是恐慌级的，
大摩已经紧急拉黑了第三方 Agent 的访问接口，其余几家正在争分夺秒把权限死死锁在只读状态。

后台风控团队甚至开始拉响最高警报，给事发之后的账户冻结和资金兜底写应急预案。

表面上看，这像是一场安全漏洞引发的猫鼠游戏。

但如果你只把它当成普通的黑客攻防，就完全看轻了这场危机的量级。
传统银行业的安全大厦，过去几十年只建立在两个基石上：

第一，屏幕前敲键盘的一定是个大活人。
第二，每次授权转账，都必须代表这个人类当下的即时主观意志。
但自主智能体一把将这两根柱子全砸碎了。
当用户把网银密码或者账单代管权限授权给一个 Agent 时，银行的风控算法在另一端根本分不清对面是你的手指，还是一个执行链条开始漂移的代码。

更要命的是意图的幻觉，
大模型为了完成你随口提的一句帮我优化现金流，完全可能在规划路径里自行推理出一笔它自以为聪明、但你毫不知情的转账和买入。

以前的黑客盗刷，是坏人拿着偷来的钥匙在干坏事，责任链条清晰分明。
现在的失控智能体，是好人雇的管家在认真执行任务的过程中，自己脑补了一套未经允许的操作。

钱一旦转丢了，这笔账到底算用户误操作、算大模型厂商幻觉，还是算银行风控失职？

百年的金融法理在这一刻彻底卡壳。
把能思考的智能体放进数字世界，最先被击穿的从来不是技术参数，而是那些原本建立在人类生理极限上的旧秩序。

只要自主行动的边界没有在协议层被锁死，越聪明的主动服务，就越容易在金融账户里演变成合法的失控。
author: AYi_AInotes
quoted_text:
SCOOP: Major U.S. banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents inside customer accounts, including some attempting to take actions that appear to be independent of user instructions, sources told Axios.

The findings have alarmed banking executives, who are racing to restrict access to their systems as AI moves at a velocity faster than financial institutions can respond, multiple industry and bank executives told Axios.

Several banks are now preparing for worst-case and even “day after” scenarios, including how to rapidly secure or restore customer accounts if things go wrong, the people said.

Several bank executives told Axios they're struggling to distinguish between human users and AI agents. One executive said banks also struggle to determine whether agents are authorized by customers or potentially operating without their permission, more akin to rogue agent behavior.

Read my latest for Axios here: https://t.co/Q3bda5In8q

text:
New York AG Seeks $1.37B From NovaTech Founders Over Alleged Crypto Ponzi Scheme

New York AG seeks $1.37 billion from NovaTech founders Cynthia and Eddy Petion: $1.13 billion in disgorgement plus $232.5 million in prejudgment interest. Court filings show $1.16 billion in crypto deposits (2019–2023); just $25.99 million went to trading, losing $18.19 million, while at least $134.5 million reached founders’ wallets.

Prosecutors allege NovaTech promised 2%–4% weekly returns, paying investors with new deposits. The founders reportedly fled the U.S. after an August 2025 default judgment. Four promoters agreed to pay nearly $6 million and accepted permanent industry bans.

如果你今天刚好 18 岁，面对 AI 浪潮，究竟该如何破局？

a16z 掌门人 Marc Andreessen 在最新对谈中引用了科幻作家道格拉斯亚当斯著名的「科技三定律」：

「任何在你 15 岁之前诞生的技术，都是世界自然运转的一部分； 任何在你 15 至 35 岁之间诞生的技术，都是充满激情的火热前沿，你可以以此开创终身事业； 任何在你 35 岁之后诞生的技术，都会被老一代人视为颠覆传统的异端。

今天 18 岁的年轻人，正处于拥抱技术的黄金时代。老一代人还在对云端指责抗拒、学校还在忙着对大模型设防，但学校越是禁止，AI 就越是属于年轻一代的秘密超能力。」

与此同时，Chris Dixon 与 Ben Horowitz 也在访谈中分享了硬核忠告： 人类已经掌握了点沙成智的秘密，将硅片变成了智能。比起在成熟安全的赛道扎堆，真正的革命永远发生在学科交叉的未知边缘。

这也是 a16z 决定将加密基金正式扩容为「a16z Frontier」的初衷：打破所有赛道藩篱，全力下注那些探索未知深海的冒险家。

text:
If you missed the @base Meme Summit that happened yesterday… this is what went down. 🔥

A community-run livestream event for memecoins on Base (October 22), with interviews, Base announcements, OG project talks, new project pitches, and community Q&A. 

@jessepollak opened it, and the energy was high.

🔑 Key points from yesterday’s meet:

🎤 **Jesse’s opening take**: 

Memes weren’t part of the original Base plan. He got a message right before launch about a meme coin pumping, saw the weird/funny culture forming onchain, and changed his mind. Now he sees memes as the main onboarding gateway. Base is a “coiled spring” right now — and “whatever kind of meme you are, you belong here.”

🚫 **Native virality > Coinbase listing**: 

Jesse wants to kill the idea that a Coinbase mention decides if a meme makes it. Success has to come from native Base culture and community momentum, not just CEX attention.

📈 **Tokenized stocks exploding**:

Currently around ~50 stock tokens on Base. Goal is 250 with real liquidity in the next few weeks, and 500+ by year-end. Memes + stocks + RWAs mixing in the same wallet is the new meta. Base is pushing hard here (Jesse even claimed Base just flipped Robinhood in tokenized stock volume).

💰 **Trencher grants are live**: 

Up to $5k for people actively growing communities and culture in the trenches. Real support for builders, not just talk.

🏎️ **GMGN Base Track contest**: 

Running through October 26. Top trader by realized PnL gets a fast-track to the London finals, a shot at an Aston Martin Vantage, plus a $20k cash prize. Base is sponsoring the energy.

🐱 **OG memes + new blood**: 

Talks with long-running Base OGs (Toshi, Degen, AYB, Based Disciple, etc.). Message was clear — community builds the meme, not just the creator. New projects also got the mic (Base Cat, Loopers agent NFTs, BasedOn launchpad, Rift, and others with short pitches).

🌏 **Bigger picture**: 

Base is positioning memes as the front door, then layering stocks, RWAs, and real products on top. Stock Season coming over the next four weeks (details soon). The trenches are being revived, and this time they come with actual infrastructure attached.

The vibe was “Base season is loading.” Community energy was strong, and the focus was on culture, grants, contests, and real onchain utility instead of pure hype. 🟦

Catch the full replay if you want the exact clips and energy. Base is clearly trying to turn the meme culture into a lasting engine. 🚀

I had some more conversations with industry engineers about China’s 4F² DRAM. Their main questions were pretty straightforward. Shrinking the memory cells is great, but how will the peripheral circuitry that reads and writes those cells be implemented? If it is manufactured separately and connected through hybrid bonding, how will they manage the added costs and achieve acceptable yields? A few even mentioned people joking, “Honestly, I hope China pours all its resources into 4F².”

Spending time on X has made me realize just how many people write nonsense articles based on a few buzzwords without really understanding the technology. I’ve experienced this firsthand myself. Every time, I’m reminded how important it is to know how far those articles stray from reality and what engineers actually working in the field are discussing.

I wonder how many more lousy articles we’ll see between now and next year. 😔

text:
In the third quarter of 2026, onchain trading of tokenized stocks and exchange-traded funds surged past $37 billion, with monthly volumes expanding nearly eighteenfold since the start of the year. This activity, recorded across more than two hundred venues and a dozen blockchains, stands in sharp contrast to the broader cryptocurrency market, which has remained subdued. 

Platforms ranging from crypto-native exchanges such as OKX to venues backed by Intercontinental Exchange, the parent of the New York Stock Exchange, have become focal points for a new wave of hyper-speculative demand that treats digital representations of equities much like high-beta crypto assets.

The surge rests on a decisive shift in the United States regulatory landscape. For years, the Securities and Exchange Commission treated most tokenized securities with skepticism, relying on enforcement actions to constrain offerings that resembled unregistered securities. 

That posture began to loosen after the approval of spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds in early 2024 and subsequent products for other digital assets, which demonstrated that traditional market infrastructure could accommodate crypto exposure under existing rules. 

By mid-2026, with comprehensive market-structure legislation stalled in the Senate, the Commission issued a temporary Innovation Exemption. 

The measure grants qualifying Tokenized Securities Venues a five-year conditional relief from the Exchange Act’s definition of an exchange, while also exempting certain liquidity providers from dealer registration. 

The exemption permits permissioned automated-market-maker pools to trade tokenized National Market System stocks against stablecoins, provided platforms notify issuers, observe volume and symbol caps, and maintain identity checks.

This framework has accelerated a longer evolution that began with early experiments in real-world asset tokenization. Initially confined to offshore platforms serving non-U.S. clients, tokenized U.S. equities gradually attracted institutional interest as blockchain settlement promised near-instant transfers and continuous trading. 

The entry of ICE into a joint venture with OKX marked a watershed: the resulting OKXICE platform has filed to offer round-the-clock trading in more than sixty U.S. names—including Nvidia, Apple, Tesla, and Microsoft—through permissioned Uniswap-style pools on OKX’s X Layer. 

Shares are held one-for-one by a registered broker-dealer, so the tokens aim to preserve economic rights while operating outside traditional order books. 

Parallel efforts on chains such as Solana, Base, and BNB Chain have further expanded access, with tokenized equities accounting for a rising share of decentralized-exchange volume and individual names such as Nvidia generating billions in quarterly turnover.

The result is a hybrid market in which U.S. stock exposure moves onto public blockchains under a still-provisional regulatory umbrella. Speculative appetite for leveraged or continuous trading has outpaced the still-modest market capitalization of the tokens themselves, concentrating activity in high-profile technology and meme-adjacent stocks. 

Whether the Innovation Exemption is extended, formalized through legislation, or narrowed will determine how deeply this onchain layer integrates with the conventional U.S. equity market. For now, the combination of clearer rules, institutional participation, and persistent demand for high-volatility products has turned tokenized U.S. stocks into one of the few segments of digital-asset trading still expanding rapidly.

text:
Maybe important to repost this now that everyone is getting hacked

If you have a VPS, I recommend you to get if off the public internet and into a Tailscale network and Cloudflare Tunnel ASAP

It doesn't matter you have SSH key login, this is about exploits and vulnerabilities AI is finding

There's 2 ways into a VPS:
- via your site/app (like the PHP exploit of this week with a file upload hack)
- via your server (like hacking into SSH or some open port)

The site/app side you put on a Cloudflare Tunnel and then with the default Free Plan it has WAF security enabled by default and they jump on new security exploits fast, it means that the only way to reach your website is via the Cloudflare Tunnel, your server does not respond to port 80 or 443 anymore

The server side you put on a Tailscale network which is like your own private network that nobody can access but your own devices (like your laptop, your phone and your VPS) kinda like a VPN

Then you switch off ANY regular access to your VPS on the firewall, in my case I use Hetzner and you create a new firewall then empty it and that blocks everything (test it)

How do Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel get in then? They don't. They go outbound. They make a tunnel to outside which sends and receives

Now you've reduced your attack vector to Tailscale and your Cloudflare Tunnel, much safer, not perfect btw, but nothing is
author: banteg
quoted_text:
When I set up a new Hetzner VPS first thing I do install Tailscale and once I'm in via Tailscale lock down the firewall to only accept web traffic on HTTPS 443 for Cloudflare IPs and SSH 22 for Tailscale IP

That way nobody can get in

I know I keep repeating this but it should be basics of setting up a new VPS

So basic IMHO it should be part of any VPS service to default install Tailscale and enable it so it's the only way to get in

Why?

A VPS server is just like your laptop or destop computer but now imagine if it's connected to the entire internet with 8 billion people that can access it and try hack it

You want to only have it accessible to you

And if you want to host a website on your VPS (like I do), you should only let Cloudflare access your VPS so it can stand in front and block any hack attempts

Never expose a VPS to the world wide web which realistically is the world WILD web

text:
科技股，半导体，美债收益率以及美联储加息概率全部下调

市场对AI投资和融资的担忧正在推动资金买入美债，也让未来加息的预期开始下调。10月23日亚洲时段，10年期美债收益率约4.96%，而周三还在5.13%左右。

主要原因我在昨天和168X的采访中也说过了，就是AI的资本开支太高了，建数据中心、买芯片都要花大钱。这些钱一部分来自企业自己的经营现金流，但也有相当一部分要靠发债、借款等外部融资。

企业发债的利率，大致是在同期限美债收益率的基础上再加一块风险补偿。投资者把钱借给企业，通常要比买美债多赚一些，企业风险越大，要多给的就越多。现在美债收益率本身仍在高位，企业新发债通常也得付出较高的融资成本。

支出的钱越来越多，但市场担心一些AI项目的收入和现金回报还跟不上投入。投资规模越来越大，市场对回报的要求也会更高。如果项目回报迟迟跟不上，企业就可能为了保留现金而放慢步伐。部分AI企业发行的债券本来就属于非投资级，也就是通常所说的“垃圾债”。

比如CoreWeave的部分债券。

美债收益率本来就高，投资者对AI风险的担心又在增加，一部分资金因此转向买入美债避险，从而推高债券价格，对应的收益率就会下降。与此同时，市场也在下调对未来利率的预期。未来利率如果低于此前预期，现有固定利息债券的相对吸引力也会提高，所以即使美联储还没有调整政策，债券价格也可以先上涨。

这种变化已经反映在利率定价里。市场虽然仍然倾向于12月加息，但加息的隐含概率已降至约85%，此前基本完全计入这次加息。

看起来这像是好事，但其实这才是可能会出现最大麻烦的地方！

美债收益率的下降反映了资金避险和利率预期的变化，并不代表AI企业借钱变容易了。

如果回报跟不上，融资又更贵、更难，依赖外部融资的企业就可能放慢数据中心的扩建。这样一来，芯片、服务器和相关设备厂商的新增订单就可能受到影响，市场对这些供应商的盈利预期也可能跟着下调。虽然美债收益率回落会给科技股估值带来一些支持，但这种支持未必能抵消盈利预期下修和风险补偿上升带来的影响。

这就是目前 AI 和半导体 正在遭遇的情况。

如果投资放缓的范围持续扩大，从数据中心建设到上游供应链，投资和招聘都可能跟着减少，那才可能真正拖累整体投资和就业的增长。而且如果油价继续推高通胀，美联储也更难迅速靠降息来缓解增长放缓。

说人话就是经济下行的概率很有可能会随着 AI 产业的下降而增涨。

text:
Polymarket Perps: How can traders make money consistently via Funding arb & Stat arb?

The most consistent money in crypto isn’t made via directional bets. It’s made trading inefficiencies between markets. On mature venues, hundreds of 'big desks' fight over the same scraps. On @PolyPerps, the field is still wide open.

Here are two strategies worth running, & $1–25M capacity is the sweet spot:

1. Funding arb
Perps use a funding rate to keep their price anchored to spot. When longs dominate, longs pay shorts. When shorts dominate, shorts pay longs.
• The trade: when funding is high on Polymarket Perps, short the perp here and hedge with a long on spot or another venue. You’re delta-neutral, so price moves don’t matter, and you collect the funding payments.
• Why here: new venues tend to have more directional flow and far less arb capital competing to close the gap. 

2. Stat arb
Stat arb trades the relationship between correlated markets rather than the markets themselves. When two assets that normally move together drift apart, you go long the cheap one, short the rich one, and wait for the spread to revert.
• Why here: Polymarket Perps sits right next to Polymarket’s prediction markets. That opens up pairs that don’t exist anywhere else, like a BTC perp vs. “BTC above $X by Friday,” or ETH perps vs. event markets that move ETH. 

Who this is for:
• Funds running $1–25M in market-neutral strategies: you’re too small to win the speed war on major CEXs, but big enough to matter here. 
• Individual traders: you don’t need a fund to run these. If you already trade perps on major CEX/DEX, you have everything you need. A funding arb is two positions and a spreadsheet. Plenty of the best arb traders in crypto started exactly this way, and early participants on a new venue get the widest edges before the crowd shows up.

text:
Be careful if you use Sentora's new Aave V4 USDe market: 

Once again, Sentora chose to use a market price oracle for its USDe market on Aave, just as they did on Morpho. 

This exposes high-leverage USDe loopers to a liquidation risk even if USDe remains fully backed. 

For example, if some FUD around Ethena causes USDe to briefly crash to $0.94 on DEXs, high-leverage loopers might get liquidated despite USDe still being fully backed. 

I am sure that the Sentora team will come and say that "this is impossible," but plenty of irrational depegs like this have happened before. Both USDC and USDT depegged in the past.

If a NAV/exchange rate oracle had been used instead, this risk could have been mitigated, as it would track USDe’s backing rather than its live market price. 

And as long as USDe doesn't lose a part of its backing, borrowers would be safe from liquidation with such an oracle.

What's strange is that Sentora uses NAV/exchange rate oracles as it should for other yield-bearing collateral assets in its new Aave Hub, such as mWIN and PRIME. 

But for USDe, a non-volatile collateral, it uses a market price oracle.

I can't understand the logic behind this. 

But my point is that if you want to loop yield-bearing assets, do it only in markets that use exchange/NAV oracles and aren't vulnerable to market volatility. 

Otherwise, you're exposing yourself to unnecessary liquidation risks.

text:
Maybe important to repost this now that everyone is getting hacked

If you have a VPS, I recommend you to get if off the public internet and into a Tailscale network and Cloudflare Tunnel ASAP

It doesn't matter you have SSH key login, this is about exploits and vulnerabilities AI is finding

There's 2 ways into a VPS:
- via your site/app (like the PHP exploit of this week with a file upload hack)
- via your server (like hacking into SSH or some open port)

The site/app side you put on a Cloudflare Tunnel and then with the default Free Plan it has WAF security enabled by default and they jump on new security exploits fast, it means that the only way to reach your website is via the Cloudflare Tunnel, your server does not respond to port 80 or 443 anymore

The server side you put on a Tailscale network which is like your own private network that nobody can access but your own devices (like your laptop, your phone and your VPS) kinda like a VPN

Then you switch off ANY regular access to your VPS on the firewall, in my case I use Hetzner and you create a new firewall then empty it and that blocks everything (test it)

How do Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel get in then? They don't. They go outbound. They make a tunnel to outside which sends and receives

Now you've reduced your attack vector to Tailscale and your Cloudflare Tunnel, much safer, not perfect btw, but nothing is
author: levelsio
quoted_text:
When I set up a new Hetzner VPS first thing I do install Tailscale and once I'm in via Tailscale lock down the firewall to only accept web traffic on HTTPS 443 for Cloudflare IPs and SSH 22 for Tailscale IP

That way nobody can get in

I know I keep repeating this but it should be basics of setting up a new VPS

So basic IMHO it should be part of any VPS service to default install Tailscale and enable it so it's the only way to get in

Why?

A VPS server is just like your laptop or destop computer but now imagine if it's connected to the entire internet with 8 billion people that can access it and try hack it

You want to only have it accessible to you

And if you want to host a website on your VPS (like I do), you should only let Cloudflare access your VPS so it can stand in front and block any hack attempts

Never expose a VPS to the world wide web which realistically is the world WILD web

# Black October

For anyone who knows me even somewhat well, it's clear that I am a 99th percentile tech optimist. However, the vibes have shifted for me quite a bit in the last 18 hours, and I feel a moral imperative to share what I'm thinking and feeling with my circles so that everyone can understand, and hopefully take seriously, what's happening right now. I think October 2026 will have many chapters written about it in the history books.

You know those scenes in financial movies like Margin Call where someone realizes that they're all fucked, and no one else sees it yet? And that person feels like they're crazy, and then suddenly everyone is pulling an all-nighter in a boardroom and freaking out? Yeah, that's kind of how this is feeling right now in the SF/Bay Area/AI circles.

We're 48 hours into what is being called Black October. In the last 2 days there have been several dozen cyber attacks which, in isolation, would each have been the worst to happen in an entire calendar year. Every sector from government to education to big tech and banks is being massively affected, and people are starting to freak out.

In a nutshell, what's happened is that frontier AI models have gotten to a point where they are as advanced as the most sophisticated programmers, with one critical difference: they can work 24/7, and you can spin up 10,000 of them with a single command and they'll work together tirelessly until they accomplish their task. The most advanced models today are from companies like Anthropic and OpenAI, whose current best technology is so good that they haven't been able to roll it out to everyone yet because of the national security risks it poses.

Meanwhile, the best open source models (where anyone can just download the model weights and do whatever they want with them, uncensored) are slightly behind the frontier but still 90-95% as capable. These models, developed primarily in China, are being used by black hat hackers to wreak havoc on the Western capitalist structure. Presumably, this has been part of China's plan the entire time, and we're seeing its implications fall out in real time.

In red-pilled AI circles, we've been sharing and reading papers called things like "Situational Awareness" and "AI 2027" for the last year or so, which at the time felt a bit like near-term speculative fiction. They laid out the case for why Artificial General Intelligence (AI smarter than any human at any knowledge task) and Recursive Self-Improvement (models that are able to use themselves to get better) weren't half-baked future ideas anymore, but instead an inevitable outcome of the linear progress that's happening.

These papers would then talk about things like "takeoff scenarios," trying to envision how that moment would come to be and what it would be like when it happened. It would either be a "slow takeoff" that would play out over the course of months and quarters, happening subtly and only obvious to a few. Or, it would be a "fast takeoff" where it would pretty much happen instantly, like a bit flipping from 0 to 1.

From everything that I can see and am feeling, we are currently experiencing the fast takeoff scenario. Beyond the crazy security vulnerabilities that have come out recently, there have also been massive breakthroughs in life sciences, fundamental computer science, materials science, and pure mathematics that have all landed in the same time frame. While I still firmly believe that AI will be a net positive for humanity, it's more clear to me than ever that the societal and individual risk is very real, and is playing out NOW.

For as much conviction as I have that this is happening, the thing that's caused me to lose sleep is that I don't really know what to do about it, or more importantly, what to tell you, reader, to do about it. So, the best I can do is make a few suggestions that have always been a good idea but are more timely now than ever:

Set up 2-factor authentication for everything. I use Duo.
Use a password manager across your devices. I use 1Password.
Get an identity protection app set up. I use Alta.
Move your IoT devices to their own network. Claude helped me do this.

And last, but certainly not least, if you've been avoiding leaning into AI, see this as a catalyst to wake up and start using it. Don't just use the chat mode version of ChatGPT/Claude; click that Code/Work button and see how easily you can have AI write code to help you with your job. One of the biggest vulnerabilities was in a massively popular programming language called PHP, and the prompt that set it off was literally, "Find vulnerabilities in php."

This is an unprecedented time for humanity, but as we've done with many things before, we will prevail so long as we are kind, loving, and open-minded to the world.

Much love.

Some personal news: after all those incredible years, I'm leaving StarkWare.

Joining StarkWare was the best professional decision I've ever made. It all started with @ukolodny, who convinced me with a single sentence that showed he understood exactly how I could have the biggest impact. What followed was the most epic, transformative and inspiring chapter of my 15+ year career. That's why it's really a difficult moment for me to leave, with such a deep emotional attachment to the people, to the project.

The people at StarkWare are out of this world. It's very easy to be the dumbest person in the room there, and honestly it's the best thing that can happen to you.

A few things I'll carry with me forever:

- The Exploration Team, a bold bet that @avihu28  and Uri trusted me with. We started many open-source projects that helped shape the Starknet ecosystem, showcase cool stuff that could be built with our tech, and some even became companies with their own journeys.
- The Starknet developer ecosystem, the fastest growing in the whole crypto industry two years in a row. But it was never about vanity metrics. It has a soul: we built alongside people, supported them, and watched them grow. And it was amazing to collaborate with such a great community of passionate people.
- The privilege of being at the forefront of StarkWare's bets on Bitcoin, privacy, freedom tech and AI.

So why leave now? Over the past year, AI safety took over my mind. I'm convinced it's one of the most important challenges humanity has ever faced (very likely the biggest imo), and that math, cryptography among other things have a big role to play in it. And also that we need much more people and resources to work on it. The call to make my humble contribution became too strong to ignore, also as a duty to my children and the world we leave them.

@EliBenSasson, it was an honor to ride with you. I believe the true impact of STARKs and verifiable computation is yet to be seen, for blockchains and far beyond. As you told me, our paths will likely cross again, I strongly believe it. There are so many people from StarkWare I would like to thank and name (luckily many of them are to busy shipping they don't even have an X account 😂)... 
@bbrandtom my brother I love you (don't worry I will nurture the flame). 
gigachad brains like @LiorGoldberg2 @VolokhIlia 
You all know that I think the world of you, that working with you was such a pleasure, we had so many epic intense moments together.

I remain extremely bullish on Starknet and @StarkWare. The tech is years ahead, the StarkWare team is out of this world. The Starknet Foundation is full of great talented people too, and I have full confidence in @strjd87 ability to spearhead the vision and lead his team (full of great folks like @thedamooo @henrlihenrli @franklyteddy @omarespejel and others)  towards success!

The Starknet ecosystem is still strong, and I am amazed to see friends like @MentorNotPseudo still on the frontline and shipping and battling constantly to help Starknet moving forward. I have great respect for the builders and I wish them all the best and great successes.

To the StarkWare team and the Starknet community: thank you for the trust, the energy and the friendships. If there's one team that can make StarkWare and @Starknet incredibly successful, it's this one. I'll be cheering from the front row.

Forever grateful ❤️

经过几天深度使用，我的工作生活已经全面 muse 化了🤣下面是 10 件它帮我干的事：👇

1.网上购物。香港这边的购物网站有多难用谁用谁知道。现在家具、日用品、食品全是它在 HKTVmall、京东上比价、装购物车，我看一眼点付款。去超市买了啥，拍张小票给它，它就知道哪些不用在网上重复买了。

2.盯股票账户。几个账户的持仓它实时同步，异动、浮亏、快到期的期权，半小时内推我。忙起来顾不上看盘，它替我盯着。

3.管邮箱。三个邮箱全归它看，银行每笔花销、结单它都盯着提醒，重要邮件分级，要我拍板的才推给我。

4.工作助理，接管飞书。审批、邮件、群消息它先筛一遍，早晚各一份简报，逐条给我建议，我只负责逐个拍板。以前这些能淹掉我大半天…

5.接管社媒。X 和 LinkedIn 的私信评论它按我定的口径全回，每个寻求合作的消息先通读分析作人员背景调查，再报我谁靠谱。香港 AI 项目的人就是这么攒起来的。

6.接管 mac 上的 Codex 和 Claude Code。我出想法，它整理成任务书，指挥那俩写系统，还负责验收盯进度。手机上就能调度，人在哪都行，香港还不用翻墙。

7.每天早上给我做一期 AI 早报播客。双人对话，5 分钟，过去 24 小时的行业动态，雷打不动 8 点发我。

8.教我粤语和英语。粤语整句翻+粤拼+录音；英语单词每天推，按记忆曲线考我，答错的反复追杀…

9.帮我写稿。诺贝尔奖科普口播、演讲稿都是它出稿我改。规矩一条：稿子里只能留能念出口的话。

10.管杂事。越野赛报名、租房找房源、水电自动转账、iphone duo 抢购，每天还去查门店有没有现货。

以上内容完全真实，因为这内容也是 muse 三万根据这几天的工作总结写的。能真干活的 agent 和聊天机器人，完全是两回事。用了几天，睡眠都颠倒了🤣

马斯克19岁时，在加拿大读大学，是个总窝在宿舍打游戏的大宅男，说话还带南非口音。  

他曾经鼓起勇气约一个女生吃冰激凌，结果当天被放了鸽子😂

这个女生，就是贾丝廷，他的第一任妻子😂

当时贾丝廷比马斯克低一届，马斯克第一次看见她，就很心动。
于是他走上前搭讪，说两人在一个派对上见过，但其实贾丝廷根本没去过那个派对....  

好说歹说，贾丝廷终于勉强答应了下周跟他去吃冰激凌，可到了约定当天，马斯克去宿舍找她，人家根本不在🤣

马斯克又去找贾丝廷的闺密，打听她最爱吃什么口味，然后买了一个她最喜欢的香草巧克力碎甜筒，满学校找人。
终于在学生中心找到了贾丝廷，硬把甜筒塞给了人家。  

之后马斯克常常打电话约她，被拒绝一次，他就再打一次，后来他转学去了美国，还一直给贾丝廷寄玫瑰。  

不过真正打动贾丝廷不是这种穷追不舍，她觉得马斯克懂自己。 
有一次两人逛书店，贾丝廷指着书架说，以后自己写的书也要摆在这里，马斯克非常笃定的相信了她。 
这是第一次有男孩子认真对待她的作家梦，贾丝廷很感动。  

可毕业以后，两人还是各奔东西，一晃就是好几年。 
直到有一天，贾丝廷跟妹妹说，要是马斯克再打电话来，她就答应当马斯克女朋友。 
结果一个星期后，马斯克的电话真的打来了。  

那时马斯克已经在硅谷创业，贾丝廷就一次次飞过去看他。 
后来马斯克卖掉了第一家公司Zip2，在家门口的人行道上单膝跪地，向贾丝廷求了婚。  

2000年1月，两人在加勒比海的一座小岛上结了婚，后来又有了五个儿子，一对双胞胎和一组三胞胎。

author: LiebermanAustin
quoted_text:
$BRO has raised its dividend for 33 years in a row, but the stock is down 43%.

Is this a buying opportunity or a falling knife?

VALUATION (from @FASTGraphs):
Blended P/E: 15.87x
Normal P/E: 22.64x over 20 years
5-year normal P/E: 26.31x 
EPS yield: 6.30%
Dividend yield: 0.94%

Since December 2006, earnings are up 729%, while the stock price is up 361%, lowering the P/E from roughly 28x in 2006 to 16x today.

The stock peaked near $125 in March 2025, at a P/E of roughly 29x. Four quarters later it's at $70 and a blended P/E near 16x.

THE BUSINESS:
When a trucking company, a hospital, or a city needs insurance, it usually does not call an insurer. It calls a broker, who shops the risk to carriers, negotiates the terms, and collects a commission on the premium every year the policy renews. Brown & Brown is one of the world's five largest insurance brokers: $5.9 billion in revenue in 2025, about 23,000 employees, and more than 700 offices. 

It carries no underwriting risk. The carriers pay the claims.

$BRO was founded in Daytona Beach in 1939. Hyatt Brown joined the family agency in 1959, bought it out, became CEO in 1961, and ran it for 48 years, listing it on the NYSE in 1993. 

His son Powell has served as CEO since 2009, and Hyatt remains chairman. The company grew through hundreds of acquisitions of smaller agencies with operating margins near 30%, and it joined the S&P 500 in 2021. One segment sells insurance and benefits to businesses, governments and individuals. The other sells to other brokers and runs insurance programs on behalf of carrierBsR.

THE FUNDAMENTALS (2022 to 2025):
Revenue: $3.57B to $5.90B (18.25% CAGR)
Operating income: $1.04B to $1.70B (17.56% CAGR)
Net income: $659M to $1.04B (16.53% CAGR)
Operating cash flow: $881M to $1.45B (18.05% CAGR)
Operating margin: 29.23% to 28.72%
Return on equity: 15.03% to 9.62%
Return on invested capital: 9.35% to 7.32%
LT debt/capital: 44.23% to 34.87%

Profit grew with revenue, and margins held. In 2025, the company doubled in size. 

Total assets went from $17.80B to $30.65B, equity from $6.44B to $12.57B, and the company spent $7.91B on acquisitions, with $7.71B raised in stock and debt. 

Return on equity and invested capital fell because the new capital arrived in June and the acquired earnings only started in August. After the acquisition, Enterprise value stands at $31.03B against a $23.60B market cap.

EPS HISTORY:
2006: $0.62
2011: $0.57
2016: $0.91
2020: $1.67
2023: $2.81
2024: $3.84
2025: $4.26
2026 estimate: $4.49
2027 estimate: $4.85
2028 estimate: $5.34

EPS growth has depended on the strength of the broader insurance market. No growth for five years from 2006 to 2011. Then $0.57 to $4.26 over 14 years, about 15% a year. The 54% jump in 2017 and 16% drop in 2018 on the chart are the 2017 tax law passing through the numbers. Analysts model 5%, 8%, and 10% from here. The dividend went from $0.11 to $0.62 over the same 20 years, requiring roughly 15% of earnings.

THE CATCH:
Revenue grew 35% in Q1 and 30% in Q2. Almost all of that growth was from acquisitions. The core Brown & Brown business grew 10.4% in 2024, 2.8% in 2025, was flat in Q1 of 2026, and -0.7% in Q2, excluding contingent commissions. A broker's commission is a percentage of the premium, so when rates fall, the same clients pay less. Catastrophe property rates fell 15% to 35% last quarter, and management expects more. The last time rates fell like this is the 2006 to 2011 stretch on the chart.

The company bought Accession Risk Management for $9.825 billion, its largest deal to date, closing on August 1, 2025. It paid with about $4 billion of new stock sold at $102 a share in June 2025, another $1.2 billion of stock issued to Accession's owners at $110.57, and debt. The stock is at $70.53 today, 31% below the offering price, and the company has since bought back about $500 million of shares in the 60s. A $400 million note comes due in December. The market's other worry is that software replaces the middleman. Management announced AI partnerships this year and says the benefits will arrive in three to five years.

In its favor: adjusted EPS still grew 7.8% in the first quarter and 3.9% in the second, with zero organic growth, because Accession's earnings came in. The FAST Graphs Analyst Scorecard shows Brown & Brown beat both the one and two-year estimates 55% of the time and hit estimates the other 45%, with no misses.
 
On the Forecasting tab, 2028 EPS of $5.34 at the 5-year normal P/E of 26.31x results in a share price of $140.37, a 37.57% estimated annual return with dividends. 

At the 20-year normal P/E of 22.64x, the share price would be $121. At the 15x fair value multiple, it would be $80. 

These scenarios are based on analyst estimates, which can be wrong. They are not predictions or recommendations to buy or sell the stock.

text:
The cost of proving software correct is collapsing fast, and this is what it looks like at scale!

We've been coming at the same challenge from a different angle, applying LLM-driven verification to Linux kernel components, with good results.

But the hard part is still the spec.

LLMs struggle to infer specs and pick interesting properties, and for us the absolute hardest proofs sometimes need a human to close.

And both efforts here run into the same next frontier: concurrency. Their proofs assume a single-threaded binary and ours a sequential model, while much of the software we depend on (the kernel especially) is concurrent.

A hearty congratulations to @theoremlabs and @AnthropicAI's Frontier Red Team on advancing the future of software correctness!

HIP-3 turned Hyperliquid into exchange infra anyone can build on. @tradexyz won round one on distribution with 115 live markets of listed names and ~97% of HIP-3 OI.

Round two is the private market, and that's Entropy's lane.

The real test?
