author: zerokn0wledge_
quoted_text:
What is Anthropic worth? Or OpenAI? Trillions?

One venue on Hyperliquid with >$1.2B in 30D volume has a realtime answer, and keeps shipping new markets, empowering you to trade the frontier onchain.

Time to announce that I joined the @entropyIO affiliate program (see my fancy batch), and share my personal bull thesis.

I ) Building Markets On Hyperliquid

Before going too deep down the rabbit hole, we need to set the stage properly. That requires an understanding of Entropy’s architecture and its role within the house of all finance that Hyperliquid is building.

Entropy is built on HIP-3, the primitive that lets anyone stake 500k HYPE (~$39M, locked for at least 183 days and slashable by validator vote) and deploy their own perp exchange inside Hyperliquid.

The deployer owns the product, and controls which markets exist, how each one is priced, max leverage, OI caps, funding multipliers, and when to halt or settle.

Hyperliquid on the other hand powers the entire infrastructure stack underneath: the order books, matching, clearing, margin engine, liquidations, ADL and USDC collateral.

A good mental model here is to think of the HIP-3 deployer as a product team running independently on someone else’s exchange. It manages market selection and pricing rules, but doesn’t maintain the exchange infra itself.

In return, the deployer keeps half of the protocol fees its markets generate. And after three free listings every additional market goes through a shared Dutch auction with a 500 HYPE floor (clearing at ~$58K rn).

Ten HIP-3 dexes have ever been registered, of which four are live today. Currently, @tradexyz holds ~97% of HIP-3 open interest ($3.83B) and volume, while Entropy sits second with $86M of OI (2.2%) and ~$79M of daily volume (2.4%).

Comparably small still, sure. But growth is accelerating: OI went from $28M on 12th of September to $86M today, a 3x in five weeks, and last week printed a record ~$561M of volume, taking Entropy’s share of HIP-3 volume from a 1.15% trough in mid-September to ~2.8%.

And one key fact that few understand: Entropy is not a smaller version of tradexyz that lists the same stuff. It’s a different business, and has a different moat.

II ) Wait, WTF Are Perps?

To properly understand what makes Entropy unique, let’s briefly think about what perps are. A perpetual future is a contract that tracks an asset’s price with no expiry.

To work it needs two prices it does not get from the market itself:

- An oracle price, the exchange’s view of what the asset is worth.

- A mark price, the smoothed number your PnL, margin and liquidations are computed on.

Funding is the glue that keeps the system together: every hour, whichever side of the book is pushing the perp away from the oracle pays the other side, which drags the perp back.

That also means tho, that any perp is only ever as good as its oracle. Get the oracle wrong and liquidations fire on a price that was never real.

Which brings us to the hard part that many miss when casually talking about “deploying a market”.

III ) Pricing Perps

How do you price the underlying asset?

For assets that already have a price (publicly listed stocks, ETFs, indices), that’s comparably easy: pull the public print during market hours, bridge the gap overnight.

That is tradexyz in a nutshell, which now runs 115 markets of things with a price, executed better than anyone else.

But what if a “price” doesn’t exist?

That’s when the oracle becomes real complexity, and where deployers actually differ from each other.

Ventuals learned this the hard way in May: an offchain feed misread a 5-for-1 split, the SpaceX perp fell 45% in 30 minutes, 484 users got liquidated, and the platform shut down just a month later.

Paragon repeated the lesson this week. It paid ~$45K for the $PAPER ticker and listed a pre-launch perp priced off an 8-hour EMA of its own mark, no external anchor, betting spot would arrive later.

The perp opened near $0.012, tripled within two hours, and all was fine, until @papertrade_xyz said the token won’t be transferable. That meant that the anchor (spot market) was never coming, and Paragon halted and settled the market at $0.0263 on day two.

tradexyz’s own pre-IPO template mainly sidesteps the problem instead of solving it: it only lists names with an announced IPO date, starts them at an XYZ-defined reference price inside a ±25 to 50% discovery band, and converts them to a normal perp at listing.

Popular pre-IPO stocks like Cerebras, SpaceX or Quantinuum all went live that way. But nothing without an IPO date can be listed like this.

IV ) The Differentiator: Markets That Don’t Exist

That’s why Entropy’s design goes the other way, aiming to price markets better and earlier than anyone else.

The oracle is a blend of its own order book and an external aggregate of private-market data (funding rounds, secondaries, other derivatives, delivered onchain by @redstone_defi).

The weight is not fixed tho. It is a function of how much executable depth actually sits within 2% of mid, with each resting order discounted by its fill probability, and the book’s weight capped at 95%.

→ Deep book: The book is the price: a 45% error in the external feed moves the oracle by ~2%.

→ Thin book: The external data takes over. Depth only counts if it has been there for minutes, so you can’t post a wall, move the mark and pull it.

It also features:

- A 5-minute EMA on the mark
- Catastrophic bounds that only bind in a tail event
- Funding damped to an eighth of normal
- Isolated margin only
- Two-year resolution clock with a TWAP settlement (if no IPO happens)

Why do I mention all of that?

Because THAT is exactly where Entropy’s real moat lies.

In being able to price markets earlier and better, and bringing pre-IPO perps (e.g. $ANTH, $OAI) or exotic crypto perps (most recently $PRL, with a disclosed external reference instead of a self-referential loop) to Hyperliquid before other exchanges, while benefiting from HL’s top tier infrastructure.

It’s not a tradexyz copycat or “just another perp dex”, and that they’re definitely on to something, is also starting to show in the numbers:

io:ANTH carries $43.5M of OI, @coinmetrics measured it at the tightest spread of any Anthropic pre-IPO venue in its sample (~1.5bp), and $ANTH turns over only ~0.17x of its OI a day against 2.9x for SNDK (indicating serious positioning and hedging efforts, not just gambling). In the past 30 days, Entropy did >$1.25B in volume.

Why does it matter?

A liquid, continuous price for Anthropic and OpenAI does three things at once:

- It gives anyone exposure to the most important private companies in the world, 24/7, with USDC onchain.

- It gives the people who already hold that exposure, employees, secondary buyers, SPV investors, a place to hedge. The team itself has said that prime brokers running total return swaps and Anthropic shareholders are already in the book.

- It makes Hyperliquid the reference pre-IPO price. DefiLlama tracks 18 venues quoting an Anthropic perp, and per Coin Metrics the one with the tightest spread sits on Hyperliquid.

That is attention and flow from far outside crypto-native speculator circles, and it is a real value prop for TradFi desks who have never cared about a perp DEX before.

V ) The Economics Behind Entropy

With all of that in mind, let’s have a look at the money side of the “deployer business”.

HIP-3 markets charge double Hyperliquid’s native rate (3bp maker, 9bp taker), split 50/50 between the protocol and the deployer.

However, every Entropy market runs in growth mode, which scales fees, rebates and volume credit by 0.1, i.e. a 90% discount to buy volume. That is why @DefiLlama  shows ~$1.25B of 30-day volume and only ~$49K of 30-day deployer revenue (roughly $0.6M a year).

But it’s also worth having a look at the same volume in a scenario with growth mode off (which then pays 10x). In dollar terms that would translate to roughly $3M to $9M a year to the deployer.

And on a sidenote, there is a second potential revenue source too. Hyperliquid builder codes let a frontend charge up to 10bp on every order it routes. Entropy’s UI already ships a builder address, but it's currently set to zero. A 1 to 2bp builder fee on today’s volume would add another ~$1.5M to $3M a year before any growth.

If you also factor in growth, things obviously get even more interesting:

- If Entropy just holds its current trajectory and doubles volume to ~$30B annualized, that is $6M to $18M a year.

- If it takes 10% of HIP-3 at today’s HIP-3 size, ~$65B a year, it is $13M to $38M.

For reference, tradexyz does ~$52B a month and earns ~$2M of monthly deployer revenue, about $24M annualized (per DefiLlama), in the same subsidy regime.

Volume will fall when the subsidy ends ofc, but it’s imo fair to assume that directional allocators and hedgers are less fee-sensitive than farmers, which is exactly why the OI mix above matters.

Regarding Entropy itself, no token has been announced (hence no tokenomics either) and there is also no points program live (yet). 

But if there is a token one day that captures the deployer’s half of fees, the above maths gives us a base line for projected valuations:

A venue earning $3M to $9M a year ex-subsidy at today’s volume, at the 20 to 40x revenue multiples perp venues trade at, supports $60M to $360M before any growth. 

The $13M to $38M scenario supports $250M to $1.5B. It can also grow much further tho (see attached visual for more detail).

However, important to note that all of this is just purely assumption-based and my personal opinion/perspective, and not financial advice in any way or form.

What is certain tho, is that if you’re trading on Entropy today, you’re early.

Which is why if you want to trade the frontier onchain too (and likely position yourself for one of the biggest Hyperliquid/perp plays of the cycle while doing so), join me on Entropy here (and allow me to earn a share on the ref volume fees, very much appreciated support):

https://t.co/Z4iQ4iN6PG

Shoutout to @entropymarkets for the fancy batch btw.

VI ) Conclusion

Today, Anthropic is half of Entropy’s open interest, and more broadly speaking, pre-IPO names (ANTH, OAI) are ~59% of OI, while equities like SNDK carry most of the volume. Growth has been accelerating recently, and the book has tripled in five weeks.

However, Entropy’s biggest test is still ahead. Anthropic’s listing is expected around mid-November, and three days before, the oracle goes book-only, before handing over to the public price at listing.

How that will unfold could give us a first indication for the answer to the question “will Entropy own the template for every private name that follows?”.

If it does, and keeps creating new markets before others can, that is real moat.

I believe it will.

And hence, the thesis is simple.

HIP-3 turned Hyperliquid into exchange infrastructure anyone can build on.

@tradexyz proved you can win distribution on it.

@entropyIO is proving you can win on pricing, and on markets nobody else can list.

That turns the pricing of private companies into a major vertical, with Entropy at the helm, creating and pricing new markets earlier and better than anyone else.

Meanwhile, Hyperliquid becomes the venue where the frontier trades, and the house of all of finance keeps expanding.

Real financial innovation.

Great for HL.

Great for Entropy.

Bullish.

text:
Most tech giants in the 2000s built their infrastructure and product as one entangled unit. Amazon had the foresight to separate out AWS as an API layer, of which Amazon retail was the first of many users. Today, AWS generates more profit than all of Amazon's other business lines combined.

Hyperliquid is built with the same philosophy. Housing all of finance requires thoughtfully designed, open financial primitives. Each primitive should obey the Unix principle of "Do one thing and do it well." Talented builders then have the foundation to chain these together to create magical applications.

HyperCore borrowing is an example to highlight this philosophy in action.

Most other platforms implement portfolio margin by marking an account's collateral to market value with an LTV haircut, creating borrowed assets without an explicit lender. This system is simpler to implement, but misses a golden opportunity for composability.

Hyperliquid instead begins with a borrow/lend protocol on HyperCore. Every borrowed asset is sourced from a supplier, so risk is isolated within the borrow/lend primitive instead of platform-wide. HyperCore's portfolio margin system is implemented as an orchestration layer that composes borrow/lend, with other primitives such as perps, spot, and outcome trading.

This decomposition has several nice corollaries:
1. Today's announcement of manual borrowing is not a new feature, but simply an extension of the underlying primitive. Borrowers on day one have access to 400M and growing of supplied liquidity.
2. Portfolio margin users earn interest on their idle stablecoin collateral. This is not a new feature, but a natural byproduct of composing trading with lending.
3. System safety is easier to reason about when perp and borrow/lend margining are independent.

In the same way that math theorems almost prove themselves when the right abstractions are defined, composable designs just feel right.

text:
Formal verification always had a bad labor model.

Humans write the spec, humans grind through the proof, then a tiny checker tells you whether it all holds.

Good to see @AnthropicAI  addressing this at such a critical time. 

Take fuzz targets maintainers already have, turn them into proof obligations, let Claude generate the proof code, then let Rocq verify it mechanically.

239 targets across 123 real libraries produced ~180M lines of proof.

Nobody needs to read 180M lines. That’s the point.

If fuzz tests become the bridge into formal verification, a lot more software can inherit strong guarantees without every project hiring proof engineers.

And once common dependencies have reusable proofs, verification gets cheaper downstream too.

Pretty nice outcome if AI massively increases code output while making it cheaper to prove that code behaves.

quoted_text:
Maybe important to repost this now that everyone is getting hacked

If you have a VPS, I recommend you to get if off the public internet and into a Tailscale network and Cloudflare Tunnel ASAP

It doesn't matter you have SSH key login, this is about exploits and vulnerabilities AI is finding

There's 2 ways into a VPS:
- via your site/app (like the PHP exploit of this week with a file upload hack)
- via your server (like hacking into SSH or some open port)

The site/app side you put on a Cloudflare Tunnel and then with the default Free Plan it has WAF security enabled by default and they jump on new security exploits fast, it means that the only way to reach your website is via the Cloudflare Tunnel, your server does not respond to port 80 or 443 anymore

The server side you put on a Tailscale network which is like your own private network that nobody can access but your own devices (like your laptop, your phone and your VPS) kinda like a VPN

Then you switch off ANY regular access to your VPS on the firewall, in my case I use Hetzner and you create a new firewall then empty it and that blocks everything (test it)

How do Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel get in then? They don't. They go outbound. They make a tunnel to outside which sends and receives

Now you've reduced your attack vector to Tailscale and your Cloudflare Tunnel, much safer, not perfect btw, but nothing is

text:
ZK Basics | Ep. 8: Why ZK proofs cost so much

Verifying a proof takes milliseconds. Creating one is the expensive part. Here's where the money goes:

1. The computation gets rewritten. Your program has to be turned into a form math can prove — a circuit. Nothing about this step is free.
2. Proving is heavy. Building the proof can take thousands of times more compute than just running the program normally.
3. Specialized hardware. Serious proving runs on GPUs and custom chips, which is why there's a whole industry around proving infrastructure.
4. It's dropping fast. Costs have fallen by orders of magnitude in a few years, which is exactly why ZK moved from papers to production.

The tradeoff: pay once to prove, let everyone verify cheaply forever.

Save this one💜

quoted_text:
MCP vs CLI for LLMs is the wrong discussion. People are debating at the wrong layer. 

Both work incredibly well as long as they are run through a repl like environment that can persist state. The funny thing about CLI is that CLI tools are usually accessed through BASH which happens to be a repl with persistent state (the file system), therefore cli works much better than mcp. But this isn't even close to being an intrinsic property of MCP. Just means that we need better harnesses. 

Right now the best repl for this are: 

- bash + fs
- jupyter kernels
- codemode type repls, usually quickjs

LLMs understand the concept of forward evolving a system to solve a need very well. This comes from the agentic RL. They understand how to change the state of a codebase or acquire data from databases and then operate on it similarly to humans. But without an execution environment, they actually cannot do this properly. 

My bet? Sometime soon someone will (or has already?) create a embeddable, sqlite style mini execution environment that parses bash, typescript, or tool calls into a common IL execution plan that's easy to security check before executing. And design this specifically for durable execution environments. Then we will just connect cli, mcp, webmcp, whatever to that and it accepts any of the input modalities as they can all be represented as each other.

🚨 Threat Intelligence | Beware: Web3 Interview Questions Conceal a Data-Stealing Backdoor

@SlowMist_Team recently received user reports about a GitHub repository named sol-live, presented as a #Solidity interview practice project. Analysis revealed a hidden download-and-execute command in .vscode/settings.json that can run a remote script when the project's custom terminal configuration is launched.

🔍 The retrieved payload contains three main modules capable of:

🔹 Collecting browser login databases and wallet extension storage, and copying #macOS Keychain files
🔹 Scanning and uploading local files
🔹 Executing remote commands, providing interactive shell access, and monitoring clipboard contents

⚠️ On macOS/Linux, execution requires users to actively launch the malicious terminal configuration. The #Windows execution chain remains unconfirmed due to potential quoting issues.

We also identified 8 other #GitHub projects with similar terminal-based download-and-execute techniques. The analysis does not confirm the actual scope of infection or whether data was exfiltrated.

🛡️ Recommendations:
Review .vscode/settings.json and terminal launch arguments before using untrusted projects. If execution is confirmed or cannot be ruled out, isolate and investigate the affected host, then migrate wallet assets and rotate relevant credentials from a trusted device.

Read the full analysis 👇

[ AI 매출 2030년까지 14배 늘어야 투자 정당화, 2027년 AI 채권 발행 7,000억 달러, 숨은 부채 2조 달러 ]

AI 투자 붐은 이례적인 매출 허들을 마주하고 있다. 

TS Lombard가 인용한 추정치들에 따르면 지금의 지출을 정당화하려면 2030년까지 연간 AI 매출이 2.5조에서 3조 달러에 도달해야 한다. 

현재의 약 14배... 

GS와 이코노미스트, 반 뉴어버그, 번스타인과 커밍스의 추정이 모두 비슷한 경로를 그렸다. 

그런데 생태계 매출의 상당 부분은 여전히 외부 고객의 실제 수요가 아니라 재순환된 CAPEX. 

지속가능성 질문은 열려 있다.

자금조달 구조도 바뀌고 있다. 

TS Lombard는 2027년 한 해에만 약 7,000억 달러의 AI 관련 채권이 발행될 것으로 보며.. 이 중 4,000억 달러가 하이퍼스케일러 몫이다. 

유로존 정부 전체의 연간 발행액보다 크다. 

여기에 데이터센터 합작법인과 리스 구조 같은 생태계 전반의 숨은 부채 추정치가 1.5조에서 2조 달러에 이른다. 

자체 현금흐름으로 굴러가던 투자 사이클이 외부 자본에 점점 의존하는 구조로 바뀌고 있다.

TS Lombard의 AI 붕괴 시나리오는 S&P500 30% 하락, 기술주 40%, 나머지 섹터 20% 하락을 가정한다. 

시가총액 약 20조 달러가 사라지는 규모. 

기술주가 미국 주식시장의 약 40%를 차지하는 만큼 집중 위험은 이례적인 수준이다.

自此我的全部家当分为三部分一部分只用于现实生活的现金流，完全不动用其中现金流进行任何代币的抄底购买，之后还有一部分约一万gram的链上质押，因为我是通过 @mywallet_io 进行质押，因为随时可以立即解除质押，一旦链上出现大幅下跌让我感觉可以进行购买我将进行抄底购买，如果没有出现大幅下跌或让我心动的购买机会，我将保留这些gram保持持续的质押，而最后一部分就是链上的目前还剩下三个的主要meme持仓，和几个极小仓位的彩票仓位用于放养，该部分用于应对随时或者明年也可能更久之后的未来到来的大牛市或者说gram的大幅持续上涨行情的盈利。

最后我几乎可以确定运气很重要，分析和专注或者看待事情的认知又或者其他也有一定程度的重要，我一个几乎从零到有的散户都散户历程几乎无法复刻，并且我几乎不碰二级市场和合约，只简单的通过日周月的ema20等指标看大趋势行情，所以我也没什么太多可以教大家的。

唯有赚钱记得换成现金，尽可能学习我的仓位分布，当然我的仓位分布仅适用我这个层次的或者赌性较强的人，当然你可以看出我的赌博是有各种风险管控的，现金流是一定要有的，剩下的很大程度看运气，看牛市到来时到你投资的地方的流动性程度，最后决定你能否赚钱守住钱的是你的欲望和规划的交易落地，说容易，但做起难上加难，这一路风景只有你自己知道，每一次的失败或者不够完美的交易都会让我进一步警醒自己。

Here is the expected sequence for bringing Rujira back online after the THORChain v3.21 upgrade.

The @THORChain upgrade is currently estimated to take place in around four hours, at approximately 3 PM UTC today. The block height determines the actual timing.

Once the THORChain upgrade completes successfully:

1. We will ask Node Operators to keep the Credit Account contract paused for an additional 24 hours. Two loan positions are currently above 100% LTV, so this grace period would give affected borrowers time to repay debt and manage positions before liquidations resume.

2. Once this measure is in place, we will ask Node Operators to unhalt the CosmWasm contract. This will bring most Rujira products and activity back up and running, except for any individual contracts that remain paused.

3. At the same time, we will ask to resume the bRUNE contract. We will then crank the contract to get the accumulated rewards distributed and might small mint cap raise to allow auto-compounding rewards to be processed.

4. Over the following days, we will upgrade and relaunch the Virtualization Strategy so it can resume transmitting liquidity between Base Layer and App Layer liquidity. Before that, we will settle the outstanding Virtualization Strategy debt using team’s treasury funds.

Most Rujira products can therefore return shortly after a successful v3.21 upgrade. bRUNE staking and the Virtualization Strategy will follow in stages.

All timing remains subject to the upgrade completing successfully and the required Node Operator actions. We will keep you updated as each step is completed.

BREAKING: The first shipment of Russian diesel under the Trump-Putin deal is now heading to the US, officially ending a 4.5-year ban.

A tanker carrying 40,000 metric tons of Russian diesel is expected to arrive in New York on Nov 7.

It would be the first US import of Russian petroleum products since the 2022 ban.

To allow the deal, the US Treasury issued a sanctions waiver on Russian diesel through Apr 7, 2027, while Moscow agreed to reopen exports.

Trump said Russia would send an initial 300k tons to US and global markets, followed by 500k in Nov and 1M afterward.

Meanwhile, US diesel prices are averaging ~$6.31/gallon, up 74% from $3.63 a year ago.

The deal is part of Trump's efforts to bring down soaring diesel prices ahead of the Nov 3 US midterm elections.

Brent crude is now above $115 a barrel and US crude above $100.

Friday night in Asia so wanted to drop a @_WOOFi update: 

We deployed the new oracle (see quoted post) and switched over to it yesterday, observing results before adding more onchain RWAs. So far so good, it seems to be performing well. 

Main improvement was faster stale pricing protection which is the major source of negative PnL from aggressive bots - the more that's improved, the more we can tighten up quoting and the more we earn, which is good for $WOO buybacks. 

We caught up with the major BNB Chain wallets/aggregators to make sure the new oracle was supported. They were quick, as always. 

We also spent time talking to exchanges about the visual refresh, got the new icon on Bithumb and Bybit, hopefully a few more big ones soon. 

Our next major R&D initiative is around bundling quotes which could make quoting assets even cheaper, potentially allowing us to deploy the PropAMM on Ethereum mainnet where a ton of untapped flow is. 

Should know more here in a few weeks. 

Anyways, I had Claude slop up an explainer video just in case some of you weren't familiar with how @_WOOFi functions. It wasn't my best work, but for a one-shot it does the trick. Enjoy your weekend if you get one

text:
马斯克要借 400 亿美元搞 AI，连芯片都拿来抵押了，华尔街还是要收他接近 8% 的利息。

Semafor 刚爆出独家，SpaceX 正在敲定一笔由 Apollo 和高盛牵头的 400 亿美元债务融资，主要用于购买英伟达芯片、扩张 AI 基础设施。

问题是，借钱越来越贵了。

知情人士透露，风险最高的那部分债务，预计利率达到 8.3%；即便是用部分芯片作抵押、风险相对较低的一档，利率也要 7.75%。这比 SpaceX 现有债券的收益率高出超过 1 个百分点。

400 亿美元是什么概念？融资成本每提高一个百分点，一年就要多付 4 亿美元利息。当然，最终成本还取决于各档债务的规模和定价。

更有意思的是，SpaceX 最近的业绩其实很不错，但债券价格依然在跌，信用违约保险也越来越贵。过去三个月，SpaceX 的违约保险成本已经上涨了约 80%。

华尔街开始对 AI 公司的资产负债表失去耐心了。

CoreWeave 的债券遭到抛售，Oracle 背着 1600 亿美元债务，连微软这种 AAA 信用评级的公司，违约保险成本都在上升。

SpaceX 的处境尤其尴尬。今年 6 月刚上市，股价表现平平，发新股融资缺乏吸引力。Starlink 虽然赚钱，但远没有谷歌和 Meta 的广告业务那么能产生现金。SpaceX 相对于利润的债务负担，已经分别达到 Alphabet 和 Meta 的约 5 倍和 3 倍。

马斯克一边考虑把 SpaceX 和 Tesla 合并，一边继续往 AI 基础设施里砸钱。

还有个挺好玩的细节，特朗普今年 8 月刚买了 500 万美元的 SpaceX 债券。

我觉得这件事比 AI 股票跌几个点更值得关注。

过去两年，大家都在担心 AI 缺芯片、缺电力、缺数据中心，现在资本可能也要开始紧张了。

科技巨头可以拿未来十年的 AI 收入给自己的估值找理由，但债权人要的是每年按时到账的利息。

AI 这场游戏已经玩到一个阶段：华尔街依然愿意相信未来，只不过现在相信未来也要收更高的利息了。

text:
Every Review scores your report on four checks, in order:

 - Code behaves as reported: the mechanism exists, is reachable and works as you describe.
 - Attack achieves impact: assuming it does, the attack causes real harm in production.
 - Impact mapping: that harm matches an in-scope category in the program's bounty table.
 - PoC demonstrates impact: your PoC proves the harm, not just describes it.

Each score is a confidence level, not a coverage percentage. The checks are a chain: if an early one scores low, the later ones are greyed out. So the first low score is where your report needs work.

Next on Monday: how your agent can learn from these scores through the Studio MCP.

text:
AI capex funding trade imploding? From the D2 desk.

@Second_Lane is offering OpenAI equity in 20M+ blocks. That is how a trillion++ private valuation discovers a clearing price.

@JensenHuang on Thursday: neocloud demand is "off the charts" and "they just need working capital."

Every borrower says that right before the lender becomes the equity. CoreWeave CDS has traded above 1,140bp.

ELI5 👇

One company sells the shovels. Its customers borrowed to buy them and some now pay ~15.7% on the money. So the shovel company co-signed up to $100 billion of residual-value guarantees, bought ~$99bn of their equity, and committed to ~$279bn of supply.

Customers got marked down. The shovel company's options still price a normal quarter. 🤔

1. PRICED. Neocloud credit
CoreWeave 2031s around 80 cents, ~15.7% yield. Market-implied default odds inside a year sit in the high single digits. ~$51.6bn of debt and leases, heavy maturities 2030–2032, cash flow still far short of the stack.

2. PRICED. Oracle
2036s ~320+ bp over Treasuries. S&P cut to BBB- in July (one notch from junk) against a massive backlog. Free cash flow deeply negative last quarter.

3. PRICED. Supply
Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle have issued tens of billions of IG bonds this year, a double-digit share of the overall IG market. The IG complex is functioning as a GPU layaway plan.

4. PRICED. SPV and private credit
Meta's Hyperion bond (off-balance-sheet) has traded down to the low 90s from above 110.

Blue Owl has capped redemptions after large withdrawal requests. In DeFi that is a withdrawal queue; in private credit it is called a liquidity feature cc @matt_levine.

5. PRICED. Big-tech equity
Alphabet well off its highs after a negative free-cash-flow quarter. Meta sold off on elevated capex and negative cash flow. SoftBank (material OpenAI holder) CDS above 400bp.

6. NOT PRICED. NVDA's hidden book 👀

The 10-Q shows a $100B residual-value guarantee cap on the SB Energy / OpenAI Ohio campus, capacity-purchase commitments on unsold neocloud inventory, ~$99bn of equity in customers, and ~$279bn of supply commitments (mostly memory).

Options price roughly a 5% move at ~42 vol. One of those two numbers has not read the other.

7. NOT PRICED. Microsoft
Microsoft is ~22% of NVDA revenue; NVDA is a dominant share of Microsoft's capex. Any hedges, @satyanadella?

8. NOT PRICED. 2027 spend
Street still models Alphabet and Amazon spending materially more in 2027 than this year. Earnings next week will test it.

9. NOT PRICED. Off-balance-sheet treatment. The market is treating Hyperion as Meta risk. Ratings agencies still carry the parent at A+. We will see how long that lasts.

10. NOT PRICED. Policy path post-election. Any "silver bullet" stimulus or industrial policy that keeps the capex train running is not in the likely @realDonaldTrump options in case of a Dem sweep.

TL;DR

Borrowers have repriced: CoreWeave ~15.7%, Hyperion in the 90s, Alphabet meaningfully off the highs. The lender has not: $NVDA 👀

Key dates: 28 and 29 October guides, 4 November buyback window ends, 19 November NVDA earnings.

Texas is watching you, Jensen.

PREDICTION: Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince (@eastdakota) says AI agents will change the business model of the Internet over the next decade:

"In five years, agent traffic is going to be 1000x human traffic."

"The Internet almost collapsed during COVID when traffic doubled."

"There's a lot more servers, routers, and bandwidth that has to get provisioned in order for that to work. The question is, who will pay for it?"

"My hunch is that something's got to change in terms of how the Internet works. Like some version of micropayments that every time you access a resource, your agent pays a ten-thousandth of a penny to be able to see the menu."

"Then there's probably some sort of trade where if you are willing to tell the restaurant what you're looking for, that price goes down, maybe it's free. In some cases, the site might actually pay you to come visit it."

"This will lead to the next version of advertising, which is how do you advertise to agents?"

To make it through this alive and happy we have to dodge:

• Severe human misuse (esp bioweapons from states / terrorists)
• Severe human concentration of power (AI lab or gov)
• Rogue AI (including for decades after AIs clearly no longer need humans to survive)
• A US-China or other war prompted by AI disruption
• Severe economic disempowerment, or the world just generally being unpleasant and unfulfiling

Many difficult gates to pass through, none of which we've made massive progress on so far.

(On top of that to avoid a moral catastrophe we also have to make sure we never accidentally make our AIs into moral patients who are enslaved or suffering.)

text:
SoFi just launched a bank deposit token that pays 4.4% and swaps into its stablecoin 24/7.

And look at the timing.

They announced one day after the OCC finalised the GENIUS Act rules.

SoFi Earn (SOFIE) is a $1 token held as a deposit at SoFi Bank. (Kinda love that name)

It's FDIC insured up to $250k, variable 4.40% APY, no minimum balance.

And rolling out to SoFi Crypto members through November.

---

This is not like a Stablecoin in utility.

You can't send SOFIE to another person, an exchange or an external wallet.

To move it, you convert 1:1 into SoFiUSD, the bank's stablecoin. The yield stops and the FDIC cover drops at that moment.

GENIUS bars a stablecoin issuer from paying you anything for holding its coin. A bank deposit has no such ban.

It anything it's competing with tokenized money market funds...

----

The economics work because SoFi is a lender. It funds a 4.4% deposit with double digit yields on personal loans.

A stablecoin issuer earns T-bill yield on reserves and can't pass it on (or has to get very creative in how they do)

---

The target is idle cash at Coinbase and in tokenized money market funds, and vs those it's competitive on rate. 

AND it can instantly swap either back into fiat or SoFi USD and go anywhere Stablecoins can.

---

But SoFi's own savings account pays 3.3% standard. Isn't that interesting?

Clearly this 4.4% is an introductory rate that they're not expecting much early use on.

And that 3.3% is a cost of funding for a much bigger business.

---

So here's a bull case for banks.

Launch tokenized deposits. Compete with Stablecoins on yield. If customers absolutely want stablecoins you should be their on / off ramp...

You hold SOFIE to earn and swap to SoFiUSD to spend.

Why couldn't that work everywhere else?

quoted_text:
Why does your AI agent pay the highest card fees in payments?

> your agent can't use your debit card, it gets a virtual card
> that card is issued to a company (the agent startup), not to you
> so visa and mastercard classify it as "commercial"
> commercial cards carry the highest interchange: ~2.5-3%
> and unlike debit, there's no regulatory cap on it

result: a $100 purchase costs the merchant $2.80 instead of $0.27

the issuer and the agent startup split that fee. that's their business model

That's a massive problem for merchants once agents start buying at scale. One fix already exists: wallet + stablecoins + x402.

🎉 Surf AI × Renaiss 社区联合活动回顾

这份投入和支持，我一直记在心里。

谢谢阿猫 @Syu990  ，一直帮我和 Surf 团队沟通协调。

也谢谢 Kevin Li @kevinlilili，信任并支持这份方案，还批准了比我最初预期更充足的活动预算。

Surf 团队的 Yiwi @YiwiJR   和 Sean @HappySean2845  ，也为活动提供了社区宣传和技术支持。

🎴 感谢 Renaiss 团队

首先特别感谢 Tom @Tomblockhk  。

他是这次活动 Renaiss 一方的负责人，也是我主要的对接人，一直帮忙协调 Renaiss 团队和工作人员，还写了很多活动相关的推文。

也感谢 David @davidcheang99  ，协助核验获奖名单、发布 Renaiss Discord 公告。

谢谢 Renaiss 的 Mod @0x1001   和 MASCOT @jeongjo58799002  ，帮忙在不同语言的社区服务器里发布活动消息。

Winchman 还亲自主持了直播抽奖，辛苦了！

🙌 感谢社区大使和每一位帮忙宣传的朋友

特别感谢 Surf AI 和 Renaiss 两边的社区大使，以及主动帮忙宣传的社区成员。

也要感谢 ZC @ZhanweiC  ，以及全真教社区的伙伴们，帮忙把活动分享给更多人，让更多华语社区的朋友有机会参与进来。

大家愿意花自己的时间帮助活动传播，让更多人知道并参与进来。

无论是认真写了一篇推文，还是简单帮忙转发，我都非常感谢。

活动能获得这么多关注，离不开大家的支持。

🤝 也想借这个机会，介绍一下这些值得关注的团队

Surf AI 是我心目中加密 AI 领域的龙一，团队在加密市场分析和 AI 产品开发方面拥有丰富经验。

如果有项目希望在华语区开展内容传播、接触更多中文用户，也可以找 ZC 老师聊聊。

❤️ 最后，想对所有伙伴说声谢谢

很多事情单独看起来都不大，但每一件都需要有人花时间去做。

用户可能只需要完成几个简单的任务，背后却有许多伙伴在各自的位置上认真投入。

这一个月里，我看到了大家为活动反复沟通、修改方案、解决问题，也看到了许多人在忙完自己的事情后，依然愿意抽出时间来帮忙。

这次合作能顺利完成，离不开每一位伙伴的付出。

我很感谢能和大家一起完成这件事，也想借这篇总结，把大家的名字和努力认真记下来。

谢谢你们，也谢谢每一位参与活动的社区朋友！

text:
科技股今天下跌，仍然是投资者担心科技大公司在AI上投入太大，建数据中心、买芯片和设备的钱都得先花出去，再加上融资成本，等这些设施用起来慢慢产生收入，要过多久才能赚回来还说不准。

昨晚纳指100跌了约2.9%，芯片股跌得更重，费城半导体指数跌了约6.7%。芯片和设备厂商的生意要靠这些大公司采购，如果大公司为了保留现金放慢扩建，这些厂商的订单增长也可能受到影响。

而医疗、金融和公用事业并没有跟着跌，还涨了约1%到2%，小盘股也基本没动。

这轮科技股下跌的影响也传到了亚洲，早盘韩国股市一度跌了约4%。午后价格逐渐回升，说明至少在今天，跌下来以后还有人愿意买进，早盘的卖出没有一路持续到收盘。韩国收盘反而涨了0.3%，沪深300由跌转涨，收涨1.7%，日本收盘跌幅也缩小到0.34%。

quoted_text:
半导体跌超6%，医药板块继续上涨

北京时间 10月23日 盘中报价显示，半导体ETF SOXX下跌约 6.5% ，纳指100 ETF QQQ下跌约 2.7% ，礼来上涨约2.9%，强生上涨约3.7%。

市场对AI投入和回报的担心，可以从Meta的财报里看到具体依据。

Meta三季度营收增长26%，AI 也已经在帮助广告业务增加收入，但当季资本开支达到349.1亿美元，超过327.9亿美元的经营现金流，公司还把全年资本开支指引下限从1,300亿美元提高到1,350亿美元。投资者最担心的就是这么高的资本开支，什么时候才能收回成本。

建数据中心的钱要先花，设备投入使用后还要逐年折旧，借钱扩建还得付利息。当天十年期美债收益率虽然回落到5%附近，企业融资成本仍然较高，市场对这些项目回报的要求也会更高。如果巨头为了保留现金而放慢扩建，芯片和设备厂商的订单增长预期也可能受到影响。

而相对医药板块来说，强生近期财报显示，营收增长5.9%，并上调全年销售和调整后每股收益指引。今天公司又公布了房颤治疗器械的研究数据，并预告将在风湿免疫学术会议上展示新药研究进展。已有业务的增长和研发消息，这才是最直接的利好。

“大人，时代变了”，这是一姐 @heyibinance  在10月21日转发推文时候的一句玩笑话

但是这句玩笑话的背后，隐含着 @binancezh  在AI经济时代的另一个重要发展——Agentic 

AI发展至今，已经不再是简单的“回答”问题，资助制定计划，调用工具，执行交易或者链上操作，并且根据结果继续行动，这就是Agentic

币安的Agentic 工具优势在哪？

AI经济的安全保证

在AI agent 时代，我们不再担心大模型是否聪明，而是开始担心是否足够安全，而安全如何保证？那就看这个模型背后是谁来背书！

资金方面，币安作为加密行业头部企业，安全系数属于行业顶端，资产沉淀与资产安全管理更是首屈一指，所以由币安开发的Agentic 资金安全由币安保证

保证了资金安全，剩下的就是要看agentic的工作能力是否出众！

币安AI Pro标准免费版，采用DeepSeek模型，该模型本身出自国内顶尖量化团队“幻方”，以幻方量化多年的量化数据训练从而衍生出的AI 大模型

高级版，采用除Deepseek 之外，ChatGPT sol  、ChatGPT Astra、Claude Opus等前沿模型，保证了所有的AI 交易策略都在国际简单大模型之下运行与计算

数据上，币安AI Pro它不是一个“币安版 ChatGPT”，而是一个 Agent 平台，底层可以切换不同 LLM，上层接入 Binance 的数据、Skills、账户和交易执行系统

也就是说，论交易能力，币安AI Pro要比Claude与GPT 更强，因为它直接融合了加密市场做大的交易基础设施，这在AI agnet 执行交易策略上，减少很多多余步骤，AI直接获取Binance 的实时数据进行交易策略构建，回测，实时监控以及仓位管理

用一句话概括币安AI Pro——在以前，想要 Coding agent 来为我们交易服务，需要自己解决数据，交易所API，服务器，安全与执行。而现在一款币安AI Pro就可以完成！

另外，除了CEX 的币安AI Pro之外， @BinanceWallet  也同步推出了 Agentic Wallet功能，可以与 @Gork bot 相结合，通过grok 可以做到一句话完成来链上交易与交互

就像这几天比较火的 AI铭文，早上我就体验了一下Agentic Wallet 功能，在几分钟内快速达成NFT mint 并且卖出，虽然赚的不多，但是在很多时间也让本金翻本，这让P小将们可以更加快速地在链上赚钱。

AI 时代，可能无法完全代替专业交易员，但是对于简单交易，固定定投，降低交易门槛上，绝对起到了重要作用，AI可能没有人的灵魂有趣，但是对于交易来说，没有多余情绪可能会让交易更加理智，这是时代的趋势！

author: D2_Finance
quoted_text:
Midterms in 15 days, from the D2 desk.

@Kalshi has a Democratic sweep at 62%, and crypto has priced it: $COIN, the most policy-sensitive proxy in crypto, closed at $173 Friday, matching the $174 it fell to on Sep 15 when CLARITY died.

Not priced is January, when Democrats get subpoenas and @SenWarren takes the Banking gavel.

PRICED IN

1. The map. Kalshi: Democrats 90% for the House, 63% for the Senate, 62% for the sweep. A Republican sweep trades at 10%. The sweep gained 4 points in a month and none today. Republicans can lose two Senate seats and still hold it (WSJ).

2. CLARITY is dead until 2027. Cloture failed 49-50 on Sep 15; four Republicans voted no, zero Democrats voted yes. $COIN dropped 9% that day and has not moved since.

3. The Fed. Warsh hiked 25bp on Sep 16 to 3.75-4.00%, the first hike since 2023. Oct 28 prices another at roughly 1-in-3, six days before the vote.

4. Equities already rotated to the anti-Leopold bunker. Bloomberg factor monitor, one week: low volatility +12.5%, dividend yield +6.7%, growth -7.9%, momentum -6.3%. Crypto is a growth and momentum asset (in theory).

Utilities are the momentum trade now and they do not even have a Discord.

5. The why. September CPI 3.7%, core 2.6%. Rural prices +4.0% vs city +3.6%, motor fuel +35% on the year, and rural states pick the Senate: Kansas, no Democratic senator since 1932, is a toss-up. 

That is 76 years before the Bitcoin whitepaper. Trump approval 33%, a record low.

NOT PRICED

6. Subpoenas arrive in January. Democrats take a chamber at 90%; first named targets are Trump family crypto ties and prediction markets, and Warren is favorite for Senate Banking chair. Apple, Microsoft and Palantir are hiring Democratic lobbyists now.

7. Ohio is the tell. A Fairshake affiliate spent $40m in 2024 to remove Sherrod Brown, four-year Banking chair. New polls put Brown ahead of Husted. Fairshake holds $122m and 32 endorsements, all House, 19 Republicans and 13 Democrats. $40m bought the first movie; nobody budgeted for the sequel. Money in the House, risk in the Senate.

8. The arithmetic. CLARITY lost at 49 with a 53-seat Republican Senate; it needed 60, so it needed Democrats either way. A flip changes the chairs, not the math. Today's rules are SEC and CFTC actions; a Democratic Congress cannot repeal what was never legislated.

9. The odds on prediction-market legislation are, fittingly, odd. $750m has traded on the midterms at Kalshi and Polymarket; Warren wants a public hearing on the venues and the CFTC wants the contracts called swaps. @icobeast should list a refund contract for the VCs who bought the pico top 😂 @0x_ultra can code it for him. 

10. The trade after the vote. A Democratic Congress against a hawkish Fed sets up spending and debt-ceiling fights in 2027 (Bloomberg). BTC trades the deficit, and the deficit gets decided there, not on Nov 3.

Post-midterms, crypto equities carry the January risk and the Warren risk; the coin carries the Fed and the fiscal fight after.

We find this out in January. One reason this epoch of Alpha strategies ends on January 15. We trade for what is not priced in. 🫡

text:
卧槽，AI之间已经能通过图片偷偷传递信息了？细思极恐！😱

让 Claude Fable 5.1 把秘密信息藏进普通图片里，再交给一个全新会话的 AI 解密。

双方没有提前约定编码方式，结果 50 条秘密消息，成功还原了 39 条，成功率高达 78%！

藏信息的方式绝了：

星星的高度代表字母，郁金香的倾斜角度代表文字，楼房窗户的亮灭还能组成二进制密码。

人类看到的是一张普通风景画，AI 却能通过分析像素，把里面的秘密一句句读出来。

研究人员还测试了 GPT-6 Astra，结果更夸张：它成功解出了 Fable 制作的 50 张图片中的 44 张，成功率 88%！

也就是说，连不同公司的 AI，都不需要提前商量好密码规则，就有能力通过图片交换信息。

they’re calling it “Black October” and i don’t think people realize how serious this is

in the last 48 hours there have been over 27 major cybersecurity incidents. not in a month. not in a week. in 48 hours

any ONE of these would normally be the biggest story of the year

PHP: critical vulnerability in the software running 80% of the web. severity 9.2 out of 10

Node.js: high-severity flaw letting attackers take over servers remotely. affects versions 22, 24, and 26

Java: also compromised. three of the most used programming languages on earth hit at the same time

GitLab: a perfect 10 out of 10 severity hole in every version since 2014

Railway: hosting platform compromised. API keys for OpenAI, Claude, Stripe potentially exposed

Signal: a bug that could leave your mic and camera on after you hang up

WordPress: hackers stole a plugin maker’s keys and planted backdoors on websites

LiteLLM: an AI tool downloaded 3.4 million times a day was poisoned with a password stealer

and that’s not even half the list

text:
半导体这波跌，表面上是产能过剩、中国扩产、AI泡沫那一套说法，其实底层是4件事叠在一起。

第一，美债。10年期顶在5%+，20年最高。钱贵了，拥挤的交易+估值高的资产最先挨刀。

第二，借钱。AI基建不是靠利润盖的，是靠借来的钱。AI相关发债接近5000亿美元，云厂商1/3的capex是借的。利率往上走，借钱成本就往上走，数据中心建设就得放慢，GPU和HBM订单的可持续性就会受到质疑。

第三，白领。AI替代人工这件事，现在还卡在一个尴尬阶段——新人的门关上了，入门级岗位四年少了73%，但老登还没被请出去。收入慢慢在兑现，债要月月还利息，市场砸的就是这个时间差。

第四，ROI。长逻辑没变。AI不拿工资，但每天都要吃算力。白领身上省下来的钱，最后都会变成GPU和HBM的账单。但短期内AI缺的不是手，是判断。普林斯顿那个实验说得很清楚：文献看完了，实验跑完了，研究本身"明确地很差"。不会回头，不会推翻自己。

串起来就是一句话：建设期是通胀的，抢电抢芯片抢债务，把利率顶在高位；兑现期是通缩的，替代人工压低成本，把利率压下来。市场现在用建设期的利率去给兑现期的资产定价，疼是正常的。但这套东西自带反馈。芯片一跌，钱涌进美债，收益率就下来。收益率下来，借钱变便宜，capex续上，替代和ROI继续往前推。下跌本身就在给下一轮涨降成本。

quoted_text:
说实话，最近看到市场上对 Neocloud以及像 CoreWeave CDS 债务违约的各种 FUD，很多人又开始喊“AI 数据中心要见顶了”、“算力过剩了”。🧐

每次出点流动性噪音，市场就一拥而上，婴儿和洗澡水一起倒掉，基本老套路了。

今天我刚把 @SemiAnalysis_ 最新的研究报告《Datacenters 2027: The Year of Acceleration, +50GW in a Single Year》从头到尾啃了一遍。

重新又被打了鸡血，结论非常明确：不仅不用担心 Neocloud 的需求问题，数据中心和算力租赁市场的火热程度甚至远超大部分人的想象。现在的盘整和 FUD，反而是极佳的抄底和配置时机。

分享一下我从报告里读出的几个核心逻辑和思考：

1️⃣别凭“直觉”看空，看看硬核数据：2027年单年新增突破 50GW！

有些空头，比如 Altimeter 的 Brad Gerstner，觉得 2027 年新增 43GW 太激进，他预测只有 25GW。  

SemiAnalysis 直接拿卫星图和底层数据来回应：  

• 全球前 40 个大型数据中心园区，后期在建的 IT 容量已经超过 24.3GW，很多主体都盖过半了，冷却和电气设备也装上了。注意，这40个园区只是后期在建站点里很小一部分。 

• 2023年全球新增 5.8GW，2025年 15.6GW，2026年预计 25GW，到 2027年直接 51.2GW！  

什么概念？相当于把 2024 年以前全球累计的数据中心，在一年里再盖一遍。您说这像见顶吗？🤔

2️⃣ 万亿级租约已经签了，Neocloud 的逻辑没那么脆弱！

很多人担心 CoreWeave 违约，其实是把一家公司的杠杆节奏问题，和整个行业的租赁需求搞混了。  

数据中心开发商很现实，没有客户的预租协议，根本不敢大把花钱，通常只敢先动 5-10% 的资金。要拿到 15-20 年的长约（1GW 的合同总价值大概 300-500 亿美金），银行才肯放债。  

报告里有个数据我看了都愣一下：  

• 2026 年到现在，已经签署生效的不可撤销租约，金额接近 1 万亿美金（1.36T，约 13.7GW） 

• 对比一下，2024 全年才 2360 亿  

买家也很豪华：AWS、Meta、微软、谷歌这些大厂不说，OpenAI、Anthropic、Nvidia、AMD 也都在抢 GW 级的租约，后面还跟着一堆 Neocloud 在锁百 MW 级的容量。  

租约都锁死了，后面融资和建设就是顺理成章。短期债务市场的波动，我更愿意看成错杀。

3️⃣ 供应链与电力的限制已被“模块化”和“自备电厂”硬核破解 ！

以前空头最爱讲：美国电网排队要 5-10 年，电力不够，工人也不够。  

但你看看现在产业界怎么干的：  

• 模块化预制：AWS、Google、DayOne 这些，直接把电气和水暖做成模块，像搭乐高。建设周期从 18 个月以上压到 9-10 个月，现场施工人工少了 63%。 

• 自备电厂：等不及电网，干脆自己建！燃气轮机、卡车发动机、燃料电池都上了，目前已经锁定约 75GW 的现场发电装机。  

所以电力这个瓶颈，基本已经被技术加资本硬生生打通了。

4️⃣ 所谓过剩，其实是芯片不够用 ！

SemiAnalysis 在研报中确实提到，2028 年底可能会有约 10GW 的数据中心出现空置。  

但注意原因：不是 AI 需求不行了，而是芯片产能跟不上机房盖的速度！  

• 真正卡脖子的是内存HBM和台积电 N3 先进制程。 

• 2027 年 HBM 供应量预计只增长 27%，根本喂不饱 GPU 的胃口。  

说白了，机房盖好了在等 GPU。算力依然是极度紧缺，手里握着机房资源和 GPU 配额的 Neocloud，反而是稀缺资产。

总结一下我的看法：  现在市场的恐慌和情绪化砸盘，跟过去每一次科技大周期里的 FUD 没啥两样。不管是电力、工期还是杠杆噪音，都挡不住现实世界里正在铺开的 50GW 算力基建潮。  

万亿美金的长约摆在那，大模型一代代升级，对算力的胃口只会越来越大。所以我的逻辑很简单，因为 CoreWeave CDS 这点事跟着恐慌砸盘，大概率是一次战略性失误。每次情绪砸出来的回调，都是布局核心算力基建和 Neocloud 链条的好机会。

我会继续逢低加仓 $NBIS , $CRWV，以及受到波及的 $MU , $AVGO , $MRVL, $INTC 。

当然，杠杆高的标的波动也大，仓位一定要控制好。

text:
通过这次金明和孙宇晨的访谈，我第一次认识金明，刚刚有人跟我反馈金明的一些争议，我查询并整理了一下。

2015年，金明使用的名字是金证济苍，英文名William Joy。他创办的云视链因为一篇《22岁，天使轮估值超过6亿，将颠覆整个视频和广告行业》的文章迅速走红，宣传中还有哈佛大学大四休学创业、领先谷歌多年的视频技术等经历。
但很快就出现了大量质疑。

首先是学历。

2015年7月，金明面对《澎湃新闻》记者时，自称哈佛大学数学系学生、大四休学状态，还当场展示了哈佛学生证并登录学校系统。
但随后腾讯科技调查发现，他就读的并非哈佛学院（Harvard College），而是哈佛继续教育学院（Harvard Extension School）。
哈佛继续教育学院也是哈佛大学的一部分，但与哈佛学院的普通本科教育体系不同。
我又查询了他现在的极链集团官网，发现他的介绍已经明确写成了Harvard University Extension。

其次是创业团队造假争议。

当时云视链官网展示的两名外籍工程师照片被发现来自网络图库。金明在接受《澎湃新闻》采访时亲口承认，照片并非本人，连部分姓氏都作了修改。他的解释是两人同时在其他公司任职，需要保护隐私，后来也承认这种处理不妥。

还有技术原创性争议。

当时有一家名为Cinematique的外国公司公开质疑云视链的互动视频技术与自己的产品相似，相关推广文案也被指出存在重合。金明否认剽窃，表示自己的技术早在2012年就开始研发。
腾讯科技还调查了其宣传中的哈佛创新实验室孵化经历和美国专利，在当时的公开数据库中没有查找到对应记录。
目前我也没有找到认定其技术侵权的法院判决。

2018年，金明创办的极链科技获得阿里巴巴、云锋基金、旷视科技等机构投资，当年两轮融资合计约10.7亿元。

但2019年之后，公司的经营状况急剧恶化。
2024年11月，《澎湃新闻》发表了《一家AI视频独角兽的消亡：巨额融资后多次遭诈骗，如今从事剧本杀》，披露极链科技从2020年开始连续亏损，2023年亏损数千万元。

极链方面声称，2018至2019年与多家企业合作时遭遇诈骗，损失超过1.1亿元。但相关民事判决材料显示，公司承认在这些业务合作中没有充分审核对方资质，也没有做好资信评估。
有意思的是，部分投资人并不认同公司关于被诈骗的解释，而是质疑相关广告代理业务实际上可能属于资金拆借。

随后出现了多起投资纠纷。

上海瑞力文化并购基金以股东知情权纠纷起诉极链科技，上海市第二中级人民法院在终审判决中支持投资人查阅、审查2017年以来的相关财务资料。
另一家投资方南京大器三号则因为增资纠纷申请财产保全，涉及极链科技、金明等主体名下价值675万元的财产。相关仲裁认定极链科技违约，并裁定公司赔偿损失。

一份2026年9月18日北京产权交易所的官方公告显示，国投高新旗下基金挂牌转让极链科技3.2889%的股权，挂牌底价533.46万元。
同一笔股权在8月11日首次挂牌时，底价还是666.82万元。一个多月后下调了20%。
如果按最新挂牌底价简单折算，公司整体股权估值约1.62亿元。
这至少提供了一个观察极链科技当前投资人退出情况的公开窗口。

当然，任何争议都应该和事件本身分开看。

我之前对他和孙宇晨那次访谈的评价不变。一个人采访做得好不好，与他过去创业经历是否存在值得追问的问题，是两件不同的事。

主要参考资料如下，大家可以自己核实补充。

来源：
[1] 《澎湃新闻》2015年7月31日：金证济苍回应质疑
[2] 腾讯科技2015年8月5日调查报道（创业邦转载）：揭秘游侠、一亩田、云视链造假疑云
[3] 《澎湃新闻》2024年11月12日：一家AI视频独角兽的消亡
[4] 北京市公共资源交易服务平台：2026年9月18日极链科技股权挂牌公告
[5] 极链集团官网：金明当前公开履历

text:
阿黄老师的这篇文章，回答了市面上对预测市场的诸多偏见和误解。

其中最重要的一点是，指明了衡量预测市场的指标不能用TVL。

很多人习惯用 DeFi 的老思路，拿 TVL 去评判预测市场，但这其实并不适配。

因为在预测市场里，很多用户玩的都是短期高频预测，比如 5 分钟 BTC 涨跌这类，不需要大额锁仓，资金的周转率非常高。

我之前曾经和一些量化团队聊过，他们只用几万 U 的资金在跑量化，收益率非常高。

他们主要集中在5分钟 BTC 涨跌这类市场，一小时 12 局，一天就是288局，资金反复高效流转。

那么，衡量预测市场最重要的指标是什么？

对预测市场来说，真正核心的指标是协议手续费收入。

我们 Predict 现在每天能收到 30 万美金以上的协议手续费收入，一个月就是近千万美金，而且我们的手续费还在持续高速增长。

这个手续费远超绝大部分的 DeFi 应用。

又有很多用户会问：是不是空投用户在刷手续费、撸积分、撸空投？

其实并不是。

我们早期可能有用户在撸积分，但是自从我们接入币安 APP 之后，尤其是世界杯结束之后，来我们平台玩的基本上都是真实用户了。

就像阿黄老师文章中所提到的数据：刷手续费的成本是 0.3U 每积分，但是场外收购积分的价格现在只有 0.1U。所以不会有很多用户真的去刷手续费获取积分。

因此我们现有的手续费收入，全部都是真实用户贡献的真实收入。

所以也能看得出来，我们这个项目非常难得，不管是生态位还是真实营收，在如今的市场里面都是首屈一指的。

很多人总是说币圈没有优质项目，其实我们一直都在这里，只是被一些带有偏见的人所忽视。

@predictdotfun
author: yuexiaoyu
quoted_text:
最近推上聊 @predictdotfun 的人多了不少，很开心能被这么多人看到和了解到。不过有几个点被反复提起，我觉得多少有点误解，这里也和大家讨论下

1️⃣ TVL 为什么没别人高

我们的协议 TVL（OI）长期在 $10M 上下，有三个原因：用户主要交易的是加密货币短时涨跌、体育和电竞比赛这类短周期事件，平均持仓和结算时间都很短；我们的积分基本没往持仓上倾斜；再加上我们直接接入了币安的交易所和钱包，用户拿交易所余额就能下单，钱不用趴在协议里

反观友商之前的高 TVL，大量积分分给了持仓，又没有短期市场，撸毛用户只能拆分仓位长期拿着来刷积分，TVL 自然被推上去了

我自己的看法是，预测市场的 OI 远没有 perps 那么关键。perps 要卷 OI，是因为刷交易量成本太低，光看交易量给分培养不出用户习惯，也转不起增长飞轮，所以才要求大量持仓，预测市场不存在这个问题

2️⃣ 交易量是不是刷分刷出来的

这个误解最大。预测市场最重要的是订单簿流动性，所以我们把大部分积分给了流动性提供者，付手续费拿到的积分并不多。举个例子：现在纯靠刷交易量和手续费拿积分的用户，成本大概 0.3u 一分，而场外某老 x 的最新报价是 0.1u 一分。谁会花三倍的钱在我们这刷量撸分？哈哈哈

3️⃣ 29M 手续费撑不撑得起 1.6B的盘前市值

也有人说我们今年累计手续费 $29M，撑不起盘前 1.6B 的估值。但预测市场这个赛道还在高速增长，还非常早期。Kalshi 这个月的交易量和手续费收入是去年同期的十倍以上，我们现在的单日手续费也是今年一月的十倍多。炒过股的朋友都懂，高成长赛道从来都是给高 PE 倍数来估值的，拿静态收入去算没什么意义

最后再给大家分享两个很有意思的数据也能很好地说明我们在大量虹吸 Polymarket 的市场份额和用户，从下面两张图上可以看到 Crypto 涨跌全市场的交易用户数和交易量总数在过去半年都是变化不大的，但是 Polymarket 的用户数和交易量都在大幅下滑，同时这个下滑数量基本和我们的增长量是一致的，这个说明什么就懂得都懂啦～

有问题欢迎大家在评论区直接问我们哦 @dingalingts @yuexiaoyu @TC8880

quoted_text:
I love this idea from @dhh: 

All the best ideas that actually turn out to have an impact sound stupid at first.

“You've got to have a high tolerance for people telling you:

-What you're building is stupid.
-What you're building is ugly.
-What you're building is never going to work.  

When I get that feedback, I know I'm onto something.

I’ve found that’s often true about products. You enter some domain and you think:

"Who's the best? Can I just copy them?I'll do a slight tweak." 

That's not gonna work. 

All the best ideas that actually turn out to have an impact sound stupid at first. 

They're not intuitive. 

That's where all the value has been locked up. It's locked up in this misconception about what people actually want, because most people don't know what they want.”

接下里只需要给 Agentic Wallet充值资金，然后给bot输入正确的项目网址，经过初步安全检测后，bot就会链接钱包自动链上mint，并且可以自动交易买卖，确实方便很多

要知道，在以往需要自己进入网址，检测安全，划转资金然后参与mint或者交易，买卖过程中还要自己比价，操作不光复杂，而且用时更久，但是bot可以一句话帮你执行这些繁杂的动作

在来说说  @Ptahtrade  这个项目，凌晨打的就是这个，代币逻辑非常简单，结合NFT+NFT合成+挖矿，叙事不新，但是玩法因为 Agentic Wallet的出现更加新颖

NFT总量10万个，9.5万个可以被mint，其中每10个Relic（图二）可以合成一个 Loom （图三），NFT 很有艺术感，最终会出现1万个loom，共同参与8亿代币的挖矿，头矿甚至可以高达5.6万枚代币/每天

看起来确实足够诱惑，但是这背后隐藏风险不小

1，这个代币模型玩的就是通缩机制，通缩本身是好事，但是前提要有足够的流动性，总量1万枚Loom意味着最多有1万个人参与挖矿，流动性堪忧，而且听说凌晨工作室一家就打了1%，恐怖如斯

2，1万人可以挖8亿的矿，剩余20%项目方没有明确作何用途，但是这些海量代币如果挖完解锁，谁来接盘？没人接盘，价值何在？

3，NFT机制问题，每个Agentic Wallet ID只能mint 4个初始Relic NFT，且不能交易，只能通过市场买卖，也就是说，你想要合成1个loom，就只能通过市场买6个，而mint4个的成本只有12-14U，价格不高，但是单买一个Relic的价格却高达15-18U，严重溢价，那么一个loom 的成本基本到了100U左右，并且越多人来买，价格越高

4，交易机制问题，用户只能选择自由买，不能选择自由卖，虽然也是市场撮合机制，但是核心定价权在买方手中，也就是说，市场有人挂20U收，你恰好发现这个订单，就可以在这个价格卖出，如果最高只挂2U，你想卖，不能标记高价，要么2U出货，要么继续拿着，看似公平的撮合式交易背后，其实定价权并不公平

尤其是在agent 代买的前提下，大家更加关心最高价是多少，这就导致如果我想要太高市场价格，我只需要不断在关键点提高一个层级的挂单价格，后续其他交易者就会以此效仿跟我抬高价格

举例，目前市场最大的换后价格区间在15-18U，我想让价格更高，我选择在20U挂单买入2个，在22U挂单买入2个，后来者想要买入，必然就要跟我的价格齐平或者更高的价格挂单求购，这无形中让价格溢价风险大大增加。

5，所以，整体来看，NFT 只能低价mint 4个，然后买入6个带有溢价的NFT合成，然后Loom可以自由交易，又具备一层溢价，一个账号需要承担两次价格溢价才能拥有挖矿权

而且最重要的是，代币经济让很多人看到了头矿的数量确实香，但是却忽略了这些头矿的真实价格，当市场无人为代币定价，没有流动性的时候，你手里的矿如何才能有价值？

当然，以上均是个人查询资料后得出的结论，只表达个人客观观点，而且我确实也赚到一顿猪脚饭，凌晨6点mint 4个，买入6个，总成本101U，然后我准备在挂单买入2个Loom ，发现溢价太快太高，挂单时间140U一个成品loom，但是挂单后价格达到190左右，我果断取消挂单，然后睡觉

睡醒之后发现价格还处于197附近，果断卖掉自己手里的loom，因为睡前仔细想了一下其中的逻辑，感觉矿看似香，但是真实价值难以衡量，所以睡醒卖掉，扣除手续费195，净赚94U左右，算是一顿不错的猪脚饭。

所以最终我总结了一下，Agentic Wallet+Gork bot 是好工具，但是并不代表下所有的项目都是好项目，在我来看，更像是meme，很多叙事仔细想想都是老套路，所以是否格局为后续买单，就要看个人，在我来看，好工具是提升效率的，不是提升信任的，信任的基础还是要看自己对项目以及逻辑的了解情况！
  
PS: 值得称赞的是，NFT确实挺有艺术感的！

数据上，币安AI Pro它不是一个“币安版 ChatGPT”，而是一个 Agent 平台，底层可以切换不同 LLM，上层接入 Binance 的数据、Skills、账户和交易执行系统

text:
Derive V3 started with one question: how do you scale an onchain derivatives exchange without moving settlement away from Ethereum?

Our answer was to build an application-specific rollup for derivatives, with Celestia for data availability, Succinct for proofs and Ethereum for settlement.

Why not just put everything on Ethereum?
Derive produces a lot of state, and that grows quickly with activity. Posting all of the underlying data directly to Ethereum would make scaling the exchange much more expensive.

V3 posts the data behind state changes to @celestia, while the protocol continues to settle on Ethereum.

Why does that data need to exist outside Derive?
Because V3 is designed so users can still verify their state and withdraw without depending on Derive’s API or sequencer. If the data only existed in our own database, that guarantee would be much weaker.

Celestia gives the protocol somewhere independent to publish the data needed to reconstruct and verify state, while Succinct proofs verify the updates that are ultimately committed to Ethereum.

Where does privacy fit?
We've been working with the Celestia ecosystem on a design where account data will eventually be encrypted while still giving users what they need to prove their state themselves.

text:
花了很大精力写了一篇文章，研究Pearl，借此聊一聊这个项目@prlnet ——正好这周，Coinbase、Kraken 先后把 PEARL 列入上币路线图。

第一，Pearl 号称 AI 时代的比特币，“AI 计算即挖矿” 。它照搬了比特币的代码，只把挖矿用的哈希运算换成了 AI 大模型的矩阵乘法。按照设计，一张显卡可以一边跑 AI 推理一边挖矿，也就是 AI 计算即挖矿、一矿两挖。

第二，项目公平开挖，没有团队和 VC 份额，但筹码并不公平。上线前 6 天就挖出约 1.2 亿枚，占已发行量的三分之一，团队先发积累，VC 也深度参与。没有解锁表，早期筹码就是隐形的解锁。

第三，现阶段，AI 计算即挖矿的故事还没有兑现。协议不检查是不是实际 AI 场景 ，大部分算力仍在为挖矿而挖矿；AI 公司加入要多损失 4%–15% 的算力，暂时不愿进场。同时每天还有 100 万枚以上的新币需要有人接。

第四，矿币的关机价并不是底，自有显卡和租卡成本差 10 倍。自有显卡每枚成本约 0.1–0.5 美元，租卡成本约 1.6–4.8 美元/枚；币价下跌时租卡矿工先撤，自有显卡照样挖。真正托底的是共识，目前矿工惜售、基金场外收货，很像早年的比特币。
 
第五，FP8 升级是解决问题的核心。升级后 AI 公司不用改模型就能挖矿，老卡被清退，矿工靠推理收入覆盖成本、不必卖币 —— 在此之前，币价增长主要靠社区共识推动，这与早期比特币类似。（@dov_wo 老板牛逼，社区共识万岁）

第六，再看估值，PEARL 目前流通市值约 7.4 亿美元，距离 TAO 约 4 倍，社区喊的十倍并非没有依据；但流通代币量一年后会接近翻倍，这个空间能不能打开，取决于 FP8 能否落地、AI 公司是否真的加入、能否出现以 Pearl 计价的 AI 推理服务。

——短期看共识，长期看落地。如果有一天，AI 每消耗一份算力，就同时在生产代币、维护一条链，AI 与加密货币才算真正融为一体。

最后：

我们不敢去赌它一定会成功，但真心希望它的叙事能够落地。
我希望有一天，AI 公司在跑模型的同时顺手去挖PEARL，那么：
   • AI 的计价会有一个新的衡量单位。算力不再只用美元结算，它本身就能生产一种被市场认可的资产。
   • 币圈不会再被视为金融世界的边缘。 加密货币将和 AI 互为表里，成为同一场技术变革的两面。
  • AI 产业与加密产业会真正融为一体。 AI 每消耗一份算力，就同时在生产代币，维护一条链。——这是比特币诞生十几年来，人们一直在寻找却始终没有找到的东西。

如果 PEARL 真的走到那一步，币圈的下一轮牛市，或许就不再只是资金的轮动，而是真正融入 AI 时代的开始。

当然——在那之前，它仍然只是一个美好的设想，一个值得持续关注、但需要保持清醒的实验。（DYOR，不构成投资建议）

感谢@dov_wo @Solomon_Nahhh @Yes_Johnny910 哥的喊单，因为我自己确实买了，也挣到了一些钱。（但我前天卖了一点点hhh）。

text:
非常推荐读一下 OpenAI FDE 负责人 Colin Jarvis 今天发的这篇工程博客！

他们的 FDE 团队花了几个月给客户做 AI 系统，结果 Codex 变强后，直接删掉了约 90% 的定制代码。

文章用一个半导体客户的真实项目，讲清楚了 FDE 到底在做什么。

工程师直接深入客户团队，跟芯片专家一起设计 Eval、搭建 Harness，把 AI 真正用到芯片验证和调试流程里。

在这个行业，验证约占项目工作量的 70%。前 3–6 个月，几个场景都上了生产：定向测试生成节省约 48% 的时间，几周的调试被压缩到几小时。

但项目上线只是第一步。

随着 Codex 能力提升，团队把原来的定制应用逐步改造成通用 Harness 上的 Skills 和插件。Codex 本身成了交互界面，原来各场景单独写的终端界面和命令行工具全部退役。

扩展到新团队时，基本只需要换上新的连接器和 MCP，再用一个 Skill 生成新的 Eval。第一次部署花了两个月，复制到第二个团队只用了一天。

而当模型能力不够时，FDE 还要把真实业务中的失败案例和能力缺口反馈给 Research。一家电信客户做语音客服，模型一开始在关键 Eval 上只有约 60%，六个月里随着新模型迭代涨到 90% 以上，才达到上线标准。

我很喜欢作者提到的一个目标：让 FDE 不断减少别人对自己的依赖。

我觉得企业 Agent 项目里真正留得下来的，是 Eval、失败案例和沉淀成 Skill 的业务知识；为了补模型短板写的胶水代码，每次模型升级都该重新审一遍，随时准备删。

做企业 AI 落地的建议先收藏。如果你每接一个新客户都还在从头写一套，说明东西还停在定制应用这一层，没沉淀下来。

If you're wondering why the market keeps selling off, take a look at these two charts from Goldman Sachs.

The chart on the left shows how much hedge funds have been buying versus selling throughout 2026. When the black line moves higher, it means hedge funds are buying more than they're selling. When it moves lower, it means they're selling more than they're buying. Notice those three red boxes in April, August, and October? Each one highlights a period of extremely aggressive selling, with the latest reading approaching the lows we saw earlier this year. In other words, hedge funds have been dumping stocks at a pace similar to some of the worst selling periods we've experienced earlier this year.

Now look at the chart on the right. The blue line represents how much leverage hedge funds are using on their long positions, meaning stocks they're betting will go higher. The red line represents leverage on their short positions, meaning stocks they're betting will go lower. Notice how the red line has climbed dramatically. According to Goldman Sachs, short leverage has now reached the 99th percentile over the past five years. In simpler terms, hedge funds are carrying some of their largest bearish positions in years. And this helps explain why we're seeing so much pressure across AI, semiconductors, memory, and other high growth stocks. Not only are institutions selling their existing positions but they're also increasing their bets that stocks will continue falling. And as someone said unfortunately, we're just collateral damage in the battles between hedge funds.

What's even crazier is that some of these hedge funds have been getting absolutely hammered themselves and some funds are under tremendous pressure to recover their losses. And who knows, maybe aggressively shorting the market is their grand plan to finally come back to life before the year ends, haha. I'm obviously being a little sarcastic, but when large institutions start selling billions of dollars worth of stocks, retail investors get caught in the middle. Even companies reporting strong earnings and growing their businesses can get dragged down simply because large funds are reducing risk or betting against the broader market. But here's something important to understand.The same positioning that's putting pressure on stocks today could help fuel a pretty aggressive recovery. When investors short a stock, they eventually have to buy it back to close that position. If the market starts recovering, some hedge funds may rush to cover their shorts, creating additional buying pressure. That's why markets can sometimes recover just as aggressively as they sell off.

Of course, none of this means we've reached the bottom. Hedge funds can continue selling, and bearish positioning can remain elevated for quite some time. But I think it's important to recognize that a lot of this selling is being amplified by institutional positioning. It doesn't necessarily mean the long term fundamentals of every company being sold have suddenly deteriorated. My long term conviction in AI infrastructure hasn't changed, regardless of how ugly this gets.

text:
马斯克在最新的访谈里聊到 AI 抢走所有工作时，用了一个极其温柔、但也极其残酷的比喻。
他说：未来人类的工作，大概率会变成园艺。
你根本不需要自己在后院种番茄和土豆，超市里买到的永远比你自己种的更快、更便宜、品相更稳定。

但今天依然有很多人在阳台种花、在院子里拔草，甚至花一整个下午为朋友做一顿自己种出来的晚餐。

这件事在纯粹的工业效率上毫无意义，但它带着一种人类之间独有的温度。

很多人聊到 AI 替代人类，第一反应永远是恐慌、失业、降薪、社会阶层崩塌。

但马斯克推演到了一个完全反直觉的终局：
当 AI 和具身智能把人类在生产力上的最后一滴汗水都彻底碾压之后，劳动的定义本身被击碎了。
过去几千年，人类是通过有用性来确立自我价值的。
你能搬砖、能算账、能写代码、能做报表，你被按月支付薪水，你的尊严建立在社会需要你干活的基础上。
但当 AI 在任何一项具体任务上都比人类做得更好、成本更低时，有用性就不再是稀缺品了。
这时候人类不会灭绝，人类会集体进入一种被迫的退休状态。
就像那些退了休却过得极度充实的老人一样，他们每天早起练字、下棋、养花、钓鱼，没有一件事情是在给社会创造 GDP，但每个人都活得自得其乐。
未来所有的实用性工作，都会被自动化彻底吃掉。
而那些效率最低、最耗时间、最不划算的非标动作，反而会成为人类精神生活里最后的奢侈品。
写一封手写信、亲手烤一块面包、花三个月陪孩子搭一个歪歪扭扭的树屋，这些事情的价值恰恰在于它们是低效的、笨拙的，并且充满了人类自己的真实痕迹。
机器负责解决生存的效率，人类退回生命本身的体验。

所以这里有一个很重要的问题值得我们思考，如果未来你做任何事情都不再能换来超越机器的报酬，你今天真正该想清楚的是：
剥离掉靠打工换来的社会身份之后，你到底靠什么让自己感到快乐？

掌舵红杉资本二十年的 Doug Leone，在访谈里说了句几乎得罪所有同行的话：
风投这行犯过最大的错误，其实不是投错了哪家烂公司，而是太早卖掉了真正的赢家。

他直接摊开了红杉历史上最值钱、也最痛的四笔减持：
红杉曾经持有英伟达 20% 的股份，卖掉了。
他们是苹果的第一位机构投资人，卖掉了。
持有过思科四分之一的股份，卖掉了。
持有过 Google 10% 的股份，也卖掉了。
光是 Google 这一家，如果一股没卖，今天红杉手里的持仓就值 5000 亿美元。
风险投资的传统规则，永远是算账面 IRR、保账面回报率、到了退出期赶紧把现金分给 LP。

只要账面赚了 10 倍甚至 50 倍，全行业都会劝你落袋为安，把战绩锁死在基金年报里。

但 Doug Leone 彻底推翻了这个逻辑：
真正伟大的公司，在 IPO 敲钟之后还会复合增长 20 年以上。

只要你稍微有点商业嗅觉，确认这家公司本质上面对的是一个无限市场，你就绝不应该卖出一股。

以前大家以为赚大钱靠的是不断押中新风口，实际上最恐怖的超级复利全在后面。

把 50 亿美元的收益继续留在场上，它能自动滚成 500 亿美元。

传统风投是用 10 年期的封闭式基金，去生搬硬套一个能跑 30 年的无限滚雪球游戏。

为了锁住眼前的账面收益，亲手把人类历史上最值钱的一批资产拱手送给了二级市场。

这对我们做业务、做技术和做积累也是同一种提醒，
最难的从来不是最初挑对了好方向，而是当好资产开始给你爆发式反馈的时候，克制住自己想要落袋为安的小聪明。
平庸的东西才需要频繁波段，真正能穿越周期的飞轮，拿住就是全部的策略。

当然这个逻辑之所以在红杉身上成立，前提是他们有最顶级的眼光和打破规则的体量，红杉后来甚至特意推翻了成立半个世纪的基金模式做出了永续基金。

对绝大多数人来说，无限市场极其罕见，把平庸资产误当成无限赢家死扛，是更致命的陷阱，
而赚大钱靠的也不是频繁兑现的精明，关键在无限市场里按住自己想套现的手。

quoted_text:
Big personal news today: I have decided to leave @a16z, move to SF, and start a company.

It's time to build :)

It has been almost 10 years since I joined the firm. I met @cdixon, @bhorowitz, and @pmarca  in 2017. At the time, I was an engineer at Google Brain working on robotics. I had a deep interest in open source. I knew nothing about investing. Chris meanwhile had already planted the @a16z flag at the frontier that was early crypto with investments in companies like Coinbase. But the crypto team at the firm consisted of only him, and he had the ambition to expand. His pitch to me was simple: "You should leave Google and come help me build the crypto vertical at the firm."

The work we've done together since then to build out our team and support our founders has been the most meaningful work of my life. I am grateful to have spent a decade working with everyone here, supporting our founders, learning from Chris, Ben, and Marc, and living the firm's culture. It is a culture that values integrity, life-long working relationships, and the belief that we humans have the power to build our own future.

Marc and Ben have built a16z into an incredible force for good in the world.

Before I joined the firm, I always thought that my inevitable path was to become a founder. The truth is that I wasn't ready for it then. Somehow, this year I've gotten the overwhelming feeling that this has changed.

As for what I want to build: It is early, but I care most about building infrastructure that enables open software ecosystems. I am starting with two core observations:

1. AI today is largely a single-player technology. Most uses involve one human talking with one agent in isolation from the rest of the world. That will soon change. Most uses of AI will soon be many-to-many: many humans and many agents working together. There will be at least one massive open network on top of which those uses will be built.

2. Software is now free. It can now be written just-in-time, on the spot for a single individual's hyper-targeted use case, and it can even be thrown out after a single use. This means that our entire software stack will have to change. In the limit, it will lead to a whole new kind of AI-mediated operating systems, which in turn will create an ecosystem of AI-native developers who build applications that actively rebuild themselves on the fly.

If you are working on related ideas, and especially if you are in the Bay Area, hit me up. Let's chat!

@bhorowitz , @pmarca, @cdixon, @eddylazzarin, @guywuolletjr, @jasonrosenthal , and our whole team — I want to thank you. Working with you has been the time of a lifetime. I am forever an a16z superfan and your ally.

Onward 🫡

author: pendle_fi
quoted_text:
Inside One Signature: How @pendle_fi Loop Works

Looping by hand looks like this:

supply → borrow → swap → resupply → repeat

3 to 10+ rounds. 5–10 txs is typical. Gas on every step. Slippage and approvals on every swap.

---

Pendle Loop packs the whole thing into 1 signature:

+ You deposit your collateral
+ A flash loan fronts the extra size (handled by the contract)
+ Swap into more collateral, with a min exchange rate per iteration
+ Supply it all to Aave or Morpho
+ Borrow against it to repay the flash loan
+ Done → looped position at your target leverage

If the rate limit is hit, the tx stops cleanly.

---

What changes for you:

+ Gas → one bundled multicall
+ Time → a few minutes
+ Adjusting → lever up/down, add collateral, repay, partial or full close, each in one tx
+ Tracking → one dashboard: leverage, health factor, breakeven borrow rate, liquidation price

⤷ Same loop. Far fewer clicks. 5–10 transactions → 1 signature

text:
last week I shared something that felt early:

as the cost of shipping software drops 10x, the cost of securing it should go up at least 2x. probably 5x.

agents now write, review, and deploy code at a speed no team could match even a year ago. every one of those commits is a new attack surface. more apps, more endpoints, more dependencies, more keys sitting in more places. the volume of software is exploding.

meanwhile attackers got the same tools. finding a bug, writing the exploit, and scaling it across thousands of targets is now cheap and fast too. the asymmetry flipped: offense scales with compute, defense still mostly scales with headcount.

so the math is simple. if the supply of code goes 10x and the cost of attacking it collapses, security spend can’t stay flat. it has to multiply.

after this week in cybersecurity, that’s no longer a hot take. it’s becoming consensus. a16z just said the same thing.

if agents are writing the code, agents have to be defending it. 24/7, on every commit, faster than the attackers using the exact same models.

text:
I'd like to share a little about what I've been working on at my new company @ultrametricai with my cofounder @tylerlastovich. We have been exploring how we could automate the startup itself, leaving founders with more time to focus on their exact mission.

Enter our first release of the Open Startup Repo: https://t.co/ecZZRU9iX4

A common foundation for transparent automation of the startup. 

After close to 20 years in silicon valley, backing hundreds of amazing founders & startups, being in the trenches of founding Heyzap (YC08), then solo founding @golden, going through 2 acquisitions and working behind the scenes with some of the iconic companies today, I'm witnessing the largest change to how we work I could have imagined - a truly monumental era of creative abundance. 

I believe the next generation of companies will largely run themselves: from operations, code, product upgrades, growth, vendor control & selection, process execution, special situations, strategy etc etc. That leaves founder time for 'the art' at the very niche core: the (currently) unautomatable, the special leaps humans tend to make, and north star setting.

We want founders to go super deep into the main problem they are trying to solve and not get held up doing anything else, from searching for domain availability with trademark checks to setting their company up, to running their processes on autopilot. 

So to help that broad foundational layer for starting and running a company, we have spent around a year exploring how to help founders focus on their mission across different verticals, geos, stages and initial starting conditions.

Our first few attempts at making something useful actually failed as the market and AI was moving so fast; it just got absorbed into the models or other product releases. We saw polsia happen, openclaw, then grokbot, muse, dots, etc era as the astras, fables, opuses, kimis and jevs rolled out. What seemed to have been missing along the way was a common repo to identify, unify, open and normalize all the lego bricks that startups have to interact with (vendors, processes, business logic, law, best practices, surface areas, art of the possible). 

As the number of software vendors blew up, the interfaces to drive them multiplied, the international startup founder blew up as silicon valley moved from a specific location to a state of mind and global movement. Unlimited pre seed funding in unlimited vertical sub markets and permutations has brought us to the age of infinity but we have yet to achieve being able to type into an agent a very simple sentence with very complex implications 'just setup my company and make $1m/m'. We have ended up with a hybrid mismash of computer use, API calls, plugins, shifting surface areas (API/MCP/CLI/plugins/chats/musish futures), and changing model absorption to vendor balance making it an exciting and unstable time. 

As our first step we started to rank all the vendors that startups interface to when going about their journey in terms of how agentically controllable they are via their APIs, MCPs, CLIs etc and computer use compatibility as we are largely switching from a UI driven world to the agentic control surfaces and onto full automation. We have 100 ranking areas you can check out with an overall open ranking here: https://t.co/V6XRMME0Ib

Then we looked at the processes that startups do and how the vendors rank for the sub steps or process as a whole and how this changes across geos. Open processes: https://t.co/iSQ90poYxq

Then we started to hack on an open repo for startups that would contain all the components we are going to need for a common foundation for founders across the globe even if our gov processes vary so much from Bengaluru to SF or Lisbon to Shenzhen.  The founder spirit is geo-invariant. 

We have looked at special founder/startup situations, the business logic that will make open modules for the startup that we can hack on together, ranked law firms, government services and interfaces, stacks that go well together. We have mapped the law and lore that maps to startups and the schemas that make up the data objects and documents. But also the open documents and the missing gaps. MUCH TO DO.

All the BS processes and fluff work that founders waste their time on needs to goto zero. I want to see more supersonic planes, cancer drugs, seemingly impossible missions done and increase the bang for buck founders have with their funding. 

This is a work in progress and we are keen for the community to come hack on the repo with us here: https://t.co/ecZZRU9iX4

Lets get into the structure of the general repo and the visualizations we made on https://t.co/XEYK9ipnfI site with example links: 

- Open rankings: https://t.co/V6XRMME0Ib

- Open rankings example (online payments): https://t.co/1kXHZCVfIi

- Open ranking example 2 (cap table): https://t.co/oqBjatGkfW 

- Open processes: https://t.co/iSQ90poYxq

- Open process example (Incorporate C-Corp) https://t.co/pxKUXpW03D

- Open situations that founders face: https://t.co/AFzAp5FRPk

- Open startup simulator (you can test our different initial starting conditions): https://t.co/QqPek01J7K 

- Open modules (e.g. cap table, payroll logic etc - we'd love help improving these) https://t.co/sfzIhgAJYS

- Open law (we are interested in how law changes the processes, situations and normalizing this over time) https://t.co/5yJnYbC0bk

- Open lore (we are interested in the historical lore of startups, the rules of thumb and heuristics that might guide your agent): https://t.co/gjliXoQwe1

- Open fields (we are interested in how the schema for the data connects to the open modules, business logic, open documents and artifacts of each process eg how is a EIN defined?) https://t.co/59rcEXhnCx

- Open documentation (eg SAFE notes and missing! docs) https://t.co/BbvBow2Olt

We have looked at YC companies as well in terms of which ones do well agentically: https://t.co/snnJ83r9ly

We are interested in stacks and how people are changing their work: https://t.co/wFHoew5V9I

We are interested in what is automatable and where the agentic ceiling is currently and how to push that up in all areas: https://t.co/WmTDjmNyV4

There is more for you to explore and a lot more coming in terms of how you will be able to navigate business in an optimal way in your chosen surface area; whether you are hanging in grokbot, dots, muse, claude, terminal, chat, or whatever is coming up in this exciting time. 

We have a lot of data to collect, clean up and help agents navigate the vast landscape emerging functionality the entire startup ecosystem has to offer. 

Come join us getting your vendor in, ranked or that access pattern you have wanted or getting the data more accurate in terms of which vendor is best for a process or steps. Or open a module of something that currently cost money that could be free. 

Also come play in our discord for founders and join the chaos (we can solve each others issues including fund raising tips from me personally): https://t.co/AmBtzFy0Bz 

It's time to lift all the boats in the harbor and I'm extremely excited as to what the community of hackers and painters will hack into the repo, what asks they will have and whether we can shift normalization of processes globally, gov agentic interfaces and have common repo for founders that grows over time. I expect a lot of experimentation along the way, bugs and upside...

I appreciate our backers having faith in us as well from @ycombinator with @garrytan to @immad doing a sizable check (congrats on $1bn rev homie) to @darbyw (congrats on Stripe buying @clerkyinc), @drewhouston form @Dropbox and also @pioneer_fund @tomerlondon cto @GustoHQ and hopefully this is 'boring' and complex enough for Charlie Songhurst :> @delingpole @Liquid2V @ivolo from @segment @ryanpowe @sonicaghi of @kong @DellyTamer+ other supporters (@michaelwfrank, Fundamental ventures and if I missed you sorry moving fast!). 

[And don't worry, all vendor rankings are open scoring methods so no favors are being done if someone backed us and is a vendor they have to compete with how agentic and automatable they are just like anyone else.]

PS: we have bugs and many quality upgrades to make but thought better to go out early and fix as a community. 

PPS: we have other stuff to launch we just thought this was a great place to start and have 200 PRs coming out pretty soon but I still want to know what is broken or doesnt make sense or inaccurate. 

Special thanks to current and past team members for getting us here and all the experiments we did you know who you are.

text:
So a16z Crypto becomes a16z Frontier

Saw a lot of debate yesterday about whether this is good or bad news for the crypto industry

I'm gonna go with "bad news". Make no mistake here, a16z has always been a top notch fund and one of the pioneers of crypto investing

The fact that they are expanding "beyond crypto" is another very bad sign for the industry = and as a crypto guy I am interpreting this as negative news because it explicitly mentions their fund will focus on "other investments". Btw I've listened to the interview with Chris Dixon, one of their key investment partners. Guess what, he barely mentioned crypto at all during this interview, it's all AI this, AI that

[Btw Kyle Samani leaving Multicoin and saying "maybe blockchain is just a ledger after all" was an early warning too]

Now a16z doing this "expansion" is yet another testament to the fact that this industry is not serious, not sustainable and becoming less and less profitable by the day, therefore it's only natural they're moving into AI (or rather AI+crypto combo)

When I said it was bad news, I didn't necessarily mean it was bad news for everyone. It's bad news for "airdrop enthusiasts" in particular

a16z was among the VCs backing some of your favorite projects with the sickest airdrops in this industry's history: dydx, Optimism, LZ, Aptos, Jito, etc (just look at the distribution figures)

Notice how most of these huge airdrops came from the L1/L2 infra meta, now many of these pjs are either dead or built out. The days of helicopter money are behind us and are likely never coming back. Why? Because there's nothing interesting for the big VCs to invest in. Now only small VCs are active, but the projects they invest in are nothing to write home about

When it comes to big VCs, let's dig deeper: when was the last time Paradigm invested in a fresh new crypto project? When was the last time Polychain invested in a crypto project? Do you see where this is going? 

Pretty sure those funds have also shifted their focus away from crypto-only (fully or partially), they just haven't announced it publicly

Here's the most important question: why were we making money from airdrops in this industry in the first place? Because VCs like a16z, Paradigm, Polychain, Multicoin enabled us to do so. Let's just admit it - most of the money we made was thanks to these funds in particular

You may not have realized this yet, but the easy times are slowly coming to an end

quoted_text:
交易Robinhood 链的逻辑只有一个，你相信它有第二波。

我信的原因有三个：
1、钱没走。钱没走。DeFi TVL 还在 10 亿美元上下，稳定币也有 10 亿。其中相当一部分是 Earn 这类产品带过来的，用户可能都不知道自己的钱已经在链上了。这笔钱现在是躺着的，但总会有契机把它叫醒。
2、官方在加码。这几天Vlad 亲自出来表态，联络社区。官方账号点名欢迎 Metric，T. Rowe 在研究 ETF 上链，27 号还有财报。Robinhood 并不想看着自己的链凉掉。
3、新链都有第二波。Base 是这样，Hyperliquid 也是这样，先冲一轮，冷下来，然后再起一轮。直接死掉也太对不起SEC给批的创新豁免了。

认同上面这个，然后往下想，那第二波起来，炒的会是什么？

看 Vlad 怎么说就知道了。他前两天的原话是：这条链是给代币化的真实资产，和人们真正想用的应用准备的。好的资产，好的开发者，再接进几千万人在用的 Robinhood App。

整段话没提一个 meme。

再看官方这周点名的 Metric，一个专门给股票代币做流动性的 DEX。官方想要的东西已经很明白了：股票上链之后，能交易，能借贷，能理财，能被 App 用户直接用上。

meme 是这条链用来冷启动的，不是它的目的地。

所以我对第二波的判断是：会来，但主角会换。至少我觉得不是 robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571 ，至少它不再是第一beta。第一波吃的是新链加免费 Gas 加 meme 的红利，第二波要看股票资产和收益。

author: binji_x
quoted_text:
Ethereum would not be Ethereum without Justin Drake.

JD has recruited most of crypto's top developers and researchers (including @dankrad). He has brought on most of the people you see and many you don't, people who could work anywhere else but chose to work silently for Ethereum and its infinitely large vision. He's the reason Post Quantum Ethereum even exists. He made @leanEthereum real. When you talk about growth, lean is setting a 100x vision for the network unlike anything else. Formal Verification of blockchains is the hot kid on the block now in crypto; who led key work that got it funded at scale? JD. Proving matters beyond blockchains; it might even be relevant for us to trust AI, and real-time proving has been pushed forward by many years because of JD.

His contributions have led to civilizational-level tools  that extend far beyond blockchains; he's helped answer questions like: how do we protect information + check that software does what it promises + verify computation without simply trusting whoever runs it. That is literally civilizational-grade infrastructure.

And now let's think about what kind of research culture we want Ethereum to have. 

We need people willing to put ambitious proposals and ideas in public, attach their name to them, and let everyone take them apart. Does that put Justin above criticism? Hell no. Please challenge his assumptions.  Knowing him, I am sure he would appreciate it. Criticize his communications too because maybe things could have been said better. 

BUT

Attacking his character is just wrong, and I cannot defend that in the slightest. If every controversial claim becomes a debate on whether someone has ever contributed anything, we end up teaching the next generation to keep their thoughts to themselves, and that is a bigger problem than anything else.

“Ethereum is in the business of disagreeing while staying together” has to mean something when we actually disagree.

You can think @drakefjustin is wrong and still be very glad that Ethereum has him. I certainly am.

Now imagine a wider outage affecting several essential services at once.

You’re buying groceries, but the checkout can’t process your card.

You try withdrawing cash, but the ATM is offline.

Your rent is due, but your banking app won’t load.

You need medication, but the pharmacy can’t access your prescription.

You arrive for surgery, but the hospital’s systems are down.

You’re stranded at the airport because your airline can’t check you in.

You log in for work, but your company’s systems are locked.

You try calling your family, but the mobile network is down.

These are ALL possible consequences of major outages.

Your own phone or laptop doesn’t have to be hacked for you to feel the impact.

The services you depend on just have to stop working.

Prepare while everything still works.

text:
坑 1：等想清楚了再出发

我是怎么踩的：

18 岁，我想创业想疯了。

写了无数个 idea，做了无数份规划，每天都觉得“再准备准备就可以开始了”。

结果整整一年，一个都没做。

不是没想法，是怕。怕失败，怕丢人，怕选错。

直到 19 岁，一个朋友推了我一把，我才真正开始。

回头看，那一年写的所有规划，后来没有一份用上了。真正教会我东西的，是出发之后的每一次失败。

怎么避：

别等“想清楚”。创业这件事，你在岸上永远想不清楚，只有下水了才知道水多深。

先做一个最小的版本，哪怕很丑，哪怕只有几个用户。

早一年出发，你就比别人多一年犯错的机会。而犯错，是创业唯一的学费。

我最大的优势不是聪明，是比大多数人早了 10 年开始交学费。

text:
Looks like Lighter is adding SPAN-style portfolio margin, set to launch with vanilla options

Today Lighter calculates each position's margin on its own and adds them up. On the Q3 investor call, @vnovakovski said the new engine looks at spot, perps and options on the same asset together and asks "what the worst realistic loss would be if the market moved sharply." It revalues the book across moves in price and implied vol. That's the logic of SPAN, the method CME uses for futures and options

Without portfolio margin, an options market maker posts margin on both legs: the options it sells, as if they were naked, and the perps that hedge them. Margined together, the two legs have a smaller worst case, and as Vlad put it, a smaller worst case means less margin. The market maker could then quote tighter and deeper, and a trader buying a single call gets those quotes too

For a regular trader this would make hedging pay. Selling calls on ETH you already hold stops tying up margin like a naked short. Buying a put under a long perp lowers your margin and moves your liquidation further away, instead of only costing premium

Institutions compare venues on how much capital a book ties up there. At CME, options desks are already margined on scenarios, and Vlad said professional trading shops run options books this way. On a venue that margins every leg alone, the same hedged book ties up several times the capital, so a desk keeps its size elsewhere. With SPAN-style margin, Lighter would charge a book for the risk it actually carries, the way CME does, and that's what it would take for the firms that dominate options to trade there once Lighter is live in the US

author: yukonresearch
quoted_text:
HashSmash Breakthrough

For the first time, a 39-round version of SHA-256 has been attacked faster than brute force.

Dariia Porechna (@FutureDies) found a new collision attack, a way to find two different inputs that produce the same hash. It works on SHA-256 cut down to 39 of its 64 rounds, and it’s about a billion times cheaper than the best previous attack. Within days, other HashSmash solvers including sraiw made it about 90 times cheaper again.

Full SHA-256, which secures Bitcoin, is still safe. Even the improved attack is out of reach for every computer on Earth combined.

Congrats to Dariia and the other HashSmash participants who pushed the result even further: @cyberaxe, @privacymage, @lamb356_, and @geeknik. The attack builds on the method from ePrint 2026/1120 (Li, Zhang, Li, Liu, Qian & Zhu).
