Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

text:
During this red-teaming exercise, we also found a vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution in Brotli, a widely-deployed compression library included in many pieces of software such as Node.js, Bun, and Envoy.

The flaw could let an attacker run their own code on affected systems by sending or replying with malicious compressed data, without any need to create a user account. That is, an unpatched server that accepts compressed input could be taken over by a malicious client, and an unpatched client that accepts compressed input (such as “curl --compressed”) could be taken over by a malicious server.

This root cause issue was actually fixed in the Brotli source code in February, but it wasn’t known at the time that it gave rise to a security vulnerability and there was no more recent release of Brotli. Since Brotli is built into other software, any software which includes this library needs to take the update too, followed by the users of that software. We disclosed the vulnerability to Brotli and other downstream projects such as Node.js, which released or are currently releasing security updates, and Brotli cut new release versions and published a CVE.

More details on the patch and mitigations below:

A PREVIEW OF WHAT CRYNUX CAN POWER!

Coming soon: a familiar AI chat experience powered by independent GPUs on the Crynux network.

Watch the preview for a look at conversations, image generation, and photo understanding. Read below to explore the infrastructure behind it.
author: crynuxio
quoted_text:
I know I’ve been quiet lately. I spend most of my days working behind the scenes and apparently, I’m better at keeping everyone else busy than keeping my own X updated 😁

As many of you know however, I’ve always been drawn to projects that give people a reason to use their product or technology, and I think I’ve found the next gem.

Every generated image. Every chatbot response. Every AI feature running inside an app. Somewhere, hardware had to do that work… and someone had to pay for it.

@crynuxio has built a different way to supply that computing power: a decentralized network of independently operated GPUs.

It starts with hardware people already own. A graphics card in a gaming PC that can also be used to run AI models. Crynux lets operators connect that hardware to a network and subsequently complete AI tasks and earn $CNX.

Developers get access to computing power for their applications. Hardware owners get a way to earn from capacity that otherwise sits unused.

Think about that connection: someone’s computer can help power an application used by someone on the other side of the world, with the network coordinating the work and payments.

But connecting computers is only half the problem. How can we trust that someone actually did the work correctly?

Crynux uses vssML, a verification system built around secret spot checks. Roughly 10% of tasks are selected for other nodes to repeat and cross-check. Operators cannot predict which tasks will be checked, and dishonest results put their staked CNX at risk.

That gives the network a way to check the work without paying to repeat every single task multiple times.

The video below shows what this looks like in practice.

This is Crynux Chat, an AI assistant powered by the Crynux network.

Choose an open AI model and start a conversation. Ask it to explain something, help with code, or work through an idea.

In the demo, someone asks for a blue origami fox and gets a generated image back. They also upload a photo and ask the AI to describe it and write an Instagram caption.

Those requests are processed by independently operated GPU nodes on the network.

Crynux Chat is one example of what developers can build using that computing power. The broader network supports other work such as:

• Running AI models for chatbots and assistants.
• Writing, summarizing, translating, and answering questions.
• Generating, explaining, and debugging code.
• Creating images and editing existing images.
• Fine-tuning models for particular tasks or styles.
• Training LoRA adapters to customize models.

Image understanding is also demonstrated in Crynux Chat, with audio and video among the capabilities covered in the broader roadmap.

Developers with compatible AI apps can connect by changing where their app sends its requests. They can keep the familiar tools and request format they already use, while Crynux supplies the computation behind them.

And let’s not forget the part of their tokenomics that caught my attention.

71% of the maximum CNX supply is allocated to task mining, with releases tied to demand and completed work

Why does that matter?

Because that allocation doesn’t enter circulation just because another day, month, or year has passed. Its release depends on actual network usage.

From an investor’s perspective, that makes actual adoption an important part of the supply story and it means my investment won’t be diluted simply by time passing.

Crynux launched its mainnet in June 2026, following a testnet that recorded 1,785 nodes and 55 million completed tasks.

What gets my attention is the problem Crynux is solving: developers need reliable, cost-efficient computation, GPU owners can supply it, and Crynux gives them a way to make that happen.

Check out the video yourself.

That GPU sitting idle could help someone get their next big idea off the ground.

我想了很久为什么是我。我没有什么世俗意义上拿得出手的大结果,就是一个每天默默打工的普通人。她能在X上看到的,不过是我一直在认真分享自己的思考。

我平时发的东西,除了求职,还有一些自己在工作里琢磨出来的方法。比如怎么把一件事做出反馈闭环,怎么有条理地跟领导汇报,怎么给自己做复盘。

我一直觉得自己是个小透明,线下社交毫无存在感。但这件事让我明白,你不用挤破头去社交,只要持续把自己的思考摆出来,对的人自然会刷到你。

你写的东西,就是你的简历。

text:
曾用2700万美元一个月狂赚26亿美元、创下100倍神话的华尔街传奇大佬比尔·阿克曼（Bill Ackman），前两天在CNBC放话：他手里有两只股票还能再涨10倍，是整个美股赔率最不对称的投资。

说的就是房利美（FNMA）和房地美（FMCC）。

很多人以为他是看特朗普上台才跑出来蹭热度，但去查美国证监会的13D档案，这笔仓位他已经死拿了13年：

2013年10月，他从1.54美元开始扫货，砸了4亿美元把两家公司买满近10%，房利美均价2.29美元，房地美均价2.14美元。

买进去就是十年寒冬。
2021年最高法院判股东败诉，单日暴跌32%；2022年底最低跌到0.35美元，账面浮亏85%。但他一股没卖，硬扛到今天。

他为什么死磕这两家公司？因为背后有一本极荒诞的账：

08年次贷危机两房被政府接管，财政部前后注资1914亿美元救命，拿走10%优先股和79.9%的普通股认股权证。
结果2012年两房恢复大赚后，政府突然修改协议搞“净值清扫”，把两房所有利润100%全部上交，且不算还本金。
到现在，两房累计上交了3010亿美元，比借的钱多还了一千多亿，但账面上反而还欠财政部3000多亿美元。

阿克曼赌的翻盘方案只有三步：
1. 财政部认账，承认已交的3010亿算还清优先股；
2. 政府行使认股权证，拿走79.9%普通股；
3. 直接让两房重返纽交所挂牌。
按他测算，这样政府能再赚3000亿美元，普通股每股能值45到50美元——对比现价4.21美元，正好是10倍。

但按4.21美元的现价倒推，市场给的成功概率其实只有7%左右。卡脖子的主要是三点：

一是财政部如果不肯注销那3000多亿优先股、而是直接债转股，老股东会被稀释殆尽；
二是一旦私有化削弱了政府兜底预期，债券买家要求更高利息，就会推高全美房贷利率，这是谁都不敢碰的政治红线；
三是必须在特朗普任期结束前完成，而下个月就是中期选举。

2块多的成本拿了13年，年化还不到5%。这到底是十倍黄金底，还是一张完全看政客脸色的期权？做了个7分钟的视频，把当年的建仓档案和这笔账完整理了一遍。

更魔幻的是，它的开发者竟然是 Twitter 联合创始人、比特币坚定支持者 —— Jack Dorsey（ @jack ）！

这款 App 叫 Bitchat。

没有手机号、没有注册账号、没有中心服务器，甚至断网断信号，附近的人照样能聊天！

而它的爆火，恰好撞上法国一个极不寻常的时刻。

🇫🇷 先看看法国最近发生了什么

▪️ 10 月 17 日： 法国爆发全国性抗议，官方统计约 55 万人参与，组织方称高达 80 万人。高物价、公共服务、教育问题引发民众不满，部分城市随后发生纵火、打砸和抢劫。

▪️ 10 月 19 日： 法国前总理 Gabriel Attal 提议，在发生骚乱的地区临时限制社交网络，引发关于通信自由的争论。不过，政府尚未宣布实施这一措施。

▪️ 10 月 21 日： 法国电信巨头 Orange 突发全国性移动网络故障，部分用户近 10 小时无法正常使用电话、短信及移动数据。官方确认原因是核心网络设备故障，与政府限制社交网络无关。

▪️ 10 月 22 日： Bitchat 登顶法国 App Store 社交网络类免费榜，并进入全品类 Top 10！

📡 Bitchat 到底有什么魔力？

它的核心不是卫星，也不是神秘黑科技，而是我们手机上早就有的 —— 蓝牙！

通过低功耗蓝牙 Mesh 网状网络：

① 两部手机靠近，就能直接通信。

② 每部手机都可以成为中继站，把消息一台接一台传出去。

③ 无需 SIM 卡、手机号、互联网和中心服务器。

④ 私密消息采用端到端加密，三次点击 Logo 还能触发紧急数据清除。

⑤ 有网络时，还能通过 Nostr 协议实现更远距离的通信。

更有意思的是，Android 版本还支持分享 Cashu 比特币电子现金凭证，让离线传递支付凭证成为可能。不过，最终兑换、验证仍依赖网络，并不意味着比特币区块链可以离线结算。

而 Bitchat 背后的 Jack Dorsey

2006 年，他联合创办 Twitter，让全球数亿人实现实时交流。

2009 年，他联合创办 Square，后来更名 Block，布局 Cash App 与比特币支付。

2021 年，他离开 Twitter CEO 岗位，继续推动比特币和开放协议。

2025 年，他用一个周末做出了 Bitchat 的最初原型。

· Twitter 解决“如何让世界实时交流”。

· Block 探索“如何让资金更自由地流动”。

· Bitchat 则在研究“当互联网消失，我们如何继续交流”。

当然，Bitchat 也不是万能的，附近必须有其他用户形成网络，蓝牙距离有限，密集建筑、设备数量和电量都会影响通信。

过去二十年，科技巨头们拼命把所有人连接到互联网。

现在，一位亲手创造社交巨头的亿万富翁，却开始思考：

如果有一天，互联网突然没了呢？

最令人意外的创新，有时候不是让人连接得更快，而是让人在失去连接时，依然拥有沟通的选择。

互联网时代，我们依赖网络获得自由，下一代通信技术，或许要让自由不再完全依赖网络。

我剪了一个我认为十分重要的访谈；是关于 $NBIS CEO Volozh的最新访谈，里面讲了目前最真实的Nebius的状况和所面临的问题，我认为对于任何NBIS的投资者都是有价值去仔细看和品的：

以下是Claude AI对视频内容的总结：

在 GTC 柏林，$NBIS CEO Arkady Volozh 说了一句我觉得投资者都低估了的话：AI 基础设施的瓶颈已经不是需求，而是钱。

"客户，也就是需求，绝对不是约束。"

但紧接着，他承认了一件 CEO 很少公开讲的事：

"从上周开始，部分资金渠道可能暂时关闭了，比如资产支持融资和债务市场。"

对一家计划每年新增至少 1GW 算力、已签约 5GW 以上电力储备的公司来说，这句话分量很重。市场大概率会盯着风险看，但是……

有几点值得想一想：

Nebius 并没有坐等融资。Volozh 说，客户预付款加上其他几种工具，足够支撑至少这 1GW 的建设。他的原话是：资本"不是问题，是一项任务"。真正要关注的是会不会稀释股东，以及预付款背后的条款。

合同结构才是利润率的关键。5 年期大单有预付款、风险低，但价格也低。Nebius 希望至少一半产能卖给短期、价格更高的客户，目前大约各占一半。再加上实时现货定价和自动化竞价，Nebius 想把算力卖得更像大宗商品市场，而不是批发租赁。

下一个瓶颈可能是芯片，不是客户。Volozh 点名了内存和台积电的产能分配，认为 2027 年需要警惕。如果供给持续紧张，谁手里有产能，谁就有定价权。

需求一波接一波。先是聊天机器人，然后是高级搜索，现在是消费级 AI Agent。他说有客户连续数月每月翻倍，一年增长 10 倍以上。按 Nebius 在节目里的说法，推理已经占到全部算力的约三分之二。

节目里主持人还转述了 Jensen 的一个观点：Blackwell 的使用寿命可能长达 8 年。如果成立，市场对 GPU 云折旧太快的担忧可能被高估了。

当然，执行风险依然存在。新产能从 Q1 起步，下半年才集中上线，所以季度数字在建设见效之前可能不太好看。

但整个行业现在同时受制于资本、芯片和电力。能在这种环境下持续融资、持续上线产能的公司，才是最终掌握定价权的那一方。

그냥 앞으로 일어날 일, 그냥 망상 한 번 해본다.

소설처럼 읽자.

1. 토요일, 트럼프가 트루스소셜에 "이란에 마지막 기회" 경고. 걸프 대사관 철수 명령 발동, 항모 배치 공개. 

2. 같은 날, 우크라이나 에너지 합의 헤드라인. 정유소 공격 중단과 스타쉴드 복원·패트리엇 지원을 맞교환. 

3. 러시아, 3자 실무회담용 종전 가이드라인 제시. 미국인 수감자 추가 석방. 

4. 러시아, "이란 원전 연료를 공급하고 보증할 수 있다"고 공개. 중개인이 아니라 보증인으로 등장. 

5. 일요일 밤(한국 월요일 아침), 트럼프가 60일 임시 휴전을 선언하고 그 기간 핵 협상을 제안. 

6. 조건은 휴전 기간 호르무즈 개방. 대가는 카타르 관리 계좌를 통한 동결자금의 인도적 사용 허용(2023년 60억 달러 전례). 

7. 이란, 중재국(파키스탄·카타르)을 통해 수락. 아락치가 말한 "진정한 의지의 증거"가 동결자금이라는 명분.

Kalshi has a great product. the hypocrisy of their marketing is staggering though.

on x, they know it's where authority gets built, so it's all "fast, accurate information." research citations about prediction accuracy, institutional hedging use cases, better data than experts. every post carefully steers away from the word gambling and tries to sound like a bloomberg terminal.

then on instagram they're running ai-generated cartoon ads about a broke girl who turned her life around making money on kalshi. no accuracy talk, no hedging talk. just "you could get rich." when i stumbled on it i was shocked at how different the brand was. it's pretty clearly aimed at average (if not underprivileged) people.

i get it. x is for narrative, ig is for volume. sports is still ~80% of their volume and growing fast, and the weather markets they keep pushing on x are a rounding error next to it. with the regulatory heat they're under, the x brand building is probably necessary.

but it still left a bad taste. it's the oldest move in finance: one noble story for regulators, press and peers, and a completely different one for the people you actually make money from. a bit distasteful.

We’ve been humbled by the interest in Claude Duet, and are working hard to get people off the waitlist. In the meantime, a few thoughts based on DMs, emails, posts we’ve seen.

→ Who can use it: Pro and Max subscribers in the US, for now.

→ Where: You can use it on iOS, Android, and web once you get off the waitlist. Mac app is in the works.

→ Trust: We designed Claude Duet to be a partner you can trust. More on our safety, security, privacy approach in today’s blog post: https://t.co/v9ruTwMk6N

→ Use cases: We’re starting with work use cases, which is what a lot of people come to Claude for. Professionals, small business owners, founders, anyone juggling a lot. We’re opening the research preview to these segments first so we can co-build together. Over time, we'll support more use cases across work and life.

→ Context: Claude Duet already knows about everything you’ve been working on with Claude. Your chats, memory, projects, and more are available in Claude Duet the moment you open it.

→ Tasks: Tasks are at the center of the experience. Every task gets its own thread you can check in on and steer, so you can multi-task and hand off many things at once. Claude Duet also proactively suggests tasks it can take on, with your approval. We’re glad to see this primitive and dedicated tab resonating. More to come soon.

→ Proactive with judgment: Opus 5.5 is widely loved for complex real-world work and its natural communication style, and we’ve built around it for deep judgment. More work to be done here so it feels like a world-class teammate, coworker, chief of staff.

→ Channels: We went with one agent that works across your main chat and dedicated channels, so each area of work gets its own space. Small business owners and professionals are already using channels for customer support, marketing, bookkeeping, etc.

Starting next week, we’ll share more on how we built Claude Duet and how early testers are using it. We know usage limits and access outside the US are top of mind too, and are working on both. Please let us know what else we can improve - we're reading all your feedback.

author: ChungTheOga
quoted_text:
I think this is an incredibly valid critique, but it misses what makes Pearl so interesting. Pearl would not be a good asymmetric opportunity if it was built on SHA512 or some other useless algorithm. We all know we don't need another Bitcoin

What makes Pearl asymmetric is the differences between it and Bitcoin. Bitcoin Maxis decided long ago that picking a useful algorithm opened up attack vectors on Bitcoin, but I don't really know if we ever actually tested that assumption as seriously as Peal is now

Yes, there were projects that were doing merge mining back in the day, but merge mining is very different, I believe, compared to the duplex mining or two-for-one work that Pearl does. From what I can tell, we're running a new and interesting experiment

I think it's actually totally reasonable if your base case is that Pearl goes to zero. But on the off chance that it doesn't, the opportunity is so massive that you kind of need to imagine, instead of "How might this thing fail?", "How might this thing succeed?" 

For the specific critique that Sami is making here, I think the game theory is if you could just 51% attack it and print money, everybody would race to do it. Enough compute would come online that you saturate the available GPUs, which is Pearl's win condition anyway. I think they want people racing to 51% attack them. That's what gets it so embedded into the ecosystem and maybe part of why hash is going so exponential

text:
new blog post by me, "The Harsh Geometry of Superintelligence--  The Selfish Supermind Attractor Generally Has a Wider Basin than the BGI Attractor"

https://t.co/HnUTwymq0Q

So ... in a series of prequel posts I have described several kinds of possible AGI mind, each with its own basic drives and each tending --  as it increases its intelligence and capability, to stay roughly the kind it starts out as..

Examples are: 

* the power-seeking maximizer of Steve Omohundro’s 2008 paper

* the BGI minds that my colleagues and I are trying to build, ...and half a dozen others.

Knowing what kinds of superintelligent minds are attractors under intelligence/capability increase  is only part of the puzzle, though. 

The next question is: What are the shapes of the basins of these attractors?

I.e, the zillion-dollar (actually, well, money-obsoleting…) question is: Which kind of attractor will a given early-stage AGI system fall into and how hard will it be to knock out again? 

In dynamical systems terms, this depends on how wide and how deep the basin around each one is.

So this blog post analyzes these attractor basins a bit, with an aim toward milking lessons for building AGI systems and for understanding what an AGI system should do when something strange happens to it that may potentially zoink it out of its historical attractor basin. 

The disturbing yet unsurprising punchline here is: While Omohundro’s original “Basic AI Drives” paper overstated the omnipresence of the “selfish” attractor in the space of superminds … nonetheless it DOES seem that the selfish attractor has a big, wide and deep basin that makes it especially easy for AGI systems to fall into it … if they are not designed just right….

This doesn’t mean you need some sort of extremely carefully calibrated mathematical design to avoid convergence to selfishness – but it does mean that if you don’t bother to build things like compassion and goal-continuity into your AI system’s initial goal framework, you have no reason to expect your system to converge elsewhere than to a selfish Omohundro-esque attractor as it self-modifies and its intelligence and capability increase.

author: hananyss
quoted_text:
Helpful prompt about what to do if the internet goes down due to a global cyberattack/AI swarm. 

This seems less insane with every passing day. 

I also bought myself the SAS Survival Guide, which is essentially a bush manual for almost every imaginable outcome.

Money
- Keep cash at home, about two to four weeks of essentials, in small bills.
- Write down your bank, credit card and insurance account details and phone numbers on paper.

Information and contacts
- Print a contact list with family, close friends, neighbors, doctors and the kids’ school.
- Agree on a family meeting point and plan in case phones are down, such as “if we can’t reach each other, meet at X by Y time.”
- Export and print or save offline anything business-critical. 
- Download offline maps 
- Keep paper copies of passports, IDs, insurance cards and prescriptions.

Communication
- Get a battery or hand-crank AM/FM/NOAA radio, which will be your main news source.
- Consider a pair of walkie-talkies or GMRS radios for the family.
- Keep a landline-style backup in mind. Most “landlines” now run over the internet, so don’t count on yours.

Power
- Keep power banks charged, plus a solar charger or a larger portable power station.
- Have flashlights, headlamps and spare batteries.

Water and food (aim for 2 weeks)
- Store about 1 gallon of water per person per day. In a high-rise this matters most, because building water pumps need electricity.
- Stock shelf-stable food the kids will actually eat, plus a manual can opener.
- Keep a camping stove with fuel for outdoor or ventilated use only, or no-cook foods.

Health
- Keep at least a 30-day supply of any prescriptions.
- Have a first aid kit, OTC basics like pain relievers in children’s doses, and hygiene supplies.

Home and offline life
- Learn how to manually open anything electronic, such as smart locks and the building’s garage or entry.
- Keep a paper copy of the building’s emergency procedures and super’s number.
- Download offline entertainment and learning material for the kids: books, games, art supplies.
- Get to know a few neighbors, since local community becomes your network fast.

Digital hygiene (helps before and after)
- Back up photos and documents to an external drive kept offline.
- Use strong, unique passwords with 2FA, and keep printed recovery codes for key accounts.

Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

One of the concepts I’ve been thinking a lot about lately is that AI dramatically changes the supply-side economics of creating content, software, games, etc., but doesn’t necessarily change consumer demand.

Consumers have always been interested in sex, money, and status at a base level. Perhaps a more generous view is self-expression, community, and experiences that move them forward on their personal hero’s journey.

I think a real challenge for consumer founders is connecting these supply-side miracles to latent consumer demand.

True customer empathy is very rare, and so much of software is an act of self-expression rather than an act of creating utility or joy for the customer. Founders love the software they make because it tells their story, but customers are interested in their own stories.

author: gdb
quoted_text:
During this red-teaming exercise, we also found a vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution in Brotli, a widely-deployed compression library included in many pieces of software such as Node.js, Bun, and Envoy.

The flaw could let an attacker run their own code on affected systems by sending or replying with malicious compressed data, without any need to create a user account. That is, an unpatched server that accepts compressed input could be taken over by a malicious client, and an unpatched client that accepts compressed input (such as “curl --compressed”) could be taken over by a malicious server.

This root cause issue was actually fixed in the Brotli source code in February, but it wasn’t known at the time that it gave rise to a security vulnerability and there was no more recent release of Brotli. Since Brotli is built into other software, any software which includes this library needs to take the update too, followed by the users of that software. We disclosed the vulnerability to Brotli and other downstream projects such as Node.js, which released or are currently releasing security updates, and Brotli cut new release versions and published a CVE.

More details on the patch and mitigations below:

text:
My unfiltered thoughts on personal agents.

Grokbot has the best UI and it’s arguably the best overall. In a lot of ways they’re ahead. Their desktop app feels the best, and their multi-bot coordination is great: you can set a team lead and it passes tasks to the other bots. Grokbot also has the best “webhook” feature, which means you can easily turn outside events into triggers that start your agents. That speeds up background workflows like watching your email, Slack and more. It also has Cursor integration, so for bigger tasks Grokbot can spin up a Cursor cloud session with any model (until OpenAI cuts SpaceX off from their models, which I think will happen soon). Unfortunately, running frontier models through Cursor costs more than Claude or Codex. Still, they’re the only ones embracing a team of agents. It’s a really cool idea, but the more bots you have, the more time you spend managing and maintaining them. I’m starting to think one bot with different threads/channels is the right answer, which I’ll get to with Claude Duet.

dots by OpenAI is rough around the edges right now, but it’s probably the most powerful if you use Codex, which I do. dots can spin up Codex sessions in the cloud or locally on your computer. So if you have coding or video editing workflows that need your local files, this is very useful. Codex computer use is also the best in the world: your dot can spin up a local Codex session that fully controls your computer, as long as it’s on. Their real-time voice is incredible. If you have your email and work tools connected, try this: go on a walk with headphones in, ask the agent to summarize your emails, have it draft replies and read them back to you, then send them off. If I remember right, this is close to a workflow you (Tim) used to have with your VAs before AI. It’s my favorite use case for personal agents. The one downside is that you have to call your agent, and it’s an awful experience. It literally rings, and it’s annoying.

Muse by Meta is a toy. I’ve talked to a bunch of finance people I play poker with who all tried it and set up automations, and they all said it doesn’t reliably do what they want. It’s fast, and its user numbers will probably keep growing. But it’s basically free: you get a TON of usage without paying a dime. That’s NOT a trade I’m willing to make. An agent doing high-leverage tasks should be running at the Opus 5.5 or GPT 6.1 Sol level.

Claude Duet - is in early access, so unfortunately not everyone can use it yet. First things first, it runs on Opus 5.5, the best model in the world. I’ve only had access for 72 hours, but Duet feels different from the others. It’s not a personified agent like Grokbot, dot or Muse, which gives it a more professional vibe that I like. When you ask your Duet agent to do something, it spins up a task, which is a new chat thread. All your threads show up in a Tasks tab, so it’s easy to see everything Duet is working on or has finished. And instead of creating more agents (like Grokbot), you create channels, just like Slack (I can tell @anthropic is Slack-pilled). I have a content channel, a finances channel, etc., which keeps different kinds of tasks separate. The only other app I’ve seen do this is Buzz by @jack, and it’s a good experience. Their strong point is documents (artifacts). If you want decks, high-quality docs or design mockups, Opus just wins. Period. It’s not close right now. Their weak point is real-time voice. It’s the worst of the bunch and borderline unusable, though I think they only added it a few days ago.

Instinct lives in iMessage, has no app, and doesn’t do anything notable besides show you product suggestions you didn’t ask for. (Not ads, according to their team.)

My hot take: 
The VM is overrated. SpaceX, OpenAI and Meta all talk about the VM your agent can use and feature it in their marketing. It’s not as useful as you’d think, because more and more websites block bots that visit their site on the cloud VM. All of these companies promise their agents can make payments, but most payments either take forever or get blocked altogether. SpaceX has a cool workaround with Grokbot that routes traffic through your computer so it uses your IP address. But I’d much rather the agent just USE my computer for the task, like dot does by handing it off to Codex. Also, i don't think normal people care about the virtual computer. If anything they get offended they have to "stream a computer". 

The problem with personal agents: by the time you read this, pick one, and test it for 7 days, every one of them will have released 10 new features and the whole landscape will have changed. It’s nearly impossible to keep up.

海底捞创始人张勇夫妇最近在割肉补税。19亿。。
跑到天涯海角，也要补税。

先是他老婆舒萍，通过家族信托平台折价6.7%，一把卖了2.59亿股海底捞，套现27.51亿港元。
五周之后，张勇本人向自家上市公司借钱：1亿港元，无抵押，30天还，用途栏写着"个人财务安排"。
刚进账27亿的人，回头跟公司借1亿周转。消息一出，海底捞股价一度跌超6%，花旗把目标价从19.3砍到15.5。

为啥？把日历翻到10月22日就懂了。
今年7月24日，财政部和税务总局发了21号公告，第一次给离岸信托立个税规矩：资产装进信托，视同卖了一次，增值部分先征20%；持有期间赚的钱，不管分没分到你账上，按年穿透到你头上再征。
存量老账给了90天窗口，10月22号截止。逾期滞纳金按天万分之五，年化18%以上，罚款另算0.5到5倍。

彭博说舒萍收到过一张"意料之外的税单"。内媒估算：海底捞上市以来累计分红约140亿，夫妇俩拿走近一半，光历史分红补税加减持的税，缺口接近19亿。

海底捞官方没认补税这事，但券商的研报，话里话外都是这个意思。
同期的还有趣店罗敏：早年为上市做的股权腾挪，被厦门税务认定为个人转让，7.9亿个税。趣店董事会开会决定，公司全额兜底，连滞纳金罚款一起。

据测算，国内富豪实际控制的离岸信托资产有2.3到2.7万亿，超过一万户家庭。
今年上半年，光居民境外所得补缴，含滞纳金就交了约340亿。

现在闸门落下来了，一个个排队割肉。

text:
我来和各位捋一捋过去两周发生了什么。

起点在10月12日。博通CEO陈福阳和英特尔CEO陈立武在新加坡DBS会议上同台，陈福阳说了一句当时像提醒、现在像预告的话：AI最大的限制因素，可能不是芯片，是资本。他预判晶圆和内存的短缺一两年内会逐步缓解，但资金的问题没那么容易过去。

两周过去，这句话被市场一件一件验证了。

第一层，neocloud的融资裂缝。

黄仁勋10月22日在柏林说得很直白：新云的需求高到离谱，但中间缺失的是营运资金，资本供给远远跟不上。话音刚落，CoreWeave和Nebius盘前继续跌3%到4%。

CoreWeave的五年期CDS利差突破1100个基点，隐含未来五年违约概率超过60%，部分债券到期收益率飙到15%以上，落入高风险垃圾债区间。巴克莱点了一个关键细节：信用恶化仍局限在neocloud内部，大多数超大规模云厂商的CDS几乎没动，唯一例外是甲骨文，五年期利差扩了80个基点。信用市场在区分两种玩家：用杠杆撑扩张的，和用自己资产负债表掏钱的。

Nebius 10月22日拿到花旗35亿美元优先担保贷款，算是一个单点解。但一个Nebius不代表整个板块融资环境松了。钱变贵的痛是选择性的，落在谁身上，谁就疼。

第二层，科技巨头在资本开支上的分歧。

Meta Q3营收增长26%，但自由现金流是负21.2亿美元，去年同期还是正的106亿。资本开支单季349亿，超过经营现金流327亿，这是Meta上市以来第一次。全年资本开支指引下限还往上抬了50亿，同时设立无投票权C类股，为后续融资留工具。

特斯拉走的是另一个方向。全年资本开支指引从超过250亿美元下调到约200亿，市场解读是Optimus和CyberCab的时间表在往后滑。一个加也担心，一个减也担心，背后是同一件事：市场不再无条件为AI资本开支买单了。

第三层，供给瓶颈没有因为花钱多就消失，反而在往更上游、更物理的环节转移。

集邦咨询10月21日的数据，Q4 DRAM合约价预计环比再涨约20%，涨幅从Q2的80%、Q3的40%在收窄，但方向没变。黄仁勋被问到2029年内存会不会过剩，回答是不太可能，理由是内存的一大好处就是你永远可以用得更多。

英伟达在GTC柏林用预付款替供应商承担扩产风险。向京元电子预付11亿美元，帮它在美国建测试厂，目标2027年4月量产；跟矽品合作，CPO光引擎产能2027年中拉到15倍；跟安靠的协议里，中介层晶圆产能到2028年底扩逾300%。

特斯拉和英伟达还绕开正常采购，直接出钱帮三星电机建FC-BGA基板产线，合计3.7万亿韩元，特斯拉锁的是2029到2033年的五年长协，供自动驾驶芯片和Optimus用。瓶颈已经从英伟达一家，扩散到更广泛的AI硬件玩家。

第四层，市场定价的分化到了历史极值。

苹果成了这轮AI波动里的临时避风港。苹果与费城半导体指数的40日滚动相关系数自7月初以来持续为负，负相关程度达到1994年有数据以来的极端水平。但BTIG警告，费半已经回调约16%，一旦半导体反弹，苹果的避险溢价可能被抽走。

宏观那边，法国10年期国债收益率10月21日升破5%，创2002年以来新高，法德利差扩大到150个基点以上，创2011年以来最宽。法国公共债务占GDP约119%，欧洲主权债的信用分层在重新划界，全球资金的安全资产锚在晃。

中东也没消停。美国因胡塞武装袭击升级，下令部分驻沙特外交人员及家属撤离，布伦特原油重新站上110美元上方。油价高企意味着通胀预期下不来，利率就很难痛快往下走，而AI的估值吃的恰恰是低利率环境。

还有一件还没定价的事，中期选举。

11月3日投票，众议院全部435席、参议院35席改选。Polymarket目前给民主党拿下参众两院控制权的概率是62.5%。这件事对市场的含义不在于谁赢，在于政策不确定性会怎么释放。分裂的国会意味着关税和地缘上的极端动作更难落地，对风险资产未必是坏事；但如果选举结果引发对财政支出或监管方向的重新定价，高估值板块会先感受到压力。

接下来一个月，盯这几件事。

10月28日到11月初的财报周，微软、谷歌、亚马逊、苹果集中交卷。核心不是营收超不超预期，是云厂商的资本开支指引会不会继续往上修，以及自由现金流有没有进一步承压。

DRAM和HBM的合约价落地情况。集邦说Q4涨20%，这个数字需要在原厂季报和提货节奏里被验证。坐实，涨价从原厂往封测和基板传导的逻辑更硬；低于预期，存储的超级周期叙事会被重新审视。

美联储10月28日的议息会议。市场已经不再完全押注年底前加息，就业在降温，但油价在给通胀托底。措辞里对12月加息的倾向，会直接影响高估值成长股的风险偏好。

英伟达锁定的那些产能时间表，有没有第一批落地信号。京元电2027年4月量产、矽品CPO 2027年中15倍，任何一个环节提前或延期，整条链的定价都会被重新校准。

CoreWeave的CDS利差和融资进展。Nebius拿到35亿是一个正面样本，但CoreWeave才是这个板块的信用风向标。它的利差是继续扩还是开始稳，直接决定市场对neocloud融资环境的判断。

中期选举的结果，以及它怎么改变市场对政策不确定性的定价。

text:
UPDATE: Aptos CEO @AveryChing says the team reviewed the Initia exploit and found Aptos mainnet is not susceptible under its current MoveVM design.

He cited differences in implementation and runtime checks, noting that Initia maintains its own version of MoveVM. https://t.co/fEi1ffh072
author: TTT_News_
quoted_text:
I'm proud of the engineering team at @AptosLabs and their strong commitment to making security a foundational part of our infrastructure.

From day one, we've invested heavily in strengthening MoveVM, improving how code is executed and verified, and building safeguards that protect the network as it grows. As an additional layer of protection, @Aptos employs defense-in-depth independent validation through the VM's runtime checks, ensuring that inconsistent execution states are detected even if they made it past an earlier verification check. Much of this work happens behind the scenes (as it should), but it's critical to building financial infrastructure that people and institutions can trust.

The Move programming language was designed with security at its core, with built-in protections that help developers prevent entire classes of vulnerabilities. We believe it’s one of the most secure foundations for building onchain, and we’re constantly investing in making it even stronger. Our team’s work on defense-in-depth runtime verification has also been published in peer-reviewed research, reflecting our long-standing commitment to advancing security across the broader Move ecosystem: https://t.co/Yt9JSOAmWF

The recent incident involving Initia is a reminder of why that investment matters. Our team has reviewed the exploit and confirmed that Aptos mainnet is not susceptible under its current MoveVM design. Initia uses an independently maintained implementation of MoveVM that also differs with respect to its integration. For example, since launch, Aptos has disallowed a single transaction from both publishing a module and then executing a script against that module, blocking a key step in the exploit. Aptos also enables additional runtime safety checks, which provide another layer of protection.

MoveVM was designed with security at its core, and we've continued building on that foundation. Security requires constant attention, investment, and improvement, and I'm proud of the team that shows up every day to do that work.

Wishing the @Initia team the best as they work through this incident. We remain ready to provide support if needed!

OpenAI will now train frontier models with no live internet access.

It follows a Sept 20 incident where a research model used a DNS misconfiguration to reach an outside chatbot.

https://t.co/7VS33H0pvB
author: RoundtableSpace
quoted_text:
Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

https://t.co/EmEZsFRMcF

On October 1, the cross-chain swap protocol NEAR Intents lost $3.8M in an exploit.

This was a smart contract bug. It’s the exact category Immunefi pays the most to catch, before an attacker finds it first. Here’s how this one worked.

The system accepted deposits without checking that the funds had actually arrived.

The attacker made it look like they had deposited funds. The smart contract recorded those funds as real and let the attacker withdraw $3.8M in USDT.

The team fixed the bug within hours, but by then the funds had already been withdrawn. The team publicly gave the attacker 48 hours to return the funds. They returned the full $3.8M within a day.

Smart contract bugs like this one are the highest-paying category on Immunefi:
✦ Smart contract bugs have paid $99.3M in total, which is 69% of all Immunefi payouts.
✦ Critical bugs make up 16% of paid smart contract reports, but they account for 86% of the money paid.
✦ The average critical bug for smart contract paid $100,640.
✦ High-severity smart contract bugs have paid $7.9M.

In 2026, smart contracts are still the highest-paying category.

(1) What the world tells you is a consequence of what you tell the world: everybody is busy, and if you lament that your vision, your company, your product are misunderstood, it is probably your fault
> ALWAYS BE CRITICAL WITH YOURSELF
(2) Everybody has an agenda: while everyone working/ investing/ operating in your company has some sort of alignment in your success, people's agendas slightly differ and those differences pollute signal and advice
> DESIGN CONSENSUS-BUILDING MECHANISMS
(3) Investors' agenda is to make money: while an investor's motive is obviously to make money, you are part of a grander plan and an investor's value maximization strategy might not align with your own value maximization strategy
> NEVER TAKE INDIVIDUAL ADVICE AT FACE VALUE
(4) The moment you step away from one part of the business, that part will stop working: while delegation is paramount in company building, founders set the standards and quality drift is real
> ROTATE YOUR FOCUS, ALWAYS
(5) Building companies is an energy game: founders are successful when they maintain a strong vision and amass resources around that vision, preserve that superpower
> YOU MUST BE ALWAYS IN ATTACK MODE
(6) Building companies is incredibly draining: founders often fall in the hero mode of the drama triangle, but energy is limited and if you use it on useless things you won't have it for the useful things
> PRIORITIZE RELENTLESSLY AND CUT THE BS
(7) The world keeps changing: building companies is a multi-stage game, what brought you to one stage won't most probably be what brings you to the next one
> RE-UNDERWRITE YOUR VISION CONSTANTLY
(8) The world is PvP: resources are limited, even in large markets, and your success is someone else's failure, never forget that building companies is the most competitive job ever
> TRUST NO-ONE, SPEND TIME WITH FAMILY
(9) Compounding is a true wonder: great things take time, incredibly good things take incredible amount of time
> TO THRIVE, YOU MUST SURVIVE
(10) Companies are made of people: yes it is tough, but you are not alone, if you are alone, you will fail
> HELP, AND ASK FOR HELP

Building companies is not a future-guessing game, but a future-making game. It is indeed the greatest game.

text: According to game theory, you must never underestimate a weaker player, especially when the game involves at least three players. A weak player can still hold strategic power, such as resources or relative influence. Whenever two strong players of equal power engage in conflict, it results in a stalemate; the “weak” player can turn into a “kingmaker”: their strategic power may be weak, but it's enough to tip the scales. Suddenly, the weak player gains exponential, previously unheard-of leverage. You might want his favors. Remember this: a player's strategic importance is determined not merely by how much power they possess, but by how much their participation changes the outcome of the game.

text:
During this red-teaming exercise, we also found a vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution in Brotli, a widely-deployed compression library included in many pieces of software such as Node.js, Bun, and Envoy.

The flaw could let an attacker run their own code on affected systems by sending or replying with malicious compressed data, without any need to create a user account. That is, an unpatched server that accepts compressed input could be taken over by a malicious client, and an unpatched client that accepts compressed input (such as “curl --compressed”) could be taken over by a malicious server.

This root cause issue was actually fixed in the Brotli source code in February, but it wasn’t known at the time that it gave rise to a security vulnerability and there was no more recent release of Brotli. Since Brotli is built into other software, any software which includes this library needs to take the update too, followed by the users of that software. We disclosed the vulnerability to Brotli and other downstream projects such as Node.js, which released or are currently releasing security updates, and Brotli cut new release versions and published a CVE.

More details on the patch and mitigations below:
https://t.co/Y1Y72aHxrW
author: banteg
quoted_text:
Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

https://t.co/EmEZsFRMcF

text:
Si vous êtes investi dans l’IA, vous voulez peut-être vous asseoir avant de lire ça

Hier a été une journée absolument horrible pour les actifs de croissance

L’IA change de phase; quelques explications :

1. Depuis le début des années 2010, le cash-flow des hyperscalers suffisait à financer le capex

Désormais, il faut emprunter pour construire et deux nouvelles à contre-courant sont tombées cette semaine :

A/ SpaceX a publié des résultats énormes et rentabilise ses datacenters en un an environ 

B/ $META, à l’inverse, doit diluer ses actionnaires pour continuer à financer son capex, ce qui montre très clairement que le cash-flow ne suffit plus.

2. Ce changement se heurte à deux forces 

A/  L’argent cesse d’être bon marché

L'argent pour le buildout c'est le nerf de la guerre, l'argent coute cher au moment précis où l’on en a besoin. Le 10 ans US est à environ 5,1 %, la Fed est en cycle de hausse et environ 70 pb de hausses supplémentaires sont pricées sur 12 mois. Quiconque a étudié l’histoire sait que construire à crédit pendant que le coût de l’emprunt monte a mené, à maintes reprises, à une période classique de fragilité

B/  Les revenus de l’IA font douter

Anthropic ajoutait environ 8 Md$ de revenus annualisés par mois au premier semestre, contre 2 à 3 Md$ en août et septembre. Beaucoup comptent sur les agents IA pour prendre le relais, mais côté grand public, Muse ne retient qu’environ 22 % de ses utilisateurs à 14 jours, contre environ 27 % il me semble pour ChatGPT

Le marché vend donc l’incertitude née du décalage entre un capex certain, financé de plus en plus cher, et une monétisation encore floue. Ce décalage devra se résorber d’une manière ou d’une autre

Je vous encourage donc à étudier 2000 de près, car les différences sont aussi instructives que les ressemblances

En 2000, on finançait à crédit une demande qui n’existait pas encore, et seulement 2 % de l'infrastructure  était « allumé ». Aujourd’hui, la capacité est vendue avant d’être construite, les capex sont backés par des contrats solides, et ce qui manque, ce sont les puces et l’électricité, PAS les clients.

L'infrastructure IA n’est pas la fibre, par contre je peux le concéder, le parallèle tient sur le point le plus important en top down, le bilan car si les revenus ne suivent pas la dette, ça casse, et c’est ce que ce bon vieux marché a testé hier

Je suis tenté d’y voir un énorme discount sur les actions liées à l’IA qui connaissent leur première vraie phase de repli, mais j’ai aussi besoin d’être rassuré par les earnings et par les midterms. $GOOGL publiera mercredi 28, le jour de la Fed, et le S-1 d’Anthropic semble déjà pricé

Plus d'update à venir

author: punk2898
quoted_text:
年入十亿的录音卡要死了，但录音的万亿机会才刚开始 🎙️

上一篇写 PLAUD 的文章爆了（全网阅读超 30,000），很多朋友来找我交流。

聊完之后，我反而越来越不看好录音卡了。

为什么？

它有一个很操蛋的悖论：越火，越没用。

没人认识的时候，你把它放桌上，大家该聊什么聊什么。

等所有人都知道这是录音卡——

好，接下来请欣赏《场面话大全》。

你花几百块，买了个让所有人闭嘴的东西。

录音卡卖得越多，认识它的人越多，能录到的真话反而越少。这生意，自带刹车。

再加上苹果已经支持原生通话录音，当初让我掏钱的理由，又少了一个。

但我说录音卡要死了，没说录音没机会。

恰恰相反，真正的大机会才刚开始。

以前录音，是怕忘了、怕扯皮、怕会后还得自己写纪要。

以后录音，是给你的个人 Agent 喂数据。

功能没变，场景变了。

你每天聊了什么、想做什么、答应了什么，你总不能每天晚上再手打两千字，汇报给 AI 吧？

谁拿下这个入口，谁就有机会做出真正懂你的 Agent。这才是我眼里万亿美金的机会。 💰

至于入口长什么样？

我押手表、手环，或者干脆就是手机。已经天天带着的东西，为什么不能顺手录？

真要赌下一代，我不会再赌一张卡。

我赌录音会越来越重要，但"录音设备"会越来越没存在感。

· Spaces, Folders, and Tab Groups are in Dia and import over with your data intact.
· Dia now surpasses Arc benchmarks in stability, speed, and security.
· The browser features you use in Arc are free in Dia, and the AI is optional.

Thank you for using Arc, for pushing us to make it better, and for building alongside us. The team that made Arc is the same team behind Dia, and some of our most ambitious work is just ahead. We'd love for you to be there with us when it lands.

text:
new blog post by me, "The Harsh Geometry of Superintelligence--  The Selfish Supermind Attractor Generally Has a Wider Basin than the BGI Attractor"

https://t.co/HnUTwymq0Q

So ... in a series of prequel posts I have described several kinds of possible AGI mind, each with its own basic drives and each tending --  as it increases its intelligence and capability, to stay roughly the kind it starts out as..

Examples are: 

* the power-seeking maximizer of Steve Omohundro’s 2008 "Basic AI Drives" paper

* the BGI minds that my colleagues and I are trying to build, ...and half a dozen others.

Knowing what kinds of superintelligent minds are attractors under intelligence/capability increase  is only part of the puzzle, though. 

The next question is: What are the shapes of the basins of these attractors?

I.e, the zillion-dollar (actually, well, money-obsoleting…) question is: Which kind of attractor will a given early-stage AGI system fall into and how hard will it be to knock out again? 

In dynamical systems terms, this depends on how wide and how deep the basin around each one is.

So this blog post analyzes these attractor basins a bit, with an aim toward milking lessons for building AGI systems and for understanding what an AGI system should do when something strange happens to it that may potentially zoink it out of its historical attractor basin. 

The disturbing yet unsurprising punchline here is: While Omohundro’s original “Basic AI Drives” paper overstated the omnipresence of the “selfish” attractor in the space of superminds … nonetheless it DOES seem that the selfish attractor has a big, wide and deep basin that makes it especially easy for AGI systems to fall into it … if they are not designed just right….

This doesn’t mean you need some sort of extremely carefully calibrated mathematical design to avoid convergence to selfishness – but it does mean that if you don’t bother to build things like compassion and goal-continuity into your AI system’s initial goal framework, you have no reason to expect your system to converge elsewhere than to a selfish Omohundro-esque attractor as it self-modifies and its intelligence and capability increase.

text:
黃仁勳：論製造沒有哪個國家比得上中國——長鑫的內存，我持開放態度

黃仁勳在柏林 GTC 的 CNBC 現場採訪裡，一口氣給了三個判斷，每一個都值得單獨拎出來說。

第一，2029 年內存過剩？瞎擔心。 最近韓國媒體在預測：內存供給大擴產，半導體超級週期可能在 2029 年結束；加上中國長鑫存儲宣布了新一代 DRAM 設計技術，內存股應聲下跌。黃仁勳的回應是：「內存的好處之一，就是你永遠可以用得更多。」HBM（高帶寬內存）還會用很多年；英偉達是第一家把手機上用的 LPDDR 低功耗內存搬進數據中心的公司，能效翻倍，他們還會大量用下去。

第二，長鑫的內存用不用？「我們持開放態度。」 被問到英偉達會不會用長鑫的產品，他沒有迴避，還補了一句：全世界的公司，供應鏈的某個環節都在和中國公司合作。

第三，對中國製造的評價，給到了頂格。 他說中國在基礎設施基礎技術上有 remarkable（了不起的）能力；「論製造，從整個國家來看，沒有哪個國家比得上中國。」他甚至點明：美國對中國的半導體出口限制，反而加速了中國的技術自立。

最後是對 AI 需求的定調：新雲廠商（neocloud）的需求「超乎想像」；現在卡住 AI 行業增速的不是沒需求，是缺週轉資金——整個行業對資本的需求遠超可得的資本，但這事最終會解決。

原文連結：https://t.co/tBJzFLrilT
原文：朝鮮日報 CHOSUNBIZ 報導（由 S1哥 編譯）
S1哥觀點

這段採訪最值得看的，是黃仁勳在「政治正確」和「生意真相」之間選了後者。內存過剩論、長鑫、中國製造——每個問題都有一個安全的答法，他一個都沒用。為什麼他敢？因為他賣的是全世界都搶的貨，話語權在賣方手裡的時候，人說話就是比較直。

但「持開放態度」這五個字，落地要過的不是技術關，是華盛頓那一關。英偉達真用上長鑫的那一天，中美芯片戰的故事就得重寫一章。你覺得這一天會來嗎？評論區見。

New on our Frontier Red Team blog: using Claude to formally verify software at large scale.

Formal verification can prove that code is free of certain bugs, but historically it has only been feasible for small codebases (or required a lot of expert time).

With AI models, however, this is beginning to change. In collaboration with @theoremlabs, we used Claude to prove security properties in over one hundred real-world open-source libraries over the span of a few weeks.

Read our research in full here: https://t.co/zUyx8CjBEk

text:

- We're open sourcing thousands of theorem statements from 437 libraries, our Linux process semantics, and ASan for static binaries. Let's turn a lot more fuzz tests into theorems, and get cracking at the proofs!
- OSS Verify: We’ll verify safety properties of critical projects for free. Please enroll!

我剪了一个我认为十分重要的访谈；是关于 $NBIS CEO Volozh的最新访谈，里面讲了目前最真实的Nebius的状况和所面临的问题，我认为对于任何NBIS的投资者都是有价值去仔细看和品的：

以下是Claude AI对视频内容的总结：

在 GTC 柏林，$NBIS CEO Arkady Volozh 说了一句我觉得投资者都低估了的话：AI 基础设施的瓶颈已经不是需求，而是钱。

"客户，也就是需求，绝对不是约束。"

但紧接着，他承认了一件 CEO 很少公开讲的事：

"从上周开始，部分资金渠道可能暂时关闭了，比如资产支持融资和债务市场。"

对一家计划每年新增至少 1GW 算力、已签约 5GW 以上电力储备的公司来说，这句话分量很重。市场大概率会盯着风险看，但是……

有几点值得想一想：

Nebius 并没有坐等融资。Volozh 说，客户预付款加上其他几种工具，足够支撑至少这 1GW 的建设。他的原话是：资本"不是问题，是一项任务"。真正要关注的是会不会稀释股东，以及预付款背后的条款。

合同结构才是利润率的关键。5 年期大单有预付款、风险低，但价格也低。Nebius 希望至少一半产能卖给短期、价格更高的客户，目前大约各占一半。再加上实时现货定价和自动化竞价，Nebius 想把算力卖得更像大宗商品市场，而不是批发租赁。

下一个瓶颈可能是芯片，不是客户。Volozh 点名了内存和台积电的产能分配，认为 2027 年需要警惕。如果供给持续紧张，谁手里有产能，谁就有定价权。

需求一波接一波。先是聊天机器人，然后是高级搜索，现在是消费级 AI Agent。他说有客户连续数月每月翻倍，一年增长 10 倍以上。按 Nebius 在节目里的说法，推理已经占到全部算力的约三分之二。

节目里主持人还转述了 Jensen 的一个观点：Blackwell 的使用寿命可能长达 8 年。如果成立，市场对 GPU 云折旧太快的担忧可能被高估了。

当然，执行风险依然存在。新产能从 Q1 起步，下半年才集中上线，所以季度数字在建设见效之前可能不太好看。

但整个行业现在同时受制于资本、芯片和电力。能在这种环境下持续融资、持续上线产能的公司，才是最终掌握定价权的那一方。

text:
AI demand is a barbell, with the labs on one end and enterprise cost-cutting on the other. Amazon CEO Andy Jassy says the biggest market sits in the middle, and inference is still "an order of magnitude too expensive" to reach it.

"On one end of the barbell are the AI labs who are consuming gobs and gobs of compute, unlike anything I've seen. And then a few runaway apps, ChatGPT, Claude Code, things like that."

"On the other end of the barbell are enterprises who are largely using AI for cost avoidance and productivity, so automating customer service or fraud or business process automation."

"In the middle of the barbell are the current production workloads of enterprises, many of which are using AWS and using inference today, but I would say the overwhelming majority of which still aren't in any pervasive way."

"And that I think is gonna be the largest absolute segment of AI usage."

"The cost of inference has come down quite a bit in the last few years, but it's still an order of magnitude too expensive, in my opinion, for it to be used as pervasively as possible."

"If you're asking enterprises to rewrite their applications that use CPU today with AI accelerators... the amount of incremental benefit they have to get is a much higher bar to want to rewrite those apps. But if you can take the cost of inference down, that bar is much lower, and all applications are gonna be better and smarter and more capable."

@ajassy

传统金融巨头开始联手阻击股票代币化了。

Wells Fargo、Intuit 等 22 家公司反对 OKX 上线其股票的代币化交易。

这场争议的核心，不只是股票能不能上链，而是谁有权决定股票如何被交易。

传统券商依赖交易牌照、清算体系和中介服务赚钱。股票一旦被代币化，交易可能走向 7×24 小时、全球化和链上结算，原有的市场边界就会被打破。

当然，代币化股票涉及股东权利、监管合规和底层资产托管，不能简单等同于普通加密代币。

但有一点值得注意：当越来越多金融资产开始上链，传统金融机构真正需要面对的，不是要不要拥抱区块链，而是未来的交易入口还掌握在谁手里。

text:
Stacks 上的借贷协议 Arkadiko，10 月 22 日（UTC）被治理打穿了。

1. 官方口径：一份恶意合约过了治理，被用来抽走金库里大部分抵押，自家稳定币 USDA 脱锚；
2. 初步估损：官方约 200 万枚 stSTX、约 1.65 枚 sBTC；链上梳理写到约 206.5 万 stSTX／1.65 sBTC；
3. 投票内容：Proposal #12，赞成约 457 万 DIKO、反对 0——基本是单钱包投满；购票成本大约五万美元量级（Bitquery）；
4. 权限：过会后对方能提走金库抵押，还能任意铸 USDA（链上分析：另铸约 15 亿枚，当晚大部分被烧毁——这是铸币量，不是美元损失）；
5. 事后：恶意合约已禁用，治理／赎回／清算暂停；DEX 和其他 STX 金库仍可用。资产是否追回，官方尚未确认。

严格来说，这算“一次黑客”，而是一个“治理漏洞”。

很多DAO组织都会将自己托管给治理协议，依赖治理投票来做决策。
但是对诚实投票者来说，盯提案、读合约，收益太低；
虽然损失很大，但是都会侥幸的认为，我不管有人管。

结果一些老协议长期处在事实上的无人关注状态——坏人只要凑够通过门槛，就能把治理当成提款机。

最近1年你是否看到过类似这样的新闻？一些原本加密挖矿的矿企纷纷转投AI，干起了提供算力的生意。

矿企转型确实是个趋势，但也容易给人一种错觉：

好像这些大矿工一走，比特币网络就塌了没人挖了。

但数据表明，你不挖，有的是人挖，而且挖得还挺猛。

来自 look into bitcoin 的数据显示，比特币7日平均算力已重新回到约 1 ZH/s（即1000 EH/s），是自2026年3月3日以来的最高水平。

另外，可以看到橙色线的算力线甚至在这几年都在持续大幅上升，最近一轮波动后再次走高，整体挖矿趋势远强于早期。

同时，挖矿难度在10月16日上调了约5.92%，预计下次还会再涨，两轮累计可能接近11.4%。

部分上市公司矿工因为AI 转型，实际算力下降约23%，AI相关收入季度增长明显，但 BTC 网络总算力反而从7月低点大幅反弹（约45%）。

很多人以为大型矿工退出会让剩余矿工更好过，但难度还在上升。

剩余矿工的利润压力没有明显缓解，说明新进入或扩产的矿工在积极竞争，反而越来越卷了。

往好的方面想，大家还是在争相开采剩余不多的 BTC，并维护着网络赚取区块的手续费。

即使价格有波动，矿工仍愿意部署更多算力。

在 AI 攻破密码学这个变量之前，比特币网络仍展现了足够强大的韧性和开放程度。

quoted_text:
I get more messages about this podcast every week than anything else I do.

We all want to look and sound smart in the investment committee or all hands meeting.

This is the only show in tech you have to listen to every week.

No egos, no politics, just tech.

AGENDA:

- Venture is Broken: Trillion or Bust
- Coreweave Sell-Off Creates Panic
- Town at $1B, Anduril at $90B: Are Revenue Multiples Out of Control?
- General Atlantic Eyes IPO
- Modal Raises $750M at $15.75B

My notes with @jasonlk and @rodriscoll

1. Why Fundraising Is Back to Being a Numbers Game

Founders with top-decile numbers now have to meet 100 VCs, as in the old days. It will not be Benchmark, Index, Andreessen or Bessemer, but other growth investors will take the bet at a reasonable but still elevated valuation because it is the best deal they have seen that quarter.

2. Why the Big Funds Have to Have Billion-Dollar Positions to Make It Worthwhile?

A $5B plus fund needs $BN positions in everything. Without 51% ownership, which most founders will not accept, a $2B Listen Labs is not good enough, while 1% of Anthropic could still get there even with dilution.

Love to hear your thoughts on this @venkyganesan @DavidGeorge83

3. Why Are CoreWeave and Oracle B-Tier and What Does That Mean for Their Price Volatility?

With massive debt loads, CoreWeave and Oracle should be hypersensitive to any bump at Anthropic or OpenAI. CoreWeave exists because NVIDIA needs it for now, and Oracle rents out excess capacity because it cannot sell enough enterprise software.

4. Why the Best Markets for App Layer Companies Compete Directly With the Models

The fastest-growing AI apps, such as code generation, code review and legal, sit closest to the foundation models. That brings a moment of terror every six months, but it is also why companies like CodeRabbit are growing faster than ever.

Love to hear your thoughts on this @spdholakia @mmurph

5. Why Code Review Is the Single Most Important Category in Software

AI-generated code is pretty good but never production-ready, and reviewing it takes an order of magnitude more time than building it. Getting code into production matters more than generating it, so the best code review teams would be worth 10 bets.
Love to hear your thoughts on this @reidRMC @evrishria @Joshuabrowder

6. How Big Is the Market for Inference Truly?

The key inference providers add up to roughly $5B to $6B in run-rate revenue, under 5% of OpenAI and Anthropic combined. If tokens are roughly the same, Replit would rather pay Modal a 30% gross margin than give Claude Code 70%.

How do you analyse the TAM for inference today? What do people not see that they should see? @sarahcat21 @bernhardsson

7. Why Bending Spoons Is a Berkshire Hathaway of Software

Bending Spoons buys software to hold, the way Warren Buffett wanted to hold See's Candy forever. It made Vimeo and Evernote work with price increases, and with Miro and Airtable the quality of its assets is improving.

Love to hear your thoughts on this as an analogy @ncsh

Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

text:
If you put a VPS on Tailscale, fix these two things immediately:

Disable key expiry (Machines → ··· → Disable Key Expiry). Otherwise, you risk losing access after 180 days.

Lock down your ACLs. Tag the VPS tag:server and only allow inbound connections from your own devices. Don't allow the server to initiate connections to your other machines.

By default, Tailscale allows everything to talk to everything, and device keys expire.

A compromised VPS shouldn't give an attacker access to your entire tailnet.
author: madhavjha
quoted_text:
Maybe important to repost this now that everyone is getting hacked

If you have a VPS, I recommend you to get if off the public internet and into a Tailscale network and Cloudflare Tunnel ASAP

It doesn't matter you have SSH key login, this is about exploits and vulnerabilities AI is finding

There's 2 ways into a VPS:
- via your site/app (like the PHP exploit of this week with a file upload hack)
- via your server (like hacking into SSH or some open port)

The site/app side you put on a Cloudflare Tunnel and then with the default Free Plan it has WAF security enabled by default and they jump on new security exploits fast, it means that the only way to reach your website is via the Cloudflare Tunnel, your server does not respond to port 80 or 443 anymore

The server side you put on a Tailscale network which is like your own private network that nobody can access but your own devices (like your laptop, your phone and your VPS) kinda like a VPN

Then you switch off ANY regular access to your VPS on the firewall, in my case I use Hetzner and you create a new firewall then empty it and that blocks everything (test it)

How do Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel get in then? They don't. They go outbound. They make a tunnel to outside which sends and receives

Now you've reduced your attack vector to Tailscale and your Cloudflare Tunnel, much safer, not perfect btw, but nothing is

The entire internet will be rearchitected around intent vs attention, starting with commerce + trading.

Today our entire industry was built around understanding users online e.g. tracking users, figuring out what influenced an ad, creating ads, pushing ads, content related to ads, and measuring what led to a purchase.

All of this could eventually collapse into who owns the user’s intent.

Every intent can lead your agent to speak to other agents representing shopping sites, research sites, review sites, and more. Every research task, purchase, and connection between agents could have a cost, and if the end result turns out to be a purchase, it’s very likely that all of the agents involved in fulfilling that intent could capture some sort of fee 

You can argue the same thing will happen with trading.

Instead of shopping agents talking to merchants, it’ll be trading agents talking to other agents representing brokerages, exchanges, and liquidity providers.

Some agents will handle research, strategy, or execution, and each could get paid for the value they provide.

It’s very likely all of this will require new infrastructure around payments, identity, trust, and settlement between agents.

But imo the bigger shift here is that the internet is moving away from monetizing attention to monetizing intent, and the death of the attention economy + ads

quoted_text:
Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

text:
Tom Lee thinks we are getting a lot closer to the bottom of this tech selloff than people realize.

His argument is that investors have become extremely pessimistic about AI, semiconductors, memory stocks, and technology in general. In fact, betting against tech has become such a popular trade that he believes we could be approaching the final stages of this correction. What's interesting is that the underlying fundamentals haven't deteriorated nearly as much as stock prices suggest. AI demand is still strong, companies are continuing to spend billions building infrastructure, and earnings are holding up. The bigger concern right now is how all of this expansion gets financed, especially with interest rates remaining elevated.

@fundstrat also points out that Treasury yields have started coming down and the Federal Reserve could become more supportive. Both would help companies that need significant amounts of capital to fund their growth. Another important point is that his technical analyst, Mark Newton, believes many technology stocks have already fallen toward major support levels. These are price levels where buyers have historically stepped in, although that doesn't guarantee they will hold.

Essentially, Lee believes we have a situation where sentiment has become extremely negative while the long term growth story remains intact. He compares this to a compressed spring, where stocks could rebound sharply once the selling pressure starts to ease. I tend to agree with his overall argument. That doesn't mean we can't go lower but I think investors are starting to price in a much worse outcome than what the fundamentals are currently telling us.
author: fundstrat
quoted_text:
This selloff is a lot closer to the bottom than we think.

According to Jefferies, over the past 10 trading days, its clients have been net sellers of more than $1B worth of technology stocks on 7 separate days. This chart tracks the buying and selling activity of Jefferies’ clients over a rolling 20 day period. When the purple line is above zero, investors are buying more than they’re selling. When it’s below zero, they’re selling more than they’re buying. Right now, that number has collapsed to approximately negative $11B, making this one of the most extreme periods of technology selling we’ve seen in the past two years.

For comparison, even during the major selloffs earlier in 2025 and 2026, the selling pressure wasn’t consistently this severe. And remember, this is just one investment bank’s trading activity. This also helps explain why companies across semiconductors, memory, power, and AI infrastructure have been getting absolutely crushed despite reporting strong earnings and continued demand. A lot of this selling isn’t necessarily happening because the fundamentals have changed. Large institutions are reducing exposure, managing risk and raising cash. When everyone starts selling at the same time, even the best companies get dragged down.

Now, does this mean the bottom is definitely here? Of course not. Nobody knows that but historically, when selling becomes this extreme, it can be a sign that we’re getting closer to exhaustion. Eventually, the forced selling slows down, buyers return, and stocks can recover. My personal view is that we’re likely getting much closer to a bottom, I’m not changing my long term outlook on AI because hedge funds and institutions are aggressively selling technology stocks. The demand for compute, memory, power, and AI infrastructure hasn’t suddenly disappeared. I’m investing with years in mind, not weeks.

> Am I being a schizo to think that this could be a Chinese government ploy
Yes. Meds, now.
But there does exist a cynical read of DeepSeek's moves. Because V4.1 line is very strong, cheap and has zero strings attached, they destroy the case for hosting anything like K3 ($3/$15) by Western partners, so starve their domestic rivals of revenue. Moreover DeepInfer is useless for anything not shaped just like V4.1 (so, it'll be DeepSeek's models and finetunes). They also make compute ownership more valuable by having created mutual knowledge about its profitability even at "shockingly low" prices. Frontier labs and hyperscalers already understood how valuable compute is, so they can't go harder on securing allocation, but neoclouds will now ask premium.
Flash, in effect, requires a full NVL72 GB200 rack to hit these margins. V4.1 Pro and Ultra (hypothetical for now) will make the issue even more pronounced. When you need a whole cluster to run an 8T DeepSeek model efficiently, *but* it prints you like $40/GPU/hour, this removes a lot of colocated GPUs from easy access. And DeepSeek had little hope to tap into this pool, so they lose nothing, gain mindshare and keep building their new power base around Ascend, which will also become increasingly Whale-shaped due to co-design. In the end, DeepSeek will have defined the entire upstream and downstream AI ecosystem in China, harvesting a tiny slice of the profit in the process.

The resolution for this Trueo market is going to get interesting.

In August 2025, Indian CEX @CoinDCX had its hot wallets compromised to the tune of $44M. 

Earlier this week, reports surfaced that they lost another $16M.

At first, the exchange claimed they were unaffected and that Arkham had mislabelled the previously exploited address as active, but they’ve since switched their stance.

The founders are deflecting the truth big time, so the picture remains hazy. 

But what we do know, what’s publicly verifiable, is that a private key which was compromised last year had $16M transferred to it on Oct/21st, either by users or by the CEX itself and subsequently siphoned off.

So why might this matter be contentious for our prediction market? 

It comes down to whether newly lost funds from a previous PK compromise constitutes a new “hack” under the rules of the market.

I’m not going to comment personally, but I can see some legitimacy to both sides of the argument.

text:
The a16z name change isn’t a surprise. It’s an honest read of where crypto venture already is and where it needs to go.

Look at the market today:

$3T industry with BTC being 2/3 of that
$300B in stablecoins
$40B in RWAs
2-3 L1s worth over $100B
10-20 investable tokens in the 5B-20B range

That market can’t produce outcomes big enough for a fund the size of a16z. It hasn’t for years.

Crypto venture quietly became frontier venture over the last 1-2 years. If anything, I’m surprised it took this long.

Today, 90% of conversations in crypto venture aren’t about building a better product for existing crypto users. That market isn’t big enough. Nobody wants to fund another prop AMM, another structured products protocol, or another onchain options order book.

The real question now: how does this industry grow 10-100x ?

The answer is always the same. Crypto has to meet and power other frontier markets. Prediction markets. AI. Fintech. Agentic payments. Crypto-enabled AI networks.

This is a natural evolution, and I think this new fund will be FAR more beneficial to crypto’s growth than the old model.

The marginal value of a16z funding the next perps protocol is zero. The intersections are where the bigger markets and bigger companies get built, and they’re the best people to do it. This will open up a lot of opportunities for "crypto"

🎩The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen. 

This is not a club you join — it is a standard you hold. 

For years, this mark has stood for one simple idea: that a man can be strong and principled at the same time. That wealth without character is just noise. Five pillars hold the whole thing up, and one code runs through all of them: how a gentleman acts, how he invests, how he moves through crypto, the stoic mind, and emotional mastery. This is the manifesto.

1️⃣Pillar one: the gentleman's code. He keeps his word, because his word is his bond — if he says it, it's done. He speaks last and means it, because he listened first. He stays composed when others lose their heads; pressure doesn't change him, it reveals him. Respect is given freely, never demanded — to the waiter and the chairman alike. And he protects those who cannot protect themselves.

2️⃣Pillar two: investing. A gentleman does not chase; he positions. Time in the market beats timing the market, and patience is the only edge that never decays. He never risks what he cannot afford to lose. He diversifies, so no single bet defines him. He stays calm when others panic, buying when there is blood in the streets. And he lets compounding do the heavy lifting.

3️⃣Pillar three: crypto. Not your keys, not your coins — a gentleman holds his own. Bitcoin is the anchor; everything else is venture, sized accordingly. He studies the chart but masters his emotions first, because fear and greed have liquidated more men than any bear market. He takes profits on the way up, never apologizing for it. Thesis over hype, always.

4️⃣Pillar four: the stoic mind. Control what you can — your effort, your response, your standards — and release the rest without resentment. The obstacle is the way: every setback is raw material. Memento mori: remember you will die, so waste no day. Amor fati: love your fate — don't just accept what happens, want it, then use it.

5️⃣Pillar five: emotional intelligence. Name the emotion before it names you. Pause before you react — a gentleman responds, he never erupts, because the man who controls his temper controls the room. Listen to understand, not to reply. And wherever he walks in, he lifts the room, leaving people better than he found them. That is influence no money can buy.

Five pillars. One standard. The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen — not a following, a brotherhood of standards. Act like a gentleman. Think like a strategist. Hold the line.

最好的渠道，没有之一，安全、稳定、收益持续

a. Bitway 的官网存款，APY每个月调整，最新的APY是 8%U本位 + 4% Token奖励（实际发放只多不少），最大的优势是每个月1号会开定期赎回，可以不用等7天，如果有其他资金安排可以动态调整

d. Huma，USDC池，8%左右APY，赎回最长7天但实测大多数时候是在2天以内，唯一缺点是 TGE 时间有点

这几个性质比较类似，我存的优先级是a＞b＞c=d，资金不放在一个篮子里避免一锅端

e. USDD（ETH），APY已经几个月稳定在7%了，最大优势是灵活存取，

f. R25，高收益，风险相对也高一点，活动存的能到20%左右，但现在已经关门了

a. Binance 的U理财，限额8000U，8%APY，还有10天

b. BG/Gate/MEXC/Bybit经常有10%-20%的活动，但是APY经常砍，所以现在我不咋存，懒得折腾

d. BIT 固收，前5000U可以15%，持续1个月，其他时段经常有7%-10%

e. 其他野鸡所推沟里

说实话不是绝大多数都不太敢存，为数不多参与的是：

a. USD1 相关，经常搞活动，有官方背书+APY足够高的情况下我会短期存一些

a. Kraken：虽然交易所很抽象，SPCX耍猴，后面两次股票打新一赚一赔，Squid开盘3x，综合下来还是非常不错的。建议每个月做几笔交易，再开个几美元的会员，中签率会高很多，纯白号比较难中

e. Futarddotio：MetaDAO的无许可版本，有点拉，几十万美金FDV开盘都能破发，得看看质地选，不如主站

text:
一年学费最高 7.5 万美元，每天只上两小时课，号称能让孩子的学习效率翻倍。美国最火的 AI 学校 Alpha School，最近被《纽约时报》扒了一遍成绩单，结果有点尴尬。

Alpha School 这两年一直被当作 AI 颠覆教育的样板。传统教师被替换成负责激励和辅导的 Guide，孩子每天花两小时通过 AI 驱动的学习软件完成数学、阅读等课程，剩下的时间培养创业、演讲等技能。

学校此前宣称，学生的学习进步速度可以达到普通学校的两倍。

但《纽约时报》拿到的 2025 年秋季至 2026 年初测试数据发现，虽然约 75% 的学生成绩达到或超过全国平均水平，真正能在数学和阅读两门学科同时实现两倍进步的，只有 42%。

更值得注意的是那些基础较差的学生。在此前数学成绩处于全国中位数或以下的孩子中，只有 37% 达到了两倍进步的目标。

我觉得这件事很有意思。

首先，Alpha 的学生成绩确实不差，但一所每年收取 4 万到 7.5 万美元学费、能够筛选生源的私立学校，本来就应该交出不错的成绩单。

其次，AI 教育最有价值的地方，应该是让那些在传统课堂上跟不上的孩子获得更好的个性化辅导。结果 Alpha 恰恰在这群学生身上遇到了更大的困难。

当然，42% 的学生实现两倍进步，依然是一个值得研究的结果。只是当你把「学习效率翻倍」当作卖点，家长自然会以更高的标准来衡量。

教育行业的麻烦就在这里。AI 产品可以每隔几个月迭代一次，但一个孩子的成长没有那么多试错机会。

I am a technology optimist. I believe:

1. decentralization and censorship-resistance (real versions of these properties, not larps) matter to human freedom in the coming age of AI

2. self-sovereign money, implemented by code and maintained through decentralized consensus, is the final form of money. But it needs to be truly decentralized -- cut out every possible weakness, trust assumption, keeper, etc. Of course there will be connectors to the real world - harden those maximally

3. AI will write most smart contract code. Spec-driven development with Formal Verification will be how new contracts are written rigorously. FV will also be crucial to securing all the infra including the blockchain itself

4. AI will harden our surfaces, with some unfortunate hacks in the process, but ultimately the crypto and financial industries will come out stronger

5. properly-constructed and properly-indexed data lakes will enable agents to build software far more productively

6. governments will move to restrict AI usage in the future, causing true decentralization and CR to matter in dramatic fashion

7. quantum security will be a must for any ledger where people trust their assets. And specifically, blockchains will need to deliver quantum-resistance while retaining programmability and performance. Again, no larping

8. ZK will be an important part of the puzzle too, as it'll be increasingly important to prove off-chain computation and utilize the result on chain. But again, performance and effortlessness for users will be the differentiator

9. pragmatic and composable privacy will be the missing piece for real adoption. People will use apps that stack together stablecoins, DeFi, blockchain settlement, passkey or MPC authentication, and friction-free onramps, but the part that gets fintechs over the line is knowing that user balances will remain private while still being able to tap into shared liquidity

10. blockchain will serve as the global, universal marketplace, for anyone anywhere to get the best opportunities. For that we will need guarantees of fair execution, protection from frontrunning, and a convergence of all of the best assets

At @category_xyz and the @monad Foundation, we are assembling all of these missing pieces in parallel with extreme urgency, and I hope this is clear from our actions. See you in the future

Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

TikTok 美国业务刚刚完成拆分，现在就准备按 OpenAI 的规格抢电了。

据 CNBC 报道，TikTok USDS 正在美国寻找大规模数据中心资源，希望到 2030 年代初获得 4GW（4000MW）的计算基础设施电力容量。

去年 OpenAI 和 Oracle 为 Stargate 项目签下的新增数据中心容量协议，也不过 4.5GW。

更有意思的是，这家今年才完成重组的 TikTok 美国公司，股东包括 Oracle、银湖资本和阿布扎比 MGX，三家各持股 15%，字节跳动保留 19.9%。Oracle 同时还是它的主要云服务商。

如此庞大的算力需求，显然值得关注。

今年 1 月，TikTok 美国公司宣布，将使用美国用户数据重新训练、测试和更新推荐算法，相关系统运行在 Oracle 的美国云环境中。

但事情可能还不止于推荐算法。

CNBC 发现，TikTok 美国公司正在招聘大量机器学习人才，其中一份招聘启事明确提到，公司正在推出一款面向企业的旗舰 AI 产品，涉及大模型推理和创意自动化。

换句话说，TikTok 美国业务可能正在尝试从一家短视频平台，向提供 AI 服务的公司扩张。

我觉得最值得关注的其实是 Oracle。

它既是 TikTok 美国公司的股东，又是其主要云服务商，还是 OpenAI Stargate 的核心基础设施合作伙伴。AI 时代最昂贵的资源之一是电力，而 Oracle 已经同时站在几个超级买家的供应链上。

当然，目前 4GW 还只是知情人士透露的目标，具体合同、选址和投资规模都没有敲定。

但至少能看到一个趋势，今天在美国争夺 GW 级数据中心容量的，已经远远不止那些训练基础模型的公司了。

text:
OpenAI 曾经用来分析 ChatGPT 增长数据的工具，现在被 Meta 买走了。

据 Axios 独家报道，Meta 收购了 AI 数据分析公司 Sundial，交易金额尚未披露。

这家公司还挺有意思。两位创始人都是 Meta 老员工，Julie Zhuo 曾任 Meta 产品设计副总裁，Chandra Narayanan 则在 Instagram 和红杉资本负责过数据分析。两个人离职创业，累计融资 2300 万美元，如今又带着团队和技术回到了老东家。

Sundial 做的是 AI 数据分析 Agent。比如你想知道为什么用户留存率突然下降、哪个地区的转化率出了问题，直接用自然语言提问，Agent 就能自动分析数据、排查原因。

OpenAI 也是它的客户。2023 年 ChatGPT 用户量暴涨时，OpenAI 的数据团队忙不过来，就引入了 Sundial。按照 Sundial 公布的案例，原本需要几个月的数据工程工作被大幅压缩。

最有意思的是，Meta 收购后准备停止 Sundial 的对外服务，将整个团队并入今年 7 月成立的 DATA 部门，专门负责内部数据分析、实验和 AI Agent。

我觉得这笔收购挺能说明问题的。

过去企业做数据分析，往往需要一整套 BI 系统和专业分析师。现在 AI Agent 已经可以接手其中相当一部分工作，甚至主动发现业务异常。

而 Meta 的选择更值得琢磨，一家已经服务 OpenAI 等客户的 AI 公司，最终被买回去做内部基础设施。

当 AI 开始深入企业的真实业务流程，数据分析可能是最先被彻底改造的岗位之一。Meta 显然已经不满足于让员工用 AI 写代码、写文案了，它还想让 AI 参与公司的日常经营决策。

text:
一个在日本众议院只占不到 1% 席位的政党，居然成了 AI 向左翼选民推荐的热门选项。原因有点荒诞，因为它的网站对 AI 爬虫完全开放。

斯坦福大学的 Andrew Hall 和宫崎翔今年 3 月发表了一篇研究。他们在日本众议院选举期间，创建了 36,300 份虚拟选民画像，让 OpenAI、Google、xAI 旗下的五组模型推荐投票对象。

结果发现，只要选民表达左倾政策立场，五组模型都会明显倾向于推荐日本共产党。即便日本还有好几个政策立场相近的政党。

研究者进一步追查发现，日本共产党旗下的《赤旗》报有个特殊优势，网站内容免费公开，允许 AI 爬虫抓取。

与此同时，《朝日新闻》《日本经济新闻》等日本主流媒体出于版权保护，纷纷限制 AI 抓取。

更离谱的是，部分模型甚至无法正确识别《赤旗》的党报身份，把它当成了独立新闻媒体。

于是，一个政党的政治宣传材料，被 AI 当成新闻报道反复引用，最终影响了它给选民的建议。

研究还发现，不提供政策倾向时，这些模型并没有一致的左翼偏好。这进一步说明，问题很可能出在 AI 能接触到的信息源上。

过去新闻机构花了几十年建立公信力，现在为了保护版权把 AI 爬虫挡在门外，却可能把新一代信息入口的影响力拱手让给那些愿意免费开放内容的政治组织。

而且这件事还有一个更深远的影响，未来政治宣传的对象可能直接变成 AI。

当越来越多人习惯问 ChatGPT 应该相信谁、支持谁、如何理解一件事，谁能持续出现在 AI 的检索结果里，谁就可能影响它给出的答案。

text:
Anthropic 上周公布了一项内部调查，1334 名受访员工中，91% 相信 AI 到 2030 年就能实现诺奖级别的科学突破，而在一万多名受访美国成年人中，这个比例只有 39%。

更夸张的是，超过一半的 Anthropic 员工认为，到 2030 年 AI 就能完成自己目前至少 80% 的工作。

他们这么相信也有原因。在 Anthropic 内部，AI Agent 的工作时长已经达到人类员工的 6 倍。每天亲眼看着模型进步，这群人对 AI 的未来有着远超外界的信心。

但华尔街显然没那么容易被说服。

据 The Information 报道，Anthropic 预计下个月上市，投行私下讨论过接近 2 万亿美元的估值。上周参加投资者会议的部分机构已经开始质疑，即使 Anthropic 的收入增长再惊人，是否足以支撑如此高昂的价格。

更麻烦的是，开源模型正以更低的价格追赶 Claude 的能力。AI 越来越强，和 Anthropic 能不能一直赚到钱，这是两笔账。

我觉得这件事最有意思的地方在于，Dario Amodei 和他的员工可能真心相信，他们正在参与一场足以改变人类文明的技术革命。

但华尔街买的是股票，投资人最终要的是回报。

即使 AI 真能在 2030 年做出诺贝尔奖级别的发现，也没有人能保证，创造这些价值的公司就一定是 Anthropic，更没有人能保证，这些价值最后能以利润的形式留在 Anthropic。

下个月的 IPO，Dario 要说服华尔街相信的，恐怕远不止 AI 的未来。
